member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedBufferInvalidLength(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: GS0408: a fixed-size buffer field declared a non-positive length (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035).
member.param: The text location of the field name.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedBufferInvalidShape(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0407: a fixed-size buffer field's type was not a fixed-length array [N]T (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035).
member.param: The text location of the field name.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedBufferRequiresUnsafeContext(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: GS0406: a fixed-size buffer field fixed name [N]T (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035) appears outside an unsafe context.
member.param: The text location of the fixed keyword.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedPointerCannotEscape(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS9008: issue #2330 — an unmanaged pointer (*T) bound by a fixed statement (ADR-0125 / issue #1026) is only valid for the lifetime of the pin: the pinned handle is released when the enclosing fixed block exits. A nested closure may run after that point (or, for local functions, be invoked repeatedly across further pins), so capturing the pointer would let it escape its declaring scope's lifetime — the same "escape" concern as the existing by-ref-like (ref struct) and managed-pointer (ref T) capture rejections, but for an unmanaged pointer instead. Rejected here, at capture analysis, rather than left to reach CaptureBoxingRewriter/emission, which previously crashed with GS9998 ("has no local slot") because the pointer variable is declaration-less (bound directly by BoundFixedStatement, not a BoundVariableDeclaration) and was never boxed.
member.param: The text location of the capturing closure.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedRequiresUnsafeContext(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: GS0400: a fixed (pinning) statement (ADR-0125 / issue #1026) appears outside an unsafe context. A fixed statement binds a raw unmanaged pointer *T into the pinned buffer, which is only legal inside an unsafe context (consistent with ADR-0122).
member.param: The text location of the fixed keyword.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedSourceNotPinnable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0401: the source of a fixed (pinning) statement (ADR-0125 / issues #1026, #1043) is not a pinnable managed buffer. A managed array ([]T), a string, a span-like type exposing a public instance ref T GetPinnableReference() (e.g. System.Span[T] / System.ReadOnlySpan[T]), or a fixed-size buffer field of a variable (issue #4378) can be pinned; the pointer's element type must also match the buffer's.
member.param: The text location of the pinned source expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFixedStatementCannotSuspend(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0506: an await or yield suspension point appears in a fixed body. A pinned local cannot survive state-machine suspension, so the suspension must move outside the fixed statement.
member.param: The location of the await or yield keyword.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFloatingDocumentationComment(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: ADR-0057 §P4: reports a documentation comment block that does not precede any documentable declaration (a "floating" doc comment).
member.param: The text location of the floating documentation comment.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFunctionPointerAddressOfMismatch(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0405: &Method (ADR-0122 §9 / issue #1035) produced a function pointer whose signature does not match the target function-pointer type, or the address-of operand was not a single static method group.
member.param: The text location of the address-of expression.
A short description of the mismatch.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFunctionPointerUnknownCallingConvention(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0095 / issue #761: GS0354 — the calling convention named in a raw function-pointer type clause (unmanaged[CC] (...) -> R) is not one of the supported values. The recognised conventions are Cdecl, Stdcall, Thiscall, Fastcall.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportFunctionTypeClauseFuncKeywordDeprecated(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: ADR-0075 / issue #715: GS0303 (warning) — a type-clause slot used the legacy func(T1, T2, ...) R spelling. The canonical form is the arrow function type (T1, T2, ...) -> R (Kotlin/Swift style). Both forms are accepted for one release; the legacy form is removed in a later release.
member.param: The source location of the offending func keyword.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGenericLocalFunctionCannotCapture(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports that a generic local function (issue #1886) captures one or more outer variables. Generic local functions are emitted as genuine (non-delegate) generic methods, not closures; supporting captures would require a generic closure display-class with its own reified type parameters, which is out of scope for this feature.
member.param: The text location of the declaration's identifier.
The name of the declared local function.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGenericLocalFunctionMustBeLetBoundLiteral(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports that a generic local-function declaration (let Name[T, ...] = func (...) ... { ... }, issue #1886) is not a let-bound function-literal initializer. A generic function value cannot be represented as a delegate stored in a variable (a CLR delegate cannot close over an unbound generic method), so this form only makes sense as a direct let binding of a function literal.
member.param: The text location of the declaration's identifier.
The name of the declared local function.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGenericLocalFunctionUnsupportedOwner(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Reports a direct generic local whose required lexical host cannot be emitted.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGenericOperatorNotSupported(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports GS0537 when an operator declares method type parameters.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGoOperandIsNotACall(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: Reports that the operand of a go statement is not a call expression (Phase 5.3 / ADR-0022).
member.param: The text location of the operand.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGotoIntoExceptionHandler(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports a function-wide goto that enters a catch or finally handler.
member.param: The source location of the goto label identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportGuardLetElseMustExit(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: ADR-0071 / issue #708: GS0297 — the else block of a guard let statement must unconditionally exit the enclosing scope. Accepted terminators are return, throw, break, continue, and any block whose last statement does so. An if/else qualifies only when both arms exit.
member.param: The source location of the offending else clause.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportIfExpressionMissingElse(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: GS0276: An if-expression used in value position has no else branch. Without an else, the expression cannot produce a value for all code paths.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportIfLetGuardSplitsInitializer(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #4961 / ADR-0201: GS0624 — an if let has a guard and its final binding's initializer, which ends at the guard's &&, is a non-nullable bool. This is the shape let v = a && b ? x : y takes under the shared initializer rule, so the diagnostic replaces GS0296 there and tells the user to parenthesize.
member.param: The source location of the final initializer.
The name introduced by the final binding.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportIfLetInitializerMustBeNullable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: ADR-0071 / ADR-0163: GS0296 — the right-hand side of an if let, guard let, or while let binding is not of nullable type. The binding form is intended to strip a single layer of nullability; applying it to a non-nullable value would do nothing useful and is almost certainly a programmer error.
member.param: The source location of the offending initializer.
The name introduced by the binding.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportImplementerOverridesPrivateInterfaceMember(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0090 / issue #756: GS0336 — an implementing class or struct declared a method whose name + signature matches a private helper on one of its implemented interfaces. Private helpers are invisible to implementers; declaring a same-name method is almost always an unintentional clash.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportIncompatibleDataPrintMembers(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0199: reports a data class/struct PrintMembers(StringBuilder) whose shape cannot replace the synthesized print-members slot. Compiler-internal on purpose: it adds nothing to the public API snapshot (#4654).

true when the type is a data class; otherwise a data struct.
The accessibility the slot must have (private or protected).

member.summary: Issue #2361 / ADR-0029 follow-up: reports that a data class/struct's hand-written ToString declaration is incompatible with the slot it would need to suppress/replace (public string ToString() — zero parameters, non-static, non-generic, non-async, returning string). Unlike the other five synthesized names (which are always rejected via ), a ToString declaration gets this more specific diagnostic so the message can describe the exact shape it must match.
member.param: The text location of the member name.
true when the type is a data class; otherwise a data struct.

member.summary: ADR-0146 / issue #2243: GS0486 — a field member of a "rich" anonymous object (one with a base/interface clause, method, or event) omitted its type annotation. Rich anonymous objects materialize fields as ordinary class fields, which require an explicit type; type inference from the initializer is only available on the field-only object { ... } / data object { ... } forms.

member.param: The source location of the offending init/deinit keyword.
The rejected member keyword spelling (init or deinit).

member.summary: ADR-0065 §5: GS0284 — a user-declared init(...) overload has the same signature as the constructor synthesized from the type's primary constructor parameter list.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInlineCannotBeCombinedWithData(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: Reports that the inline modifier was combined with data or record.

member.summary: Reports that a synthesized inline-struct member was hand-written.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceAbstractMethodHasNoDefault(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol,System.String,System.String)

This is the "no default, no impl" anchor that complements the general GS0187 channel; it fires when DIM is *available* but not used to bridge the gap, so users see immediately that the interface intentionally requires an implementation.

The interface declaring the abstract method.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceCannotHaveClassBase(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #1006: GS0391 — an interface named a class or struct in its base-interface clause (e.g. interface B : SomeClass). An interface may only extend other interfaces.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceDefaultRemoved(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0085 / issue #726: GS0319 — a call site (or override) references an interface method that has been turned back into an abstract slot (its default body was removed in a later library version), and the implementer was relying on the inherited default. The binder fires this when an InterfaceImpl is satisfied solely through a default that has been replaced by an abstract signature. Reserved so binary-compat regressions surface with a dedicated, actionable error.
member.param: The source location of the implementing aggregate identifier.
The interface that dropped the default.
The method that lost its default body.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceMethodHasBody(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0085 (issue #726): GS0186 — previously reported when an interface method carried a body in Phase 3 (ADR-0018 deferral). The deferral was reversed by ADR-0085, which implements default-interface methods, so this diagnostic is no longer emitted. The slot is preserved (rather than reused) so historical references in changelogs and PRs still resolve correctly.
member.param: The text location of the offending method identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceMethodMissingSemicolon(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports GS0368 — issue #881: an interface func declaration with no { … } body is missing its terminating ;. A bodyless func is the no-body (abstract) form, and G# requires ; as the universal no-body marker for every func declaration (matching the P/Invoke shape from ADR-0086). A func that carries a { … } block (default-interface method or default shared slot) must not take a ;.
member.param: The source location where the ; is expected (immediately after the return-type clause).
The name of the offending interface method.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceMethodModifierDeferred(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0085 / issue #726: GS0321 — a deferred modifier (currently static or private) appears on an interface method declaration. ADR-0085 intentionally keeps DIM minimal in this PR (instance-virtual default methods only); static-virtuals and private helpers are tracked as follow-ups and are rejected here.
member.param: The source location of the offending modifier or method identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfaceMethodNotImplemented(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Reports an aggregate that fails to implement an interface method.
member.param: The text location of the aggregate identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfacePropertySetterKindMismatch(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #2875: reports a setter-kind mismatch between an interface property and its implementation.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterfacePropertyTypeMismatch(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)

member.summary: Reports GS0330 — ADR-0089 / issue #755 (issue #865 revision): a non-func member appears inside an interface shared { … } block. member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterpolatedStringHandlerArgument(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #368: reports an interpolated string passed to an [InterpolatedStringHandler] parameter whose [InterpolatedStringHandlerArgument] forwarding could not be satisfied (an unknown referenced argument, a missing receiver, or no matching handler constructor).

A human-readable description of the failure.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportInterpolatedStringHandlerUnavailable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0545 (issue #3730): the framework the compilation references does not declare the DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler surface interpolated strings lower onto. member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportLocalFunctionCannotReferenceEnclosingTypeParameter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Reports that a local function references a type parameter owned by an enclosing generic method or class, directly in its own parameter type, return type, or body — the sibling invalid-IL shapes of issue #1940 (a GENERIC local function declaring its own [T, ...]) and issue #2016 (a NON-generic local function that captures no outer variables). A generic local function is hoisted to its own top-level static method carrying only its own type-parameter list as CLR method-generic (MVAR) slots; a non-generic, zero-capture local function is instead hoisted to a plain top-level static method (issue #1469's zero-capture fast path) unless nested inside a non-generic user type purely for accessibility. In both shapes, the enclosing method/class type parameter has no corresponding slot on the hoisted method, so referencing it would silently emit invalid IL (an unresolvable MVAR/VAR reference) that crashes at run time with InvalidProgramException or BadImageFormatException instead of failing to compile.
member.param: The text location of the declaration's identifier.
The name of the declared local function.
The name of the referenced enclosing type parameter.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportLockTargetMustBeReferenceType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)

member.param: The text location of the operand.

The display name of the override.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportMarshalAsMissingRequiredArgument(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0096 / issue #762: GS0359 — the @MarshalAs(...) annotation is missing a knob that is mandatory for the chosen . Examples: ByValTStr requires SizeConst; ByValArray requires SizeConst; LPArray requires at least one of SizeConst or SizeParamIndex for the runtime to know the element count.
member.param: The display name of the override.
The display name of the missing knob (e.g. SizeConst).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportMarshalAsRejected(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
ADR-0096 / issue #762: GS0360 — @MarshalAs is rejected on the offending P/Invoke parameter. The two cases reported under this code are:
The enclosing function is not a P/Invoke (@DllImport or @LibraryImport) declaration —
@MarshalAs on a managed function's parameter has no CLR-defined meaning and is rejected to avoid silently dropping the user's intent.
The enclosing function is a @LibraryImport stub and the offending parameter is a string. The
outer marshalling stub uses the function-wide StringMarshalling knob to pick its encoding; a per-parameter override would require generating per-parameter outer-stub code, which v1.0 of @LibraryImport does not surface. Use StringMarshalling on the @LibraryImport(...) annotation instead.
member.param: The case-specific reason (one of the bullets above).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportMarshalAsUnsupportedUnmanagedType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0096 / issue #762: GS0357 — the UnmanagedType value passed to @MarshalAs(...) is not in the v1 supported set. The supported values are LPStr, LPWStr, LPUTF8Str, BStr, LPArray, SafeArray, I1, U1, I2, U2, I4, U4, I8, U8, Bool, VariantBool, SysInt, SysUInt, Struct, ByValTStr, and ByValArray. Everything else (custom marshallers, IUnknown, FunctionPtr, …) is filed as a follow-up.
member.param: The display text of the rejected value.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeClassReturnNotSupported(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0093 / issue #759: GS0351 — a class type is used as the return type of a P/Invoke function. v1 supports class types only as parameters (passed by reference); the return-value ownership / allocation contract is deferred to a future ADR.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeDelegateMissingUnmanagedFunctionPointer(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0095 / issue #761: GS0353 — a delegate-typed parameter on a P/Invoke declaration is missing the @UnmanagedFunctionPointer attribute. Without that attribute the runtime cannot synthesize a stable function-pointer thunk for the delegate, and the call site has no way to communicate a calling convention to the native callee. The fix is to apply @UnmanagedFunctionPointer(CallingConvention.Cdecl) (or the appropriate calling convention) to the delegate declaration.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeDelegateReturnNotSupported(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0095 / issue #761: GS0355 — a delegate-typed value is being returned from a P/Invoke declaration. Returning a managed delegate from native code is not supported because the runtime would have to allocate a managed wrapper without knowing the lifetime contract of the function-pointer it received. The fix is to declare the return as unmanaged[CC] (...) -> R (a raw function pointer) or nint (an opaque handle that the caller can wrap manually with Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeMixedDllAndLibraryImport(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0092 / issue #758: GS0342 — a function carries both @DllImport and @LibraryImport. The two P/Invoke attribute shapes are mutually exclusive on the same declaration.
member.param: The location of the offending function identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeMustNotHaveBody(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports GS0324 when a function carries @DllImport but also has a managed body (ADR-0086 §1 / issue #727). P/Invoke stubs must use a ; body marker.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeNonBlittableByRefPointee(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0094 / issue #760: GS0352 — a ref/out/in parameter on a P/Invoke declaration uses a pointee type that is not byref-marshalling-compatible. The runtime marshals the parameter as T*, which requires the pointee to be blittable. The fix is to use a blittable primitive (e.g. int32, int64, nint) or a struct annotated with @StructLayout whose fields are all blittable. ref string in particular needs an explicit nint + Marshal.PtrToStringUTF8 round trip; the runtime cannot infer the unmanaged encoding for a byref slot.
member.param: The unsupported pointee type display name.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportPInvokeNonBlittableType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)

member.param: The display name of the offending type.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefKindOnAsyncOrIterator(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefKindOnPrimaryCtorParameter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0060 + ADR-0029: rejects a ref-kind modifier on a primary-constructor parameter. Primary-constructor parameters materialize fields, and the CLR cannot encode a managed-pointer (T&) as a field type. The user must drop the modifier or move the constructor body to a standalone init(...) that does not synthesize a backing field.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefKindOnVariadicParameter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0060 §8: reports a variadic parameter (...T) declared with a ref-kind modifier. The combination is forbidden — the CLR cannot express an array of by-ref values.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefLocalAliasCannotBeCaptured(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS9011 / issue #4271: a ref/var ref LOCAL alias of the enclosing function was captured by a closure (lambda or local function). Like the GS9010 ref-parameter capture, this is unsound — the alias's slot holds a managed pointer, and the CLR gives no way to keep it alive in a heap-allocated closure; unlike an ordinary captured local, it cannot be made safe by boxing it into a shared cell either (that would corrupt the aliasing itself). Rejected rather than silently compiled into a by-value snapshot that loses write-through.
member.param: The text location of the closure whose body captures the alias.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefLocalCannotBeDeclaredHere(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #491 (ADR-0060 follow-up): reports the ref aliasing modifier on a declaration that cannot legally store a managed pointer — a top-level binding (emitted as a static field), a local in an async function or iterator (hoisted into a state-machine field), or a const declaration.
member.param: Description of the disallowed context (e.g. "a top-level variable").

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefLocalRhsHasNarrowerEscapeScope(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #491 (ADR-0060 follow-up): reports a ref-aliasing local whose initializer's ref-safe-to-escape scope is narrower than the local's declaring scope. The aliased storage would not outlive the local; reading or writing through the alias is therefore unsafe. Reported, for example, when binding a ref local to a value whose pointee lives in a scoped ref struct or to a temporary that the local would outlive.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefLocalRhsMustBeLvalue(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #491 (ADR-0060 follow-up): reports a ref-aliasing local declaration whose initializer is not an lvalue. let ref / var ref binds the local as an alias for an existing storage slot — the RHS must therefore be a variable, a field/property access, an indexer access, or a dereference of a managed pointer.
member.param: The source text of the offending RHS expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefParameterCannotBeCaptured(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: GS9010 / issue #4259: a ref/out/in parameter of the enclosing function was captured by a closure (lambda or local function). Capturing a by-ref parameter into a heap-allocated closure is unsound — the referent's lifetime is not guaranteed to outlive the closure — so the capture is rejected rather than silently compiled into a by-value snapshot. Distinct from a ref/var ref LOCAL alias capture, which is a separate ParameterSymbol-free capture kind rejected by its own GS9011 (issue #4271).
member.param: The text location of the closure whose body captures the parameter.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefPropertyCannotHaveSetter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String)

member.param: The source location of the offending accessor.
The property name (or this[…] for an indexer).
The offending accessor keyword — set or init.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefPropertyRequiresComputedGetter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Reports GS0578 — issue #3879 (ADR-0060 amendment): a ref-returning property or indexer was declared without a bodied getter (an auto-property, a bare { get }, or an abstract/interface slot). A by-ref return has to name the storage it aliases, and only a computed getter can do that.
member.param: The source location of the property declaration.
The property name (or this[…] for an indexer).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefReturnEscapesLocalScope(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: Issue #490 (ADR-0058 ref-safe-to-escape): the operand of return ref refers to storage that dies at function exit (a local variable, a scoped parameter, or a field/element rooted in one of those). Returning that pointer would expose dangling memory to the caller.
member.param: The location of the offending expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportRefReturnThroughDefensivelyCopiedReceiver(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: ADR-0184 amendment, caller side (the CS8156 analogue): the operand of return ref forwards a reference out of a member invoked on a READ-ONLY receiver — an in parameter, a ref readonly alias, or a ref readonly call/property result. The emitter defensively copies such a receiver into a function-local temp before the call, so the returned reference aliases the temp and dangles once the function returns. Reported in place of the generic because the copy has no spelling in the source the author wrote.
member.param: The location of the offending expression.

member.param: The source location of the literal's ref return modifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportSizeOfRequiresUnmanagedType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: Issue #1336: GS0415 — a sizeof(T) expression names a type that is not an unmanaged type. sizeof measures the unmanaged byte size of its operand, so the operand must be a blittable primitive, an enum, a pointer, a blittable value struct, or a generic type parameter constrained unmanaged; managed reference types and non-blittable structs are rejected (mirrors C#'s sizeof over unmanaged types).
member.param: The text location of the measured type clause.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportStackAllocCountInferredWithoutInitializer(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation)
member.summary: GS0411: a count-inferred stackalloc []T expression (ADR-0124 / issue #1041) was written without a brace-delimited initializer, so the element count cannot be determined. The count-inferred shape takes its length from the initializer (stackalloc []T{a, b, …}); supply an initializer or spell the count explicitly (stackalloc [n]T).
member.param: The text location of the stackalloc expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportStackAllocElementTypeNotBlittable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String)
member.summary: GS0399: a stackalloc [n]T expression (ADR-0124 / issue #1024) names an element type T that is not unmanaged/blittable. Stack buffers are raw, GC-untracked memory, so only blittable primitives (int8…int64, uint8…uint64, nint, nuint, float32, float64, bool, char) and pointers are permitted as the element type.
member.param: The text location of the element-type identifier.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportStackAllocInitializerLengthMismatch(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: GS0412: a stackalloc [n]T{…} expression (ADR-0124 / issue #1041) gave an explicit constant count n that disagrees with the number of initializer elements. As in C#, the explicit length and the initializer element count must match exactly; use the count-inferred shape (stackalloc []T{…}) to avoid repeating the length.
member.param: The text location of the stackalloc expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.ReportTypeParameterConstraintConflict(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLocation,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Reports GS0361 — ADR-0097 / issue #775: a type-parameter constraint list combines mutually exclusive flag constraints. member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.SuppressMemberLookupCascadeIn``1(System.Func{``0})
member.summary:
Issue #3887: runs a member lookup whose receiver is already error-typed, dropping only the GS0158 Cannot find member / GS0159 Cannot find function that such a lookup is guaranteed to produce.
The receiver can only carry TypeSymbol.Error downstream of an expression that was already diagnosed, so those two reports are always redundant with that earlier diagnostic — and actively misdirecting, since they name members that exist on the type the user meant. Every other diagnostic the lookup raises is kept.
Nothing about BINDING changes — this alters which diagnostics are emitted, never what binds. Two narrower-looking designs were tried and are wrong:
Returning an error expression instead of performing the lookup. Member resolution has
load-bearing side effects, and skipping it made an unrelated type stop resolving in a REPL session (Issue710NullConditionalIndexingEmittedSessionTests).
Dropping the diagnostic in Add. The binder's speculative rebinds use deltas and
as their success signal, so never adding an entry silently changes which lookup path the binder COMMITS to — the same session tests failed again, for a second, different reason.
So the entry is added exactly as before and merely marked; the filter happens when diagnostics are read. Count, TruncateTo and every binding decision see the bag unchanged.
member.typeparam: The result type of the binding operation.
member.returns: The result of .

member.summary: Removes every diagnostic added after the bag reached entries, restoring it to an earlier marked state. Used to roll back the speculative diagnostics produced while eagerly binding an expression that will be re-bound against a now-known target type.
member.param: The diagnostic count to truncate back to. Values outside the current range are clamped.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.DiagnosticBag.Visible
member.summary: Issue #3887: the diagnostics a caller should SEE — everything in the bag except the redundant member-lookup cascade recorded by . The bag itself keeps those entries so and retain their exact meaning for the binder's speculative-rebind paths.

Issue #909 / ADR-0109: maps a function's source accessibility to IL visibility, accounting for whether the function is a top-level member of the synthetic <Program> type.
Top-level private functions live on <Program>, but the binder's accessibility model treats them as assembly-visible: sibling top-level types (e.g. a user class) in the same assembly may call them. Mapping source private to IL makes the CLR enforce private-to-<Program>, which DISAGREES with the binder and yields a runtime despite a clean compile. We therefore emit top-level private as IL assembly (internal) so the IL accessibility matches what the binder already permits.
This remapping is scoped to <Program> members ONLY. A private member of a user-defined class/struct/ interface keeps IL so the CLR continues to enforce real user-type privacy.
member.param: The source accessibility of the function.
true when the function is hosted on the synthetic <Program> type (see ).
member.returns: The IL visibility .

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.AssemblyAttributeEmitter.EmitGSharpMagicCollectionFieldMarkers(System.Reflection.Metadata.AssemblyDefinitionHandle)
member.summary: Issue #3329: emits the GSharp.MagicCollectionFields marker for every VALUE-TYPE struct with at least one ADR-0159 magic-collection field (map/slice/fixed array/sequence) — independent of 's data struct/primary- constructor gate, so a PLAIN field-only struct is covered too. A struct literal for a type referenced from ANOTHER assembly (or, for the REPL, an EARLIER submission) cannot see the declaring compilation's own (only that compilation ever binds the struct's own field declarations); this marker lets it reconstruct the exact same sound zero value instead of silently leaving such a field at its raw CLR default (typically a null reference — the class of bug fixed by #3329). A class literal needs no marker: constructing it always calls its REAL parameterless constructor, which already runs these initializers in-type.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ConstructorBodyEmitter.NeedsSynthesizedValueStructDefaultCtor(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #3219: a value-kind struct whose declared field initializers include a NON-public field cannot be materialized by the historical call-site lowering (initobj + raw stfld per initializer) — the private-field store executes outside the type and the runtime rejects it with . Such a struct gets a synthesized owning .ctor that runs ALL declared instance field initializers in-type (mirroring the class default-ctor path), and struct-literal sites construct through it. Generic structs also require in-type initialization: their definition-bound expressions cannot execute in the literal site's generic context (#4755). Primary structs use their primary signature so declaration initializers retain the actual constructor parameter scope (#4747). Non-generic structs whose initializers are all public keep the historical inline emission. Authored parameterless constructors remain separate through a hidden literal initializer signature. Imported CLR types and inline structs (fixed synthesized-member layout) are excluded.
member.returns: true when an owning initializer ctor is required.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.CustomAttributeEncoder.EmitNullableAttributeOnEvent(System.Reflection.Metadata.EventDefinitionHandle,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: ADR-0186 §8: emits a per-event System.Runtime.CompilerServices.NullableAttribute on an Event row under the same "deviates from non-null default" condition as . The Event row is where the import side reads an event's handler nullability (MemberLookup.ApplyEventDeclarationNullability reads ClrNullability.ReadNullableFlags off the event), and it is where csc writes it; before ADR-0186 step 5 gsc wrote nothing there, so an event's handler type re-imported through the type-level [NullableContext(1)] as wholly non-null — an @Oblivious event came back non-null, and so did the string? in an Action[string?] handler.

Selects the primary or an explicit constructor by exact arity against 's positional arguments (the same "match the constructor shape" step does for CLR types, minus params-array expansion, which no G# constructor declaration can express) and writes the fixed-argument blob using each parameter's own (always-primitive-or-string, hence already-resolved) TypeSymbol.ClrType.

Reimplementing that against fields/properties (including nested-enum underlying types, arguments, etc.) is a separate, considerably larger feature than closing the GS0200 recognition gap this issue is about. Named arguments on a same-compilation user attribute are now rejected at bind time (GS0466, see DeclarationBinder.BindAttribute), so never carries any by the time it reaches the emitter — this method only ever writes NumNamed = 0.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.CustomAttributeEncoder.GetEnumUnderlyingTypeSafe(System.Type)
member.summary: Returns the underlying primitive type of an enum in a way that works for types loaded through a . The BCL helper ) requires a runtime and throws for metadata-loaded types (issue #418 / P1-8), which surfaces as an emit-time crash in the custom-attribute blob writer whenever an attribute argument is an enum defined in a referenced (non-BCL) package.
member.remarks: Per ECMA-335 II.14.3 every enum is laid out as a class containing a single instance field named value__ whose type is the underlying primitive (e.g. ). Reading that field's type works uniformly for runtime and metadata-loaded types. The result is then normalized to the executing runtime's so that the reference-equality dispatch in the blob writers matches.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.CustomAttributeEncoder.GetSerializedTypeName(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #4073: writes the assembly-qualified name of a SYMBOLIC typeof argument, recursing through every structural position so a constructed generic names its real arguments.
member.returns: The assembly-qualified name.
member.remarks:
This used to be one line — the type's own metadata name plus the assembly under compilation — which is correct for a scalar same-compilation type and wrong for everything else. A constructed generic's DEFINITION usually lives in a referenced assembly while its arguments live here, so a single trailing assembly name cannot describe it; and the definition needs its arity suffix and an argument list, which a constructed could not supply because it carries its arguments on TypeArguments and leaves TypeParameters empty (so the suffix computed to zero and typeof(MyBox[Status]) serialised as the unresolvable P.MyBox).
The shape is ECMA-335 I.8.5.2 / : Ns.DefN[[argAqn],[argAqn]], DefAssembly, with array and Nullable wrappers attaching to the NAME while the assembly stays the wrapped part's (respectively the core library's).

member.remarks: The host's own typeof(Dictionary<,>) is deliberately not used: the name written into the blob must be the one the emitted assembly references. Never MakeGenericType — a same-compilation argument has no CLR type to close over, which is the whole reason this serialiser exists.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.CustomAttributeEncoder.TryGetAttributeParameterWriteType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol,System.Type@)
member.summary: The CLR type the fixed-argument writer should encode one same-compilation constructor parameter AS.
member.param: The CLR type to encode the argument as.
member.returns: Whether the parameter can be encoded at all.
member.remarks:
Issue #4097, found in the Oahu corpus: a user attribute whose constructor parameter is a same-compilation ENUM — @OahuCapability(CapabilityClass.Safe) — has no ClrType while the blob is built, because the enum's TypeDef only exists at emit. The whole attribute used to be dropped in silence, and a first pass at this issue reported it as unsupported. Both are wrong: the program is legal, and ECMA-335 II.23.3 writes an enum-typed fixed argument as its UNDERLYING primitive, which is available here.
Three facts make this a substitution rather than a feature. The underlying type of a G# enum is always int32; the bound argument value is already that underlying constant, not a symbol (the binder's enum-literal arm stores lit.Value); and the constructor's own token and signature come from the emitted MethodDef via the injected resolvers, so nothing on this path has to encode the enum type itself. Only the value's WIDTH was ever missing.

member.remarks: What was wrong. Each structural symbol computes its own ClrType by closing an open BCL definition over its components. A same-compilation component has none while binding, so the structural symbol's ClrType came out null and the switch fell through to GetMetadataTypeName's default: arm — bare type.Name, which for these kinds is the G# DISPLAY spelling (map[string,Status], (Status) -> bool, chan), qualified to the compilation's own assembly. Nothing can decode that. Why there is no { ClrType: null } guard. The obvious spelling of these arms — gate on a null ClrType, the way the StructSymbol/InterfaceSymbol arms do — would leave a quieter half of the same defect in place. map[string, List[Status]] has a component whose ClrType is NON-null: List

member.summary: Appends a string literal to the builder produced by .

Appends and then the member's value to the builder produced by , as Roslyn's synthesized PrintMembers does: a non-nullable value-typed member (or a value-type-constrained type parameter) is rendered by a constrained. ToString() call on its address, so a mutating ToString and a ref-like value are honoured; any other member (references, unconstrained type parameters, Nullable<T>) is appended as object, where null prints nothing. member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.EmitDiagnosticException.ThrowAttributeConstructorParameterTypeNotSupported(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Throws a failure that surfaces as GS0584: a user-defined attribute one of whose constructor parameters is not a valid attribute parameter type.
member.remarks:
Issue #4097's sibling cause. The row used to be dropped in silence; this is the last line that stops it vanishing.
Its population was MEASURED rather than assumed, over a probe comparing gsc against csc on the same shapes: every shape that reaches here is one C# rejects as CS0181 — a same-compilation class, interface, delegate, or a structural type. There is no legal-but-unencodable residue, so this does NOT claim an encoder limit. The one shape that looked like one, a same-compilation enum parameter, is encoded through its underlying primitive instead (issue #4135); the Oahu corpus carries it, and reporting it here took four of that corpus's apps red.
Emit is the wrong PLACE for this check — it belongs on the attribute's declaration, once, the way csc reports CS0181 — but G# has no such bind-time rule today, so these programs reach emit unchecked. Filed as issue #4143; when it lands this becomes unreachable and can retire.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.FunctionEmitter.EmitLibraryImportFunction(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol)
member.summary:
ADR-0092 / issue #758: emits an @LibraryImport function as a pair of MethodDef rows — the user-visible managed stub (planned at cache.FunctionHandles[function]) and a hidden blittable inner P/Invoke (planned at cache.LibraryImportInnerHandles[function]). The stub:
For each string parameter, marshals it explicitly into a CoTaskMem buffer (UTF-8 or UTF-16 per
the resolved mode) and stores the resulting IntPtr in a local.
Calls the inner P/Invoke inside a try block, passing the marshalled IntPtr in place of each
string parameter.
Frees the marshalled buffers in a finally block via ), which
is a no-op on .
When the function returns string, the inner P/Invoke returns the raw native pointer (encoded as
IntPtr) and the outer stub materializes the managed string via ) / ). The returned native buffer is non-owning (the native side owns it, e.g. getenv) and is never freed — see the ADR-0092 return-marshalling table. The result is verifiable IL that has no runtime marshalling stub — every transition is explicit and AOT-publishable.
member.returns: The handle of the emitted outer managed stub.

Issue #1449: Gets a MemberRef for a delegate's canonical (object, IntPtr) constructor in a TypeBuilder-safe way.
Calling ) on a constructed generic delegate type (e.g. Func<…> / Action<…>) that is realized as a reflection-emit TypeBuilderInstantiation throws ("TypeBuilder generic instantiation does not support resolving members. Use TypeBuilder.GetConstructor instead."). This happens both when a type argument is a closed in the same compilation (#671) and when the instantiation is constructed against the in-progress assembly even though every type argument is a runtime type (#1449). member.summary: Issue #4938: the token for an opcode that names a type's exact identity rather than a value's runtime type: the array-element opcodes (newarr, ldelem, stelem, ldelema) and ldtoken for typeof(T). An array must match its T[] signature, and typeof must reflect the written type. For a function pointer that is the FNPTR TypeSpec: newarr System.IntPtr would create an IntPtr[] where the signature says method …*[] (issue #4684), and typeof(unmanaged[CC] () -> R) is a function-pointer Type (IsFunctionPointer), not IntPtr. Every other type tokenises exactly as does, which gives a function pointer its runtime projection, System.IntPtr.

member.summary: Issue #4614: emit MethodImpl rows binding the static-virtual (static abstract or defaulted static virtual) slots of the imported CLR interfaces implements to its own matching static methods.
member.remarks: The CLR never binds a static-virtual slot by name: without a MethodImpl a direct implementer (struct SD : IS) failed to load, and a type re-listing such an interface over an imported base that already implements it (class DZ : BaseS, IS2) silently kept the base's implementation. This pass binds the type's own static member of the same name and signature implicitly, as csc does, with one deliberate difference: csc requires that member to be public, while this pass (like for G#-declared interfaces) applies no accessibility check, so an own-type member of any accessibility implements the slot. That is G#'s existing policy, not an omission. The interfaces come from , the same set the type's InterfaceImpl rows are emitted from, so slots inherited through a base interface are covered and every declaration resolves against a listed interface. A slot the type does not implement gets no row, so an imported base's implementation (or the slot's default) still applies.

member.summary: ADR-0149: emit MethodImpl rows for explicit-interface-clause EVENT implementations (event (IFoo) Changed T) — the event-level counterpart of , generalizing the #2362 explicit-implementation convention to events for the first time. An event whose is set explicitly implements one specific in-compilation interface event; its add/ remove (and, if present, raise) accessors are bridged into that interface's abstract slots via one MethodImpl row per accessor, exactly mirroring the property function's generic-aware token resolution.

member.summary:
Issue #985 / #2010: emit MethodImpl rows for covariant-return interface bridges AND for mangled-name explicit interface implementations. A method whose is set explicitly implements a specific (typically inherited, non-generic) CLR interface slot — e.g. the private non-generic IEnumerable.GetEnumerator() alongside the public generic IEnumerable<T>.GetEnumerator(). A private bridge method cannot implicitly implement an interface slot, so the explicit row is required for the resulting type to load.
A method whose is set explicitly implements one specific in-compilation (G#) interface member — its mangled name never matches the interface member's own name, so ordinary name-based virtual dispatch never wires it into that interface's slot; an explicit MethodImpl row is required here too (mirrors 's generic-aware token resolution for a constructed interface).

member.summary: Issue #2362: emit MethodImpl rows for mangled-name explicit interface PROPERTY implementations — the property-level counterpart of . An explicit MethodImpl row per accessor (getter and/or setter) is required, exactly mirroring 's generic-aware token resolution for a constructed interface, but for an INSTANCE property slot resolved from rather than a static-virtual slot.

Issue #2181: maps a (possibly substituted) instance method slot on a constructed generic interface back to its open declaration on the interface definition — the counterpart of for the (non-static) table. Collects every type parameter referenced anywhere in into (order/duplicates are the caller's concern; deduplicates and canonicalizes).

Issue #4223: optional lookup of a called function's OWN promoted-extra enclosing type parameters (UserTokenResolver.GetPromotedExtras). A direct call to a callee that was itself promoted to carry enclosing type parameters requires the CALLER to supply them at the call site — a requirement invisible in the call's own argument/return types whenever the callee uses that parameter only in a body-only position (e.g. an implicit static-owner-type reference, typeof, or a constraint). Passing this lookup lets the caller discover and promote itself for the same parameters in turn; omitting it (the default) preserves the pre-#4223 behavior for a caller that does not need it (a capturing display class's reification, which runs before any zero-capture promotion in the same pass and so has nothing to look up yet).

member.summary:
Issue #3879 (ADR-0060 amendment): encodes a property's type into the return-type slot of a PropertyDef or accessor MethodDef signature, honouring the property's . A ref-returning property is T& in BOTH signatures — ECMA-335 §II.23.2.5 allows ELEMENT_TYPE_BYREF in a PropertySig, and the two have to agree. Encoding only the getter does not merely cost the alias: measured, Roslyn refuses the member outright with CS1546 ("Property, indexer, or event 'Holder.Property' is not supported by the language; try directly calling accessor method 'Holder.get_Property()'").
This is the single funnel for every property-signature return slot (instance, static, interface, indexer, and the metadata-only fallback), so the implementation assembly and the reference assembly cannot disagree about a property's ref-kind.
member.param: The property whose type is encoded.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitCheckedIntegralNegation(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundUnaryExpression)
member.summary: Issue #2023: emits checked(0 - x) for an integral unary negation bound inside a checked(...)/checked { } context. The constant zero is pushed first (per ECMA-335 III.3.62's binary-numeric-operator table an int32 literal freely combines with an int32-, sub-int32-, or native-int-typed value — only int64 requires the widened int64 zero), then the operand, then sub.ovf (never the .un variant: negation is only ever defined over the signed integral primitives). For the sub-int32 operand widths (sbyte/short) the CLR promotes both operands to int32 before subtracting, so sub.ovf alone cannot observe the exact-MinValue overflow (e.g. 0 - sbyte.MinValue == 128, which fits an int32 comfortably); a checked narrowing conversion (conv.ovf.i1/conv.ovf.i2) back to the operand's own width closes that gap, mirroring how checked narrowing conversions (issue #1881) already trap the same shape.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitConstrainedTypeParameterReceiver(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression)
member.summary: Issue #943: loads the address of a receiver whose static type is a type parameter constrained to a CLR interface, so it can feed a constrained. prefix on the subsequent callvirt. A managed pointer is required regardless of whether the type argument is ultimately a value type or a reference type — the constrained. opcode handles both. Addressable variables (parameters, locals, globals) load directly; non-addressable rvalue receivers are spilled to a pre-planned local.
member.remarks: Issue #2335 (audit follow-up): a NARROWED variable receiver (ADR-0069 smart-cast — bve.NarrowedType != null, e.g. if x is T { x.ToString() } narrowing an object-typed parameter/local to a type-parameter view T) must NOT take the fast "own address" path even though it IS a : the narrowed view still physically lives in the wider DECLARED storage slot (e.g. an object field/parameter/local), so ldarga/ldloca on that slot yields <declared>& (e.g. object&) — NOT the !!T& the constrained. prefix requires. ilverify rejects the mismatch (StackUnexpected), and the wrong pointer shape would misinterpret the receiver's bytes at runtime for shared generic code. plans a spill slot (typed as the NARROWED type, since BoundVariableExpression.Type reports NarrowedType ?? Variable.Type) for exactly this case, so falling through to the general rvalue-spill path below — re-materializes the correctly narrowed !!T value via EmitNarrowingCastIfNeeded — produces a verifiable, correctly-addressed receiver.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitInterfaceMergeCastIfNeeded(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #1480: when a conditional/if-expression or null-coalescing (??) result type is an interface (or a nullable interface), a class branch that implements that interface is a reference-level no-op at emit time — the value left on the stack is the concrete class, not the interface. At the branches' merge point the CLR verifier computes the least-common type of the two branch classes, which is their shared base class (the verifier merge never yields an interface), so the merged value fails to satisfy the interface-typed consumer (StackUnexpected [found ref 'Base'][expected ref 'IShape']) → unverifiable IL / . Emit an explicit castclass to the interface on each value branch so both branches leave exactly the interface reference and the merge is the interface itself. The cast is verifiable because the binder already proved every branch implicitly converts to the interface. A never (throw) or nil branch leaves no class value to realign and is skipped.

Both the named-delegate path () and the synthesized/CLR-delegate path ()) share this single implementation so the #1397 interface-receiver ldvirtftn and #1467 generic-receiver token handling live in exactly one place.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitNarrowingCastIfNeeded(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundVariableExpression)
member.summary:
ADR-0069 / issue #700: when a variable read carries a narrowed type distinct from the variable's declared type, emit a single conversion opcode so the IL stack matches the narrower type:
unbox.any T when the narrowed type is a value type — the load left a boxed reference on the
stack and we need the native value-type representation back.
castclass T when the narrowed type is a reference type — the load left a base-class or interface
reference on the stack and we need the derived reference. The CLR-level cast is guaranteed to succeed because the binder placed it inside a region where an is test already verified the runtime type at the same site.
The cast is suppressed when the narrowing is a pure nullable strip (e.g. string? → string) — the underlying CLR representation is identical, and emitting castclass would still be sound but pointlessly grows the body.

member.param: The statically declared type of the read.
The narrowed type, or null when not narrowed.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitNullAssertionThrow(System.String)
member.summary: Emits the throw half of a null assertion: newobj + throw, choosing the message-carrying constructor for ADR-0186 §4's synthesized coercion check and the parameterless one for a user-written !!.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitNullGuardedDelegateToDelegateAdaptation(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression,System.Reflection.Metadata.EntityHandle,System.Reflection.Metadata.EntityHandle)
member.summary:
Issue #2066 / #2083: emits the shared dup / ldvirtftn / newobj delegate-to-delegate adaptation sequence.
When recognizes a source that can legitimately be null, the sequence is guarded so a null source flows through as null instead of unconditionally rebuilding a delegate — without the guard, ldvirtftn resolves the (non-null) Invoke method pointer even over a null instance reference, and the subsequent newobj then throws at runtime ("Delegate to an instance method cannot have null 'this'") because the CLR delegate ctor requires a non-null target for an instance-method pointer.
For every other source, that same throw is the desired fail-fast behavior: a non-nullable local/parameter/field that is unexpectedly null at runtime indicates a null-safety bug. Every non-nullable case therefore keeps the plain branch-free sequence.
The null path (guarded case only) must not leave the un-adapted source value (statically typed as the *source* delegate type, e.g. Func<string>) on the stack: when the target is a covariant-adapted delegate type (e.g. Func<object>), merging that source-typed value with the non-null path's newly- constructed *target*-typed value at the shared label widens the verifier-computed stack type down to their common ancestor (), which then fails to verify against the target's expected type. Instead, the null path pops the leftover copy and pushes an explicit ldnull, whose null-reference type merges cleanly with any reference type, including the adapted target delegate type.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitPropertyAccess(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundPropertyAccessExpression,System.Boolean)
member.param: Issue #4224: when true, leaves the getter's raw result on the stack without the read tail's dereference/narrowing-cast — used by EmitAddressOf to take the address of a ref-returning property instead of loading through it.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.EmitRefReturnDereferenceIfNeeded(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefKind,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary:
Issue #3879 (ADR-0060 amendment, ADR-0056 §1): a call to a ref-returning G# member leaves a managed pointer (T&) on the stack, but the bound tree types the read as the POINTEE T — G#'s ref-alias binder does not accept a call result as an lvalue (the documented #1900 limit), so every G# read of such a member is a value read. Load through the pointer so the stack matches the bound type.
Without this the IL is either unverifiable (InvalidProgramException when the pointer flows into a by-value parameter) or a silent wrong answer (the raw address printed as an int32). That is the pre-existing shape of issue #490's deferred "consume a ref return at a G# call site", which a ref-returning PROPERTY would otherwise inherit — and a property read is far more common than a method-call read, so it is closed here rather than left to surface as new behaviour.
The guard is load-bearing: an IMPORTED ref-returning member is already surfaced as ByRefTypeSymbol and dereferenced by the binder (ConversionClassifier.AutoDereferenceRefReturn), and BaseCallForwarderRewriter synthesizes a forwarder that keeps that by-ref result type while also setting . Dereferencing there too would be a double load.
member.param: The type the bound tree gives the read.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.InstanceAccessorOpCode(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression)
member.summary: Issue #4312: the one decision that picks call or callvirt for an instance accessor on a bound receiver.
member.param: The bound receiver the accessor is invoked on.
member.returns: call for a value-type receiver, callvirt otherwise.
member.remarks: It is the complement of the predicate EmitInstanceReceiver uses to decide how the receiver is loaded: a value-type receiver was loaded as a managed pointer and takes call; every other receiver is a reference at run time and takes callvirt, so the CLR performs the null check on the receiver and an override accessor dispatches on the run-time type. The earlier tests (is StructSymbol {IsClass: true} or is InterfaceSymbol) answered call for any reference receiver whose type symbol was wrapped. A base. access never reaches this: it is lowered to a synthesized forwarder, which emits its own non-virtual call.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsAddressableFieldAccess(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundFieldAccessExpression)

Static fields are always addressable; instance fields on class receivers are addressable (the receiver is an object reference); instance fields on value-type receivers are addressable only if the receiver itself is addressable (a variable, or another addressable field access).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsKnownLegitimateNullDelegateSource(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression)
member.summary: Returns true when can legitimately contain a null delegate: either its effective type is nullable, or it reads a field-like event's compiler-synthesized backing field (which is null before the first subscription despite its non-nullable declared type). Smart-cast narrowing changes the effective type, so a guarded nullable source remains on the branch-free non-null path.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsNaturalDelegateShapeOf(System.Type,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #4358: whether is the natural structural delegate shape materialises as — the same System.FuncN / System.Action[N] definition SignatureEncoder.ResolveDelegateClrType builds for it.
member.returns: true when the target is the natural shape.
member.remarks: The name alone is not enough: a user assembly may declare its own System.Func (issue #2948 supports exactly that collision), which is a named delegate with a fixed signature. Comparing against the natural definition for THIS source also pins the arity, so a same-named delegate of a different arity can never qualify. Compared by full name and assembly identity, since the two may come from different reflection contexts (reference identity and ClrTypeUtilities.AreSame, which is full-name based, are not usable here).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsNonNullableValueOperand(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #2333: returns true when is a bare (non-) value type — a primitive, enum, struct, tuple, or a type parameter constrained to struct. Such a type's runtime representation on the evaluation stack is never a CLR null, so a null-assertion (!!) over it needs no runtime check at all. Used by EmitUnary's arm to recognise an operand that is either a direct non-nullable value or the result of a smart-cast-narrowed nullable value-type read (which 's BuildNarrowedRead already unwrapped via a synthesized inner !!).
member.returns: true when no runtime null check applies.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsOpenTypeParameterOrNullable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #831 / #2300: returns true when is an open type parameter, either bare (T) or wrapped in a (T?), regardless of constraint. The CLR storage is either a bare !!T reference slot (class/unconstrained/interface-constrained T, bare or ? — same shape either way) or a Nullable<!!T> value-typed slot (struct-constrained T?) — see . Both shapes need the same box; ldnull; ceq lowering for nil-comparison to be verifier-clean: boxing a reference is a JIT-elided no-op, while boxing Nullable<T> per ECMA-335 III.4.1 yields a managed-null reference when HasValue is false.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.IsStringOrNullableStringEmit(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #1927: true when is string, string? or (ADR-0186 §6 / issue #4324) string!. All three are a possibly-null string reference at runtime, so the existing String.Concat/String.Equals IL handles them without extra null-checks. This must stay in step with the binder's BoundBinaryOperator.IsStringOrNullableString: the binder deciding the operator exists while the emitter declines to emit it is a crash, not a diagnostic.
member.returns: Whether the operand is a string in any of the three states.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.RequiresChannelConversionEmission(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.ResolveImportedPositionalConstructor(System.Type,System.Int32)

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.ResolveInterfaceSlotOwner(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.InterfaceSymbol,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #3907: resolves the interface that actually DECLARES the slot a call reaches through , together with that interface's open method.
member.returns: The declaring interface and its open method.
member.remarks:
only ever searched the receiver interface's own definition, so a slot INHERITED from a base interface found nothing and the call fell through to the bare-MethodDef lookup, which threw "has no emitted handle". Parenting the MemberRef at the receiver interface would have been just as wrong — the derived interface's TypeSpec does not declare the method — so both halves have to move together.
SelfAndAllBaseInterfaces yields this first, so a slot the receiver declares itself still wins, and each base arrives ALREADY SUBSTITUTED with the receiver's type arguments (see InterfaceSymbol.BaseInterfaces), which is what makes the resulting MemberRef parent the constructed IBase<T> rather than the open definition. Methods is per-interface and excludes inherited members, so a candidate matching by identity is genuinely the declarer.
This is the shape ADR-0174's channels runtime is built on: ISendSelectableCore[T] : ISelectableCore[T], with Deregister declared on the base and called through the derived interface.

Whether the caller needs the receiver's address (value-type this) rather than its value.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.TryGetOpenTypeParameter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol@)
member.summary: Issue #831: returns true when resolves to an open type parameter that is NOT struct-constrained, either directly (e.g. after a smart-cast narrowing) or via a wrapper. Used by the !! (NullAssertion) emit path to recognise both self T? and the narrowed bare-T operand shape produced after a preceding nil-check guard.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.TryLoadStructVariableAddress(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundVariableExpression)
member.summary: Loads the address of a struct-typed receiver that is a bare variable read, honoring ADR-0069 smart-cast narrowing (issue #1917). When the variable's OWN declared type already agrees with the receiver's (possibly narrowed) struct type, the address is the variable's own storage — delegates to (ldarga/ldloca). When the receiver is a NARROWED read of a variable declared as a REFERENCE type (e.g. an object/interface-typed parameter smart-cast to a struct by an is test — obj is Money && obj.Cents), the variable's slot holds a boxed reference, not struct storage: taking its address directly pushes the address of the object SLOT, which a subsequent ldfld/ldflda Money::… rejects at verification time (ilverify: "found address of 'object', expected readonly address of 'Money'" — the CLR JIT tolerates the mismatched stack shape, but ilverify's stricter typed-stack model does not). The correct sequence loads the boxed reference then unboxes it: this yields a controlled-mutability (read-only) managed pointer directly to the embedded value — matching both what ilverify expects and what csc emits for the equivalent C# pattern.
member.returns: true once the address (or unboxed pointer) is on the stack.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.TryMatchTypeParameterNilCompare(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBinaryExpression,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundExpression@)
member.summary: Issue #831 / #2300: matches T? == nil / T? != nil AND bare T == nil / T != nil (and their symmetric nil == ... forms) where T is an open type parameter (class-constrained, struct- constrained-but-nullable-wrapped, interface-constrained, or unconstrained). The concrete value-type Nullable<T> arm (driven by ) only catches operands with a static ClrType; open type parameters have none, so this match fills the gap. The caller boxes the matched operand using its full type token, which resolves to a bare reference slot for class/unconstrained/interface-constrained T (bare or T? — both have the same storage shape) and to Nullable<!!T> for a struct-constrained T? (a bare struct-constrained T never reaches here — the binder's IsNullCompare rejects it because it can never be nil).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.UnwrapReferenceNullable(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #2840 / #2841: strips reference-nullable wrappers so the delegate-materialisation arms of see the bare function / delegate shape. (The channel arm above needs no help: looks through both wrapper kinds itself.) A over a reference type is a binder-level annotation that erases to the underlying type's CLR representation, so a D? or ((P…) -> R)? slot materialises byte-identically to its bare form. Genuine Nullable<T> value shapes are left wrapped so they keep reaching the value-type arms.
member.param: The declared source or target type of the conversion.
member.returns: The unwrapped type, or when no reference-nullable wrapper applies.

Issue #1515: recurse the label/local pre-pass into a pattern-switch arm body. Arm bodies are normally , but a non-block statement is tolerated by wrapping it so that any nested label-generating construct (loops, nested switches, try/finally, scope, select, fixed, …) at any depth is still visited.

member.remarks: A class reified generic over its enclosing type parameters () carries type-parameter constraints that still textually reference the ORIGINAL enclosing type parameters: cannot rewrite an imported constructed-generic constraint such as IComparable[T] (its substitution leaves the original symbolic argument in place). The deferred GenericParamConstraint rows would otherwise be resolved at flush time — after the remap is gone — encoding the enclosing METHOD type parameter as !!0 (MVar) instead of this class's own !0 (Var). That mismatch makes the class's constraint unsatisfiable, so the constrained. interface call inside a capturing lambda's display-class Invoke fails verification (StackUnexpected). Resolving here, with the remap active, encodes the class's own Var slot. Mirrors the #2118 non-capturing method path (which resolves against ). No-op when no reified-class remap is active (unregistered class).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ReflectionMetadataEmitter.ProgramHostAccessibility(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PackageSymbol,System.Boolean,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ReflectionMetadataEmitter.PackageMethodPlan)
member.summary: Issue #4676: the accessibility of a package's synthesized <Program> host type. The host is how a package exposes its top-level functions to other assemblies, so it stays public whenever it carries a function another assembly can reach, and in an executable (every package of an executable keeps its host public, to leave application behaviour alone). A LIBRARY package that hosts no such member (every GSharp.Core namespace whose code is all types, say) is a compiler-generated detail, like the C# compiler's own generated types, and is emitted NotPublic so it is not part of the assembly's API (reflection-based tooling such as an analyzer-target enumeration no longer sees one <Program> per namespace). An assembly granted InternalsVisibleTo still reaches the host's internal members, since it can see the NotPublic type too.
member.param: The package whose host is being emitted.
Whether the compilation has an entry point (an executable).
member.returns: The type visibility flag for the host's TypeDef.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.SignatureEncoder.ResolveTargetDelegateClrType(System.Type)
member.summary:
Issue #295: map an arbitrary CLR delegate type (named or generic, e.g. System.Predicate<int>, RequestDelegate, System.EventHandler) from the host runtime onto the emitter's reference (MetadataLoadContext) types, reconstructing constructed generics from a reference open definition so the produced TypeSpec / MemberRef binds to the target framework assemblies. Falls back to the host type when no reference mapping is available.
Issue #2325: this used to carry its own constructed-generic remapping loop, separate from (and ahead of) the one in — which only did a flat full-name lookup and therefore could not resolve a constructed generic argument (e.g. the inner Action<object> of Action<Action<object>, object>). That let a nested/ higher-order delegate mix a MetadataLoadContext open definition with a host-context type argument, which MakeGenericType rejects at emit time (GS9998). MapToReferenceClrType now performs the same recursive remapping itself, so both callers share one implementation.
member.remarks: Falls back to when the reference set has no matching type, exactly as every other caller does: an unmappable delegate is still a delegate the emitter must reference, and both callers here feed the result straight into a MemberRef/TypeRef that a null would only turn into a null dereference. Issue #4381: a delegate already loaded from a supplied reference keeps that exact identity because another assembly may define the same full name. Only host-fallback types need projection into the target context.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.StateMachineEmitter.GetAsyncKickoffGenericScope(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #3939: the single place that decides which type parameters are in scope at an ASYNC kickoff method — the owning type's, then the kickoff's own, in Roslyn order. Two emit paths depend on this list agreeing exactly: ReflectionMetadataEmitter.RegisterStateMachineEnclosingGenerics reifies the state-machine struct at this ARITY, and self-instantiates the struct with this INSTANTIATION. They used to compute it independently, and the second read only ReceiverType — so a shared async func Fetch[U]() on a generic Holder[T] was reified at arity 2 and then referenced as <Fetch>d__02<!!0>, which the runtime rejects with TypeLoadException ("used with the wrong number of generic arguments"). This is the same StaticOwnerType gap #3932 root C closed on the reification side, still open on the kickoff side; both now route through here, so they cannot drift again. The ITERATOR sibling has always had this property — its kickoff constructs over the very scopeTPs the class was reified from.
member.param: The async kickoff method, or null.
member.returns: The owning type's definition, its type parameters, and the kickoff's own.
