member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.ContainsFixedLengthArray(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary:
Issue #3962: returns true when structurally contains a fixed-length array [N]T.
[N]T is the one G# type whose CLR projection is LOSSY. An is backed by the plain SZ-array T[] — the very same as the slice []T and as an array of every other length — so the declared length lives ONLY in the symbol. Every other structural wrapper's CLR type is injective: a channel's direction selects a different BCL type, a rectangular array's rank is part of its , and seq[T] / map[K,V] / T? / T& / T* each map to a distinct shape.
Gates that decide between "keep the symbolic projection" and "fall back to the CLR shape" must therefore treat a fixed array like symbolically-required content — exactly as does for a named tuple, and for the same reason. Without that, List[[3]int32] and List[[4]int32] both bind to the one cached symbol for List<System.Int32[]> and become the same type.
member.returns: true when a fixed-length array appears at any depth.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.ContainsMetadataRecoveredArray(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary:
Issue #3962: returns true when structurally contains an array that came back through REFLECTION — an whose is an array — rather than as a G#-native [N]T/[]T symbol.
Such an array's length is not merely unread but GONE: metadata records only T[], so no downstream comparison can reconstruct whether the author wrote [3]T, [4]T or []T. A comparison with such a side must therefore stay LENIENT rather than reject on information neither side has — the same line Conversion.AreSameRuntimeChannelElement draws for a metadata-recovered channel element.
member.returns: true when a reflection-recovered array appears at any depth.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.ContainsNamedTupleElement(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #3746 / ADR-0172: returns true when carries tuple element names at any structural position. Like reference nullability, element names are metadata over the positional shape and have no distinct runtime , so any projection that round-trips a type through its CLR silently erases them. Callers that rebuild a type from reflection must consult this and take their symbolic path instead.
member.returns: true when a named tuple appears anywhere in the type.
member.remarks: This deliberately is not folded into ): that predicate also gates 's own CLR backing, and a named tuple must keep its ValueTuple<…> — names never change the runtime type (ADR-0172).

Named tuples share their CLR backing with the unnamed shape, so CLR-driven re-derivation (member projection, imported-call return mapping) erases the names; gates that decide between "keep the symbolic projection" and "fall back to the CLR shape" must treat named-tuple content like symbolically-required content.
member.returns: true when any tuple position declares a name.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.ContainsSameCompilationUserType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #903: returns true when is, or structurally contains, a user-defined type declared in the current compilation that has no CLR backing yet (its is null because the type is still being compiled) — a (struct or class), , , or . Such a type is erased to System.Object (or its CLR ride-through) during reflection-based overload resolution, which loses its symbolic identity. This predicate is the same-compilation sibling of : it lets the binder recognise when a symbolic projection (recovered from a receiver's ) carries information the type-erased closed CLR shape cannot represent, so the projection must be surfaced instead of the erased reflection result. This is what makes List[Check].Single((c) -> c.Id == "x") and List[Check].Select((c) -> c.Id) recover the real Check element type for both the lambda parameter and the call's return type. In-scope generic s (already covered by ) are intentionally excluded here.
member.returns: true if the type references a same-compilation user type without CLR backing.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.ContainsSourceArrayShape(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary:
Issue #4024: returns true when structurally contains EITHER G#-native array spelling — a fixed-length [N]T or a slice []T.
This is the RETENTION predicate, and it is deliberately wider than , which stays the COMPARISON predicate. The one SZ-array CLR type T[] backs []T and [N]T at every length alike, so a generic type argument written in either spelling projects onto the same closed CLR shape. #3962 retained only [N]T, which made List[[3]int32] and List[[4]int32] distinct but left List[[]int32] carrying no symbolic argument at all — and a constructed generic with an EMPTY symbolic argument vector is exactly what a metadata-recovered List<int[]> looks like, so correctly declared the shape unknowable and kept the lenient CLR comparison. Retaining the slice is therefore not an optimisation: it is the only thing that makes a source-spelled []T argument DISTINGUISHABLE from a reflected one, and so comparable against a retained [N]T at all.
Retention alone is a representation change, not a rule change. A has a real, non-null and satisfies neither nor the nested-generic or named-tuple arms of ImportedTypeSymbol.HasSubstitutableTypeArgument, so that property stays false for List[[]T], so the member projection sites that CONSULT it — parameters, indexers, iteration — are untouched, exactly as they were for List[[N]T] after #3962. A method RETURN is the exception, and is the one place retention is observable beyond type identity: GetClrMethodReturnTypeSymbol projects on a nonempty symbolic vector without consulting that property, so Stack[[]T]().Pop() surfaces the retained []T. Deliberate and pinned; see Issue4024SliceTypeArgumentRetentionTests.
member.returns: true when a slice or fixed-length array appears at any depth.

member.summary: Gets the members declared on this type — the Roslyn GetMembers() analogue (ADR-0169). Empty by default; user-defined aggregates surface their fields, properties, methods, and events.
member.returns: The declared members.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.GetWrappedTypes(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #1790: the single canonical enumeration of a wrapper/constructed 's immediate inner type(s) — the element, pointee, key/value, parameter/return, or type-argument slot(s) the composite type structurally carries. Every generic/wrapper kind that can carry another type is listed here exactly once so callers such as recurse uniformly rather than each maintaining its own divergent switch (the class of bug that let several wrapper kinds silently fall through as "no inner type"). Leaf kinds (primitives, same-compilation user types, type parameters) are not wrappers and yield nothing here; their callers handle them directly. Each yielded type is a strict substructure of (types form a DAG built during binding, never a cycle back to themselves), so recursive callers always terminate.
member.returns: The type's immediate inner type(s); empty for a leaf kind.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsByRefLike(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #367: returns true when denotes a by-ref-like (ref struct) type. This covers both imported CLR types such as Span[T], ReadOnlySpan[T], or DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler (detected via System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsByRefLikeAttribute) and user-declared ref struct types () that have no CLR type yet because they are being compiled. These values are stack-only and may not escape to the heap (no boxing, no field of a non-ref-struct, no closure capture, no async/iterator hoisting, and no use as a generic type argument). A wrapper is unwrapped first so Span[T]? is still recognised.
member.returns: true if the type is by-ref-like.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsLegalPointeeType(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: ADR-0122 / issue #1014. Returns whether is a legal pointee for an unmanaged pointer in the supported core subset: a blittable primitive (int8…int64, uint8…uint64, nint/nuint, float32/float64) or another unmanaged pointer (pointer-to-pointer). Pointers to arbitrary managed types are out of scope and rejected by the binder.
member.returns: true when the type is a legal unmanaged pointee.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsSameCompilationUserTypeTopLevel(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Returns true when — after unwrapping nullable, slice and array wrappers — is itself a same-compilation user-defined type (struct/class/enum/interface/delegate with a null ClrType). Unlike , this does NOT recurse into the type arguments of a constructed imported generic: a constructed generic over a user element (e.g. ChannelWriter[Entry]) is NOT a top-level user type, because method/extension lookup on such a non-interned constructed generic is not yet supported (#1305).
member.returns: true if the unwrapped top-level type is a same-compilation user-defined type; otherwise false.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsUnboundGenericDefinition(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: Issue #4095: returns true when denotes a CLR unbound generic definition rather than a construction whose identity depends on an in-scope type parameter.
member.returns: true for a representable unbound generic definition.
member.remarks: Source nested types can be unbound definitions because of generic containing types even when they declare no parameters themselves (Outer[_].Inner). Constructed symbols are excluded by their explicit argument vectors before the containing-type chain is checked.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsUnmanagedPointer(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: ADR-0122 / issue #1014. Returns whether is an unmanaged raw pointer (, CLR ELEMENT_TYPE_PTR).
member.returns: true when the type is an unmanaged pointer.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.IsVoidPointer(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol)
member.summary: ADR-0122 §3 / issue #1033. Returns whether is a true void-element unmanaged pointer (*void, CLR ELEMENT_TYPE_PTR over ELEMENT_TYPE_VOID) — the faithful mapping of C# void*, distinct from the byte pointer *uint8. A *void carries no element type: it may be round-tripped through nint/IntPtr and cast to/from a typed pointer *T, but it may not be directly dereferenced, indexed, or used in pointer arithmetic (those require a cast to a typed pointer first).
member.returns: true when the type is the void-element pointer *void.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeSymbol.StripToBareShape
member.summary:
ADR-0193 Phase 2: the shape a caller that deliberately ignores reference nullability used to get from . It removes a top-level reference ? and platform !, and the carrier, repeatedly, and leaves a value-type Nullable<V> alone.
Dropping the carrier also drops the inner-position flags it holds (List[string?]? becomes List[string]), while inner positions held as nested wrappers survive. That is deliberate for the few Phase 2 callers: each read a signature position erased before, and wants that exact shape (an object member called on an erased type parameter, a boxing target, a method group's inference signature, a lowered local). Nothing that wants nullability should call this. Phase 3's StripReferenceNullability(deep) replaces it with a representation-independent answer.
member.returns: The bare type.

Non-CLR-backed types fall back to the base rendering.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Lexer.ScanInterpolationHole(System.Int32)
member.summary: ADR-0055 delimiter-aware interpolation-hole scanner. Assumes the opening ${ has already been consumed and sits at the first character of the hole body. Advances to the matching top-level } (left un-consumed for the caller), tracking ()[]{} nesting and skipping nested string/char literals (recursively, so an inner interpolation is handled) and // / /* */ comments. Newlines are permitted, so multiline holes are legal. Returns false (after reporting) if the hole is unterminated.
member.param: Source offset of the hole body (for diagnostics).
member.returns: true if the hole closed normally.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Lexer.SkipInterpolationNestedLiteral(System.Char,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Skips a nested string or character literal inside an interpolation hole. Mirrors the real literal lexers: a double-quoted string uses backslash escapes (\") and may itself contain a nested ${ … } interpolation; a single-quoted char literal uses backslash escapes. starts on the opening delimiter.
member.param: Whether a nested double-quoted literal admits interpolation holes.
member.returns: false when a nested interpolation hole exceeded the nesting limit (issue #1602), so the caller must abandon its own scan; true otherwise.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.IsInLeftNestingPosition(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when sits in a LEFT-nesting chain position — the receiver-so-far of an ordinary iterative postfix step (Accessor.LeftPart, Index.Target, Call.Callee). Excludes Accessor.RightPart on purpose: being the right-hand side of a dot means a dot REACHED this node, not that anything follows it.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.IsNullConditionalHop(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when is one null-conditional operator — the G# counterpart of one Roslyn ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax.
member.returns: True for an or with IsNullConditional set.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.NextNullConditionalHop(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: The next null-conditional hop reached after when the whole chain is read left to right — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's WhenNotNull is ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax (a further ?./?[ later in the same chain, possibly past intervening ordinary ./[ steps). Because G#'s dotted continuations nest through RightPart (a later operator is a DESCENDANT, not an ancestor — see the type-level remarks), this is a left-to-right scan of the chain's hops, not a parent walk.
member.returns: The next hop in source order, or null when is last.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.NullConditionalOperatorToken(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: The G# token spelling 's null-conditional operator — ?. or ?[, a single fused token, wider than Roslyn's bare ? OperatorToken.
member.returns: The ?./?[ token.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.NullConditionalReceiver(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary:
The immediate receiver of one hop ( / ) — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax.Expression.
Exact only for the FIRST hop of a chain (there, it is the genuine, independently-evaluated receiver — see ExpressionBinder.Access.Accessor.cs's BindNullConditionalAccessExpression, which binds syntax.LeftPart as a standalone expression). For a LATER hop in the same chain, G# reuses the same LeftPart slot to hold just the next member NAME (the binder threads the real receiver value through a synthetic capture instead, with no syntax node of its own) — value-equivalent to what Roslyn's receiverless MemberBindingExpressionSyntax/ElementBindingExpressionSyntax denotes there, but not extent- or lifted-type-exact. Callers that read a LOCATION off this (I3a) get the Roslyn-exact span from ) instead.
member.returns: The hop's receiver expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.ReceiverBounds(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.ExpressionSyntax)
member.summary: The shared start-of-span computation for ) and ): the first hop in the chain keeps its natural start; every later hop starts right after the PREVIOUS hop's own ?, skipping the character that belongs to the enclosing operator rather than to this receiverless position.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.ReceiverIsElementBinding(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when 's receiver is itself a null-conditional element-access hop — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's Expression is ElementBindingExpressionSyntax. Unlike the member-binding checks above, [/?[ nests the ordinary (left/iterative) way, so a preceding index hop shows up directly as ), not as a parent.
member.returns: True when the hop continues directly off a preceding ?[…].

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.ReceiverIsMemberBinding(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when 's receiver is itself the PLAIN name half of an immediately preceding ?. — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's Expression is MemberBindingExpressionSyntax. Because dotted continuations nest via RightPart, this is a check of 's PARENT (the dot that produced this hop's name), not of )'s shape.
member.returns: True when the hop continues directly off a preceding ?. with no ordinary step in between.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.ReceiverIsPlainMemberAccess(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when 's receiver is itself the plain name half of an immediately preceding ORDINARY (non-null-conditional) . — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's Expression is MemberAccessExpressionSyntax.
member.returns: True when the hop continues directly off a preceding ordinary ..

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.ReceiverSpan(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: The Roslyn-exact span of 's corresponding ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax.Expression: for the first hop, its own natural receiver span; for a later hop, the span starting right after the previous hop's ? and ending right before this hop's own ? — Roslyn's receiverless binding shape, with no leading ? of its own.
member.returns: The hop's Roslyn-exact receiver span.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.TailIsElementBinding(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary:
True when is the LAST operator of its chain and is an element access — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's WhenNotNull is ElementBindingExpressionSyntax.
Unlike ) this cannot be read off alone: [/?[ nests the ORDINARY (left/iterative) way, so a FURTHER step after an index hop shows up as that index sitting in a chain-extending PARENT's LeftPart/Target/Callee — being wrapped as a parent's RightPart does not disqualify it (that parent is simply the dot that reached this index, not a further step past it).
member.returns: True for a terminal ?[…] hop.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.TailIsMemberBinding(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: True when is the LAST operator of its chain and ends directly in a plain member name — the G# counterpart of Roslyn's WhenNotNull is MemberBindingExpressionSyntax.
member.returns: True for a terminal ?.name hop.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.TryGetChainExtendingParent(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode@)
member.summary: The parent node that extends the SAME postfix chain participates in, whichever way that particular link nests (Accessor.LeftPart OR .RightPart, Index.Target, Call.Callee), plus the totality case: -> desugars p->m into Accessor(Unary(*, p), arrowToken, m), so a node just before an arrow has its real chain-extending parent TWO levels up, past the synthesized dereference. Reachable from a real ?. chain (a?.b->m) even though no C#-sourced analyzer can produce it (-> is a G#-only construct).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain.WhenNotNullSpan(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: The Roslyn-exact span of 's corresponding ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax.WhenNotNull: right after this hop's own ? through the end of the whole chain.
member.returns: The hop's Roslyn-exact WhenNotNull span.

member.summary: ADR-0126 / issue #1027 / #4350: pointer dereferences and ref-returning calls use the indirect compound path. Bare names and setter-based members/indexers/maps retain their established compound paths, whose binders distinguish storage from properties and capture the exact postfix value.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.CanStartExpression(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: Issue #490: returns true when can plausibly begin an expression — used by to disambiguate the contextual ref modifier from an identifier expression named ref.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.CanStartTypeClause(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: Returns true when can start a TypeClauseSyntax. Shared by parser lookaheads so every type-clause entry point uses the same complete head-token set.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.FunctionModifierRunEndsInFunc(System.Int32)
member.summary: ADR-0192: scans the run of func-member modifiers starting at — partial (ADR-0192), unsafe (ADR-0122), and the colour modifiers async/suspend (ADR-0023 / ADR-0174 D4), each at most once and in any order — and reports whether the run terminates in func. The existing probes for those modifiers used to hard-code Peek(n) == func, which is why they must route through this helper now: partial may sit between them and the keyword. The scan does not consume tokens.
member.param: The lookahead offset to start scanning at.
member.returns: true when the modifier run ends in func.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsAdditionalConstraintStart(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: ADR-0097 / issue #775 (constraint keyword renamed to init() by issue #997): returns true when begins a flag-style constraint (class, struct, or init(). These are handled in a dedicated post-loop after the legacy single-identifier constraint slot is parsed (any, comparable, or a sealed-interface name).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsAsyncVoidResultEnvelope(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.TypeClauseSyntax)
member.summary: Issue #3907: whether an async function's return-type clause names the void-result await envelope — a bare Task or ValueTask with no type arguments — so an arrow body is an expression statement rather than a return.
member.param: The async modifier token, if present.
member.returns: Whether the arrow body should lower to an expression statement.
member.remarks: The test is deliberately syntactic and deliberately narrow: only async declarations are considered, only the two envelope names issue #1918 recognises, and only the unqualified, non-generic, non-nullable spelling. Task[T] / ValueTask[T] carry a result and keep their return; a nullable or qualified spelling is left alone rather than guessed at. A non-async function named the same way really does return a task value, so it is untouched.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsCastIntrinsicHead
member.summary: ADR-0167: cast is reserved in call position, and cast[T](x) binds as the conversion intrinsic whatever T is. Its bracket is a conversion target, not a CLR generic instantiation, so pointer and function-pointer targets are legal there (issue #4938).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsCurrentOnNewLineAfter(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: ADR-0122 / issue #1014: returns whether begins on a later source line than the end of . Used to treat a leading-* token as a pointer-dereference statement boundary rather than a multiplication continuation.
member.param: The expression parsed so far on the current line.
member.returns: true when the current token is on a new line.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsFunctionColorModifier(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxKind)
member.summary: ADR-0174 D4: async and suspend share the function-color modifier slot before func.
member.returns: true for either modifier keyword.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsFunctionPointerTypeHead(System.Int32)
member.summary: ADR-0095 §6: unmanaged is a contextual keyword that heads a raw function-pointer type clause (unmanaged[CC, …] (T, …) -> R, or the platform-default unmanaged (T, …) -> R) only when the next token is [ or (. This is the single head test for that production: the real type-clause parser, its array-element dispatch, the tuple-element-name look-aheads and the speculative scanner (TryScanTypeClauseCore) all ask it, so they cannot disagree about where a function-pointer type starts (issue #4938).
member.param: The token offset, relative to Current, of the candidate unmanaged token.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.IsInterfaceMethodSignatureStart
member.summary:
ADR-0090 / issue #756: returns true if the current token starts an interface (instance) method signature. The recognised starts are:
func
private func (private instance helper)
Static-virtual members (ADR-0089) and static private helpers (ADR-0090) are declared inside a shared { … } block on the interface (issue #865 revision); the static contextual keyword is no longer recognised on interface members.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.LooksLikeTupleElementName(System.Int32)
member.summary: ADR-0172: decides whether the identifier at the current position is a tuple-element NAME (followed by a token that can start a type clause) rather than the element type itself. identifier identifier is always name + type (two consecutive identifiers never form a type), and the [ case distinguishes an array/slice/rectangular element type (name []T, name [3]T, name [,]T) from a generic type-argument list on the identifier itself (List[int32]). The unmanaged function-pointer head keeps its ADR-0095 meaning.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.LooksLikeYieldTupleLiteral(System.Int32)
member.summary: Issue #813: lookahead helper for the contextual yield at statement start. Returns true when the token at is a ( that opens a value-tuple literal (i.e. its matching ) follows a top-level ,). A tuple-literal yield like yield (a, b) must be parsed as a yield-statement; without this disambiguation the existing rule rejected every yield ( form because it treats parens as the start of a function-call expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.MatchQualifiedTypeName
member.summary: Issue #296: matches a base-type name that may be fully qualified (e.g. System.IO.MemoryStream). The dotted segments are folded into a single whose text is the dotted name, so the binder resolves it via the imported/alias-aware type resolution path. A bare identifier (e.g. MemoryStream) is returned unchanged.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseAggregateDeclaration(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: ADR-0078 / issue #718: parses an aggregate declaration whose head is [open|sealed]? [data]? [inline]? [ref]? (class|struct|enum|interface) Name[TParams]? ... The accessibility modifier was already consumed in . Issue #1602: depth-guarded — nested type declarations (class A { class B { … } }) recurse through this method.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseAnnotation
member.summary: Parses a single annotation: @ [target-kind :] dotted-name [( arguments )]. Pre: Current.Kind == AtToken.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseAnnotations
member.summary: Parses zero or more Kotlin-style annotations (ADR-0047) at the current position. Stops at the first token that is not @. The returned list is empty when no annotation lead-in is present.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseArmOperand
member.summary: Parses the operand that sits immediately before a select arm's body brace. Issue #1023's defect in another position: a call- or indexer-tailed operand (case ch <- Pair(41) { … }) would otherwise read the arm's { as its own object initializer and swallow the body. Bare struct literals are suppressed for the same reason and by the same rule as a statement header's (issue #1575): an empty { } body after a name operand — case <-ch { } — is a body, not an empty struct literal.
member.returns: The parsed operand.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseBaseInterfaceCallExpression
member.summary: ADR-0091 / issue #757: parses an explicit-base interface call base[IFoo].Method(args). Commit is decided by the caller in when the current identifier is the contextual base keyword and the next token is [. The optional generic type-argument list on the method identifier is parsed but is rejected by the binder in this PR (reserved for a future explicit-base generic-method extension).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseCompilationUnit
member.summary: Creates a compilation unit by parsing the members as read in the source text. Issue #1602: mirrors Roslyn's ParseWithStackGuard — when the recursion guard (see ) detects input nested beyond (or the thread's remaining execution stack), the parse is abandoned wholesale, GS0417 is reported, and a minimal (empty) compilation unit is returned, so the parse always terminates normally with diagnostics instead of killing the process with an uncatchable .
member.returns: A compilation unit.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseConstructorDeclaration(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: Issue #306: parses a standalone user-defined constructor init(params) [: base(args)] { body } inside a class or plain-struct body. ADR-0065 §2: accepts an optional leading convenience contextual modifier passed in by the caller.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseDeinitDeclaration
member.summary: ADR-0068 / issue #698: parses a class-body destructor declaration deinit { body }. The keyword carries no parameters, no return type, no accessibility modifier. A malformed parameter list (the user wrote deinit(...)) is consumed and diagnosed so the parser can still locate the body block and recover.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseDelegateDeclaration(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: Issue #3510: parses the canonical named delegate declaration delegate Name[TParams]?(params) ReturnType? ;. The required trailing semicolon terminates the optional return-type clause — the retired type Name = delegate func(...) spelling had no terminator, so a void delegate greedily consumed whatever declaration followed it.
member.returns: The parsed delegate declaration.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseDottedTypeNameTail
member.summary: Issue #526 / #1506: consumes the tail of a dotted type-clause name, starting immediately after the first (already-consumed) identifier. Each segment may carry its own optional [ T1, ... ] type-argument list, generalizing Outer[T].Inner, A[T].B[U].C, and the legacy single-trailing-list forms. The last segment's type-argument list is returned via the Trailing* fields (matching the historical representation); every earlier (outer) segment's list is returned via the OuterSegment* arrays, aligned to the segment sequence. Lookahead-only on . IDENT so a member access on a value-typed identifier is never miscounted as a qualifier.
member.returns: The decomposed dotted-name tail.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseFileLevelAttributes
member.summary: Parses a leading run of file-level @assembly:Name(...) and @module:Name(...) annotations, sitting after imports and before the first member. This is the producer-side opt-in surface for assembly-scoped custom attributes (chiefly @assembly:InternalsVisibleTo("Foo.Tests") — see ADR-0047 §2/§7 and issue #1929/#1953). Only annotations that explicitly carry an assembly: or module: use-site target are consumed here; anything else is left for to attach to the next declaration as usual.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseFunctionPointerTypeClause
member.summary: ADR-0095 / issue #761: parses the raw function-pointer type clause unmanaged[CC, ...] (T1, T2, ...) -> R. The leading unmanaged identifier is the contextual keyword; the [CC] slot is optional (ADR-0095 v2 / issue #3611 — bare unmanaged (T) -> R is the platform-default unmanaged convention) and accepts a comma-separated convention list. The parameter and return type-clause grammar is the same as the arrow-form function type clause (ADR-0075).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseGenericCallExpression(System.Boolean)
member.param: Whether this is the reserved cast[T] intrinsic (see ), whose target may be a pointer or a function pointer when it is called.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseIfHeader
member.summary: Parses the header after if, ( SimpleStmt ";" )? Expression. The if-statement and the if-expression both call it (issue #4962, ADR-0064), so the two forms accept the same initializer and parse the condition the same way.
member.returns: The optional initializer, the ; that ends it, and the condition.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseIfLetElseBranch
member.summary: Parses the branch after else: a chained else if / else if let, or a plain block expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseIfLetExpression
member.summary: Parses the depth-guarded value-position form (ADR-0151 / ADR-0201).
member.returns: The complete expression, retaining a missing else for GS0276.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseIfLetHeader(System.String)
member.summary: ADR-0201: every binding form uses the ordinary expression grammar with a top-level logical-operator boundary for each initializer.
member.param: The form to name in GS0625, or null for if let.
member.returns: The bindings, optional guard operator and guard.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseInterfaceMethodSignatureCore(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: Parses the shared body of an interface method signature (the part from func onward), shared by the instance path () and the static-virtual path inside an interface shared { … } block (). When is non-null the resulting function is marked as a static-virtual interface member (ADR-0089); the binder reads .

Issue #865 revision (ADR-0089): parses a shared { … } block on an interface. Each member is a func (optionally private) and becomes a static-virtual interface member — abstract when the body is omitted, default when present (body-vs-no-body discriminator, mirroring the instance DIM path). The parsed functions are appended to with set to the shared keyword token, so the binder routes them into InterfaceSymbol.StaticMethods / InterfaceSymbol.StaticPrivateMethods via the existing check. Non-func members are rejected with GS0330 (interface static state is not supported).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseLabeledTupleLiteral(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken)
member.summary: ADR-0172: parses a tuple literal whose FIRST element is labeled — (line: 1, column: 2) — reached when the token after the opening paren is identifier :. A lone labeled element (x: 1) is an error (grouping parens take no label, and there are no 1-tuples); it reports GS0543 and recovers as a plain parenthesized expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseManagedFunctionPointerTypeClause
member.summary: ADR-0122 §9 / issue #1035: parses the *managed* function-pointer type clause *func(T1, T2, ...) R. The leading * mirrors the *T pointer prefix and the func(...) R body mirrors the named function-type spelling; the return type is optional (void when absent). The result is a managed function pointer callable directly via calli with the default managed calling convention.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseNameOrCallExpression(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.param: Whether this parses the member name after ., ?. or ->. A member named cast is an ordinary member, never the reserved cast[T](x) intrinsic.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseOptionalSegmentTypeArguments(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SeparatedSyntaxList{GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.TypeClauseSyntax}@,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@)
member.summary: Parses an optional type-argument list [ T1, T2, ... ] in type position (issue #1506). Leaves the parser unchanged and emits all-null outputs when the current token does not open a list.

ADR-0078: parses the body of a class or struct declaration whose modifiers, aggregate keyword, and identifier have already been consumed by . Delegates into the shared body parser by passing the aggregate keyword as preconsumed.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ParseTupleLiteralElement
member.summary: ADR-0172: parses one tuple-literal element — an optional name : label followed by the element expression.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.PartialModifierIntroducesFunc
member.summary: ADR-0192: returns true when the current token is the contextual partial identifier and the modifier run it starts terminates in func. unsafe (ADR-0122) and the function colour modifiers async/suspend (ADR-0023/ADR-0174) may appear between partial and func in either order, so all of partial func, partial async func, partial unsafe async func are recognised. The scan does not consume tokens.
member.returns: true when partial heads a func member.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ReportAbstractAndSharedOnlyValidOnClass(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxKind)
member.summary: ADR-0195 / issue #4674: abstract and shared describe a class (an uninstantiable or all-shared reference type), so a struct, enum or interface head that carries either is an unexpected token, recovered like the other misplaced modifiers.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.ReportAndRecoverLegacyAggregateForm(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.TypeParameterListSyntax)
member.summary: ADR-0078 / issue #718: emit GS0306 (or GS0307 for record) on a legacy aggregate declaration head (type Name [mods]? <kind> ...) and recover by consuming the modifier/keyword/body sequence as if the declaration had been written in the new grammar. The recovered syntax node feeds the rest of the pipeline so that downstream tests see one high-quality diagnostic instead of a cascade.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.SkipPartialBearingModifierRun(System.Int32)
member.summary:
ADR-0192: advances past a modifier run that contains a partial token, so an accessibility lookahead can see the member keyword (func, prop, event, …) that actually follows it. Without this, public partial prop P … left public unconsumed — the lookahead stopped on partial, matched nothing, and the misplaced-modifier rejection path that issues GS0607 was never reached, so the user got a field-declaration cascade instead of the one intended diagnostic.
Deliberately returns UNCHANGED when the run contains no partial: a run of unsafe/colour modifiers alone must keep resolving exactly as it did before ADR-0192, so this helper can never alter a pre-existing lookahead decision.
member.param: The lookahead offset to scan from.
member.returns: The offset past the run, or the original offset when it holds no partial.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.SplitQuestionOpenBracketToken
member.summary: Issue #1351: replaces the current fused ?[ () with two distinct tokens — a ? () followed by a [ () — at the current parse position. The lexer fuses these for null-conditional indexing (a?[i]); in a nullable-array type clause whose element is itself an array ([]?[]T) they must be parsed separately.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryConsumeFunctionModifierRun(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@,GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@)
member.summary: ADR-0192 / issue #4301: consumes the complete run of func-member modifiers at the current token — partial, unsafe, and one colour modifier (async/suspend) — in any order, but only when that run terminates in func. This is the single consumer every call site routes through. The earlier shape probed for each modifier in a fixed sequence, which could not match an ordering that placed partial BETWEEN the colour modifier and unsafe (async partial unsafe func, unsafe partial async func): the fixed probe consumed one modifier, skipped past the slot the next one actually occupied, and left a stray token where func was expected — cascading into recovery. A single order-independent loop is the only way to keep the any-order contract ADR-0192 §A advertises without every call site re-deriving it. Consumes nothing and returns false when the run does not end in func, so each caller's pre-ADR-0192 error-recovery path still sees exactly the tokens it used to.
member.param: Receives the partial token, if present.
Receives the unsafe token, if present.
Receives the async/suspend token, if present.
member.returns: true when the modifier run was consumed.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryConsumeInterfacePrivateBeforePartial
member.summary: ADR-0192 / issue #4301 (Copilot review round 4): an interface method signature's only legal accessibility modifier is private (ADR-0090), and it must be consumed before probing for a misplaced partial — otherwise private partial func F(); left private for , whose lookahead requires func immediately after private. That lookahead fails with partial in between, so the loop fell through to an "unexpected token" diagnostic for private BEFORE the partial probe on the same member ever ran, producing two diagnostics instead of the intended single GS0607. Mirrors the class/struct member loop's own accessibility lookahead, which already skips a partial-bearing run via for the same reason.
member.returns: The consumed private token, or null when none is consumed.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryConsumePartialFuncModifier(GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken@)
member.summary: ADR-0192 / issue #4301: probes for the contextual partial modifier at member position and consumes it when it heads a func member. partial stays an ordinary identifier everywhere else (var partial = 1, func partial()) — it is only special when the modifier run it starts terminates in func, exactly as ADR-0144 made it special only when the run terminates in an aggregate keyword.
member.param: Receives the consumed token, or null.
member.returns: true when a partial modifier was consumed.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryDetectAggregateDeclarationHead
member.summary: ADR-0078 / issue #718: detects whether the current parser position begins a Kotlin/Swift-style aggregate declaration head — optionally preceded by modifiers (open, sealed, data, inline, ref) — by scanning ahead to see if it terminates in one of class, struct, enum, or interface. The scan does not consume tokens. Returning false leaves dispatch to the legacy type-keyword path (which now only handles type aliases and named delegates).

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryDetectAggregateDeclarationHead(System.Int32)
member.summary: Issue #910: offset-aware variant of ) used by the class/struct body member loop to recognise a nested type declaration head that may be preceded by an accessibility modifier (already peeked at ). The scan does not consume tokens.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.TryRejectMisplacedPartialModifier
member.summary: ADR-0192 / issue #4301: consumes a partial token that sits at member position but heads neither a func (ADR-0192) nor an aggregate declaration (ADR-0144) — for example partial prop, partial event, or partial var — and reports GS0607. Doing this here keeps the token out of ParseFieldDeclaration, which would otherwise surface a misleading "expected type clause" cascade.

member.name: M:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.ComputeSpan(System.Int32)
member.summary: Computes and caches the span of this node. The span is the minimum start and the maximum end over all children. Children can overlap even in source order: an interpolated string token contains its holes, and the parser synthesizes tokens at the position of a real one (issue #5185). The first and last child would give a truncated span and break position-based walks such as the language server's interpolated-string hole detection (issue #5136). The walk reads the children in property order, so it does not need the sorted children, which need the spans of the children (issue #5185). A node whose class overrides is asked for its span and never derived from its children.
member.param: The number of nested calls so far.
member.returns: The span.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.FunctionContainsUserGotoOrLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the CURRENT function/lambda/ local-function body contains any user-written goto statement or non-loop label: declaration (issue #4285), computed syntactically, once, before that body is bound — see . Consulted by to conservatively suppress the early-exit / post-switch narrowing lift for the whole body whenever it holds: a goto anywhere in the function can jump directly into a region a nil-guard's implicit exit was assumed to dominate, bypassing the guard and invalidating the narrowing's soundness proof. Fresh per function/lambda/local-function, matching 's scoping — reset and recomputed by LambdaBinder.EnterNestedFrame for a nested function-literal or arrow-lambda body, and restored by LambdaBinder.RestoreNestedFrame.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.InConstructorInitializer
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether constructor-initializer arguments are being bound.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.InUnsafeContext
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether binding is currently inside an unsafe context (ADR-0122 / issue #1014). When true the prefix *T type clause binds to an unmanaged pointer () and raw-pointer operations are permitted.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.InitialScope
member.summary: Gets the binder's initial scope. Unlike , this remains stable while nested statement binding pushes child scopes.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.IsCheckedContext
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the current checked/unchecked arithmetic context is checked (issue #1881): true inside a checked(...) expression or a checked { } statement, false inside unchecked(...)/unchecked { } or when no such context has been entered (the C# project default is unchecked). Innermost context wins — saves and restores the previous value, so nesting checked { unchecked { … } } resolves correctly. Only observed by the Sum/Difference/Product binary operator and by narrowing numeric conversions.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.LoopStack
member.summary: Gets the stack of (label-name, break-label, continue-label) tuples maintained for loop bodies during binding. The LabelName element is null for unlabeled loops; ADR-0070 labeled break / continue resolve their target by scanning this stack for a matching label name.
member.remarks: Issue #3501 A3: a switch statement also pushes a frame so an unlabeled break in an arm exits the switch (C#/Go alignment). A switch frame has a null ContinueLabel and a null LabelName — continue binding skips such frames to reach the enclosing loop.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.NarrowedVariables
member.summary: Gets the stack of per-scope variable-narrowing tables used by pattern matching and flow analysis. Each entry maps a variable to its narrowed type within the corresponding scope.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PatternVariableNames
member.summary: Gets the names of every ADR-0166 pattern variable bound in this binder's body. An unresolved name that matches one is reported as a pattern variable read outside the region its match dominates (GS0532) rather than as an unknown variable.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PendingEarlyExitFrames
member.summary: Gets the side-table that parks the else-branch narrowing frame of an if-statement keyed by the resulting bound node identity. ADR-0069 / issue #700: BindBlockStatements consults this table and lifts the frame into the enclosing block's persistent narrowing scope when the then-branch ends in an unconditional exit (return, throw, break, continue), so subsequent reads in the block see the narrowing.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PendingGotoAssignmentStarts
member.summary: Gets the assignment-narrowing generation at which each unresolved forward-goto target was first encountered.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PendingGotoNarrowingSnapshots
member.summary: Gets the variables known non-null at each forward goto source, grouped by target label. Label joins retain a later assignment narrowing when every incoming jump already carried that proof.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PendingPatternVariableLeaks
member.summary: Gets the ADR-0166 side-table that parks the pattern variables an if-statement leaks into the statements that follow it, keyed by the resulting . BindIfStatement records the condition's when-false variables when the then-branch ends in an unconditional exit (and the when-true variables when the else- branch does); BindBlockStatements declares them into the enclosing block scope, the same lift performs for smart-cast narrowings.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.PendingSwitchExitFrames
member.summary: Gets the side-table that parks the post-switch narrowing frame for a switch statement keyed by the resulting bound node identity. ADR-0069 addendum / issue #712: when every non-default arm either ends in an unconditional exit OR contributes the same narrowing on the discriminator (and the default arm, if any, does likewise), the common narrowing is lifted into the enclosing block's persistent narrowing scope so subsequent reads in the block see the narrowing.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext.References

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCallOperationExpression.Arguments
member.summary: Gets the arguments, in source order.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCallOperationExpression.CalledFunction
member.summary: Gets the symbol of the called method — the Roslyn IInvocationOperation.TargetMethod analogue. Typed as : a same-compilation callee is a and an imported one an , and and — the members the Roslyn call-site surface maps onto — are meaningful on both.
member.remarks:
Deliberately NOT a richer callee type. The two other members a migrated analyzer reaches through TargetMethod cannot be answered from this symbol honestly (PR #3968 review):
ReturnType — the callee symbol carries the DECLARATION's return type, so a constructed generic
call reports T where the call site produces int32. cs2gs maps TargetMethod.ReturnType to the call node's own , which is the constructed type.
OverriddenMethod — an imported callee has no override chain in G#, so exposing it here would
answer null for every call into metadata. A member that silently returns null for the common case is worse than an absent one, because analyzers branch on it; it is absent, and cs2gs reports reaching it as a gap.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCallOperationExpression.MemberGroup

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the handler only records the exception for a finally that is guaranteed to rethrow it, so control never completes the handler normally. The binder sets this on the catch it synthesizes for a scope block (ADR-0174 D6: ScopeFrame.Exit always throws when handed a body exception); control-flow analysis treats such a handler as terminating, so return inside the scope body still satisfies "all paths return".

A filter is emitted as a real CLR filter region: it runs in the first pass, before any intervening finally, and a false result declines the clause and continues the search with the next sibling handler.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundFunctionLiteralExpression.CapturedVariables
member.summary: Gets the set of outer variables this literal reads or writes. The setter is internal: issue #4221's transitive-capture reconciliation () widens this set after initial binding when a generic local function calls a sibling that itself captures outer state, so the caller's synthesized environment ends up with a field for every variable any callee it directly invokes will need at the call site.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundFunctionLiteralExpression.EnclosingTypeParameterDiagnosticReported

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundFunctionLiteralExpression.EnclosingTypeParameterOffender
member.summary: Gets or sets the enclosing method/type type parameter this GENERIC local-function literal (let Name[T, ...] = func ...) referenced in its own signature, an own type-parameter constraint, or its body, cached at the literal's own bind time (see ). Null for every literal outside that gate's scope. Issue #4223/#4221 merge follow-up: the gate rejects this combination only when the literal ALSO captures outer state (issue #4221/#4252's capturing generic-local-function path has not been extended to carry an extra enclosing type parameter the way the zero-capture path has); but can be widened AFTER that initial check, by , for a forward reference to, or a call cycle with, a sibling that captures outer state. Caching the offender here lets that later widening re-evaluate the exclusion instead of silently letting an unsupported shape reach the emitter.

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this element load reads real, addressable array storage (issue #3292). Fixed arrays ([N]T), slices ([]T, ADR-0016: CLR-array-backed), and imported CLR single-dimensional arrays all store their elements in a heap array whose element address is expressible in IL (ldelema), so a struct member write through the element can mutate it in place. member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundUnaryExpression.PlatformCheckMessage
member.summary:
Gets ADR-0186 §4's runtime-check message, or null for a user-written !!.
A non-null value marks this node as the check the compiler inserted at a T! -> T coercion. The distinction is observable in two places and nowhere else: the emitter selects the NullReferenceException(string) constructor instead of the parameterless one, and --platform-nil-checks=off suppresses insertion of these nodes while leaving every user-written !! exactly as it is.
There is no third consumer, and an earlier draft of this comment wrongly claimed one: G# has no separate expression interpreter — Interpreter.Tests drives emitted IL — so the emitter is the only thing that reads this.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundUserInstanceCallExpression.ConstrainedReceiverTypeParameter
member.summary: Gets the type parameter whose user-declared interface constraint backs this call when it dispatches through a constraint (issue #1052), e.g. x.Area() where x : T and T : IShape. The emitter then produces a verifiable constrained. !!T callvirt IShape::Area() sequence instead of a bare callvirt on the unboxed type parameter. Null for ordinary user-instance calls.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundUserInstanceCallExpression.MethodTypeArguments
member.summary: Gets the call-site (explicit or inferred) method type arguments for a generic instance method call, positionally aligned with on , or a default (empty) array for a non-generic method. Issue #1931: bind time already resolves this substitution (from an explicit [T] list or argument-type inference) to convert arguments/return type, but that substitution was previously discarded once bound whenever it did not affect the return type — forcing the emitter to blindly re-derive the method type arguments via structural unification over the (possibly uninformative, e.g. a bare nil) argument expressions, which can fail even though the call was validly bound. Stashing the resolved arguments here lets the emitter use the authoritative bind-time result directly.

When non-null, no IL local slot is allocated and the value is inlined at every read site, with a LocalConstant row emitted in the Portable PDB.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Conversion.RequiresPlatformNilCheck
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this conversion carries a platform value (T!) into a destination whose declared type is a non-null reference type, so ADR-0186 §4's runtime nil check must be inserted at the coercion point. The flag exists because ADR-0186 §4's rule is stated over the destination's nullability, not over the literal type T: T! → T, T! → object, T! → BaseClass and T! → ISomeInterface are all such destinations and all check, while T! → T?, T! → object? and T! → U! are not and do not. Classification is the only place that distinction is available as a single fact, so it is recorded here rather than re-derived at each of BindConversion's callers — which is precisely the per-site-predicate shape ADR-0186 exists to remove.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.OverloadResolution.OverloadResolver.MapClrType
member.summary: Gets the same CLR-arg cross-reflection-context (MLC) projector threaded through the emit-time Construct call sites ()). Both Construct call sites in this file build a same-compilation user type (classType is always a source-declared resolved by name in this scope, never an imported CLR generic), so under normal binding the raw ClrType args are already in this compilation's reflection context and no projection is needed. Threaded anyway for defense-in-depth / consistency with the other Construct sites touched by #2037, and to cover a future imported-generic-arg path without another audit.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.AssemblyName
member.summary: Gets or sets the assembly-identity override (e.g. from MSBuild's AssemblyName or the SDK). Setting this immediately pushes the value onto 's so binding-time internal-visibility checks () see the correct consumer name regardless of whether the caller reads / before or after calling Emit. Previously this was only set inside Emit, so any earlier access to the lazy (which caches per-consumer-assembly visibility, see ImportedTypeSymbol.AggregateCache) would freeze visibility with an empty assembly name. Callers that know the target assembly name up front (the gsc CLI, the language server) should set this before touching or .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.BoundProgram
member.summary: Gets the fully-bound program — all function/method bodies and top-level statements, plus any diagnostics surfaced during binding.
member.remarks: Like this is lazily computed and cached on the compilation. is a pure function of and ; because both are immutable on a given instance, the cache invalidates naturally whenever a new is constructed (e.g. when the language server replaces its cached compilation after a file edit). Hot paths such as the language server's per-keystroke diagnostics, hover, definition, and semantic-token requests should reuse this cached instance rather than re-invoking ), which can take hundreds of milliseconds on projects with large reference graphs.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether an implicit import System should be seeded before user imports are processed. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.IncrementalBodyReuse
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this compilation chain keeps a body cache so that successors built by reuse unchanged member bodies (ADR-0105, ADR-0212). Defaults to false, which is the batch path: no cache, no reuse. Set it before the first query, like every other option. A successor copies the flag and shares the cache of its predecessor; never does.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.PreprocessorSymbols
member.summary: Gets or sets the active preprocessor symbol set used by [Conditional("SYMBOL")] call-site elision (ADR-0047 §6 / issue #176). A call to a function marked [Conditional("SYMBOL")] is elided when *none* of the named symbols is in this set; if any named symbol is present, the call is emitted normally. Defaults to — equivalent to "no preprocessor symbols defined" — so conditional methods are elided by default unless the embedder opts in. Setting null is normalised to the empty set.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.RecordMemberGroups
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the body bind records the candidates of each call, for (ADR-0212 slice S4). Set it before the compilation binds; changing it afterwards throws, because bound bodies are reused. Only a compilation made for the semantic model or the language server sets it; gsc leaves it off so that recording costs a compile nothing.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.ReusedGlobalScope
member.summary: Gets or sets a pre-bound to reuse instead of re-binding from the syntax trees (ADR-0105 Phase 2). Only sets it, after it has re-pointed the edited file's symbols at the new syntax. Internal for tests (ADR-0212 §9).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.Compilation.Submission
member.summary: Gets or sets the interactive submission options (ADR-0156 Phase 2). When set, the compilation binds as one REPL submission: prior submissions' functions, globals, and types resolve as metadata-backed imports over their emitted assemblies, syntax trees without a package declaration fall into the submission's own package, session imports are replayed, and the trailing expression value is captured into the synthesized global for the cell echo. Defaults to null (ordinary compilation).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.EmitDiagnosticException.DiagnosticId
member.summary: Gets the diagnostic id this failure should be reported as, or null to fall back to GS9998. Issue #3755: an emit-time well-known member the target framework does not declare is a condition of the user's reference closure, not a compiler bug, so it must not be dressed up as an internal error. The emit pipeline has no DiagnosticBag in scope (see MethodBodyEmitter.Expressions.cs), so the existing exception channel carries the id instead of a new sink being threaded through it.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataTokenCache.NullableOpenCtorMemberRefs
member.summary: Gets the cache mapping an open type parameter T (constrained to struct) to the for System.Nullable1<!!T>::.ctor(!0) (issue #814 / ADR-0084 §L5). The parent TypeSpec uses the same VAR/MVAR slot as the wrapping method's signature, so a single MemberRef per T serves every instantiation of the enclosing generic method or type. Issue #3163: the parent TypeSpec is encoded through EncodeTypeSymbol, whose VAR/MVAR ordinal depends on the active generic remaps, so the key includes the (cref:RemapScope).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataTokenCache.NullableUserEnumCtorMemberRefs
member.summary: Gets the cache mapping a user-defined to the for System.Nullable1<E>::.ctor(!0) (issue #1298). The parent TypeSpec closes Nullable<> over the enum's emitted TypeDef, so one MemberRef per enum serves every E -> E? lift site. Issue #3163: a nested enum's parent TypeSpec can encode enclosing type-parameter ordinals, so the key includes the (cref:RemapScope).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataTokenCache.NullableUserStructCtorMemberRefs
member.summary: Gets the cache mapping a symbolic value-type underlying to the for System.Nullable1<T>::.ctor(!0). The parent TypeSpec closes Nullable<> over the encoded underlying, so one MemberRef serves every matching nullable lift site. Issue #3163: the symbolic underlying can encode type-parameter ordinals, so the key includes the (cref:RemapScope).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataTokenCache.NullableUserValueTypeGetHasValueMemberRefs
member.summary: Gets the cache mapping a user-defined value-type underlying ( or value-kind ) to the for System.Nullable1<T>::get_HasValue() (issue #2388). Mirrors (cref:NullableUserValueTypeGetValueMemberRefs); used to HasValue-branch a nullable-lifted Stream C/D custom-operator call over a same-compilation struct, where no real CLR (cref:System.Type) exists to drive the reflection-based (cref:WellKnownReferences.GetNullableGetHasValueReference). Issue #3163: keyed with the (cref:RemapScope), mirroring (cref:NullableUserValueTypeGetValueMemberRefs).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataTokenCache.NullableUserValueTypeGetValueMemberRefs
member.summary: Gets the cache mapping a user-defined value-type underlying ( or value-kind ) to the for System.Nullable1<T>::get_Value() (issue #1572). The parent TypeSpec closes Nullable<> over the type's emitted TypeDef/TypeSpec, so one MemberRef per underlying serves every (v!!) unwrap and narrowing-read site. Issue #3163: the underlying can be (or contain) a type parameter whose VAR/MVAR ordinal depends on the active remaps, so the key includes the (cref:RemapScope).

Mirrors : the emitter resolves this event's add/remove accessor methods to a MethodDef or (for a constructed generic interface) a MemberRef/TypeSpec token and binds a MethodImpl row per accessor so the CLR routes interface dispatch to this event's own distinct accessor bodies. Defaults to null for ordinary events.
