member.summary: Gets the field accessibility.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.ConstantValue
member.summary: Gets the compile-time constant value for a field (Issue #948), or null for non-const fields. The binder folds the field initializer to a literal and writes it here; the emitter uses it to add the Constant metadata row and to inline const-field reads.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.Declaration
member.summary: Gets the declaring field or primary-constructor parameter syntax, or null for imported and synthesized fields.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.ExplicitOffset
member.summary: Gets the explicit byte offset declared via @FieldOffset(N) (ADR-0093 / issue #759), or null when the field uses the default sequential layout. Only valid on fields of types declared with @StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit); the binder enforces the mutual constraint (GS0347 / GS0348) and writes the resolved offset onto the symbol so the emitter can produce a matching FieldLayout row.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.FixedBufferElementType
member.summary: Gets the fixed-size buffer element type T (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035), or null for non-buffer fields.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.FixedBufferLength
member.summary: Gets the fixed-size buffer element count N (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035), or 0 for non-buffer fields.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.ImportedMember

summary.para: Gets the reflected member an imported symbol stands for, or null for a declared one (ADR-0212 slice S4).

member.remarks: The language server reads it to find documentation and cross-assembly definitions until handle-backed imported symbols replace it (ADR-0209 stage 6).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.IsConst
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this field is a compile-time constant declared with const (Issue #948). A const field is implicitly static and read-only, and its reads inline . ECMA constants emit as literal fields; decimal uses initialized static read-only storage with DecimalConstantAttribute.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.IsEventBackingField
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this field is the compiler-synthesized backing field of a field-like event (issue #2083). See the constructor parameter of the same name for why this distinction matters to the emitter's delegate-to-delegate null-guard.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.IsFixedBuffer
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this field is a fixed-size buffer (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035, spelled fixed name [N]T). When true, is the compiler-generated nested buffer struct (carrying the [FixedBuffer] attribute and explicit layout size), and references to the field decay to a *T to the first element.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.IsReadOnly
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this field is init-only after construction.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.IsStatic
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this field is declared inside a shared block (ADR-0053).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FieldSymbol.Type
member.summary: Gets the field type.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.Arity
member.summary: Gets the number of parameters of the pointed-to function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.CallingConvention
member.summary: Gets the unmanaged calling convention used to invoke through this pointer. Ignored when is true and meaningless when is true.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.IsManaged
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a managed function pointer (ADR-0122 §9 / issue #1035, spelled *func(T1, T2) R) that is callable directly via the CIL calli opcode with the default managed calling convention. When false this is the unmanaged raw function pointer (ADR-0095, spelled unmanaged[CC] (T1, T2) -> R) whose ABI is given by .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.IsUnmanagedExtended
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this unmanaged pointer uses the open CLR calling-convention model (ADR-0095 v2 / issue #3611): the signature encodes SignatureCallingConvention.Unmanaged and the conventions (if any) ride as CallConv* modopts on the return type. true for bare unmanaged (T) -> R (platform default, empty ) and for every non-legacy or combined [CC, ...] list.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.ParameterTypes
member.summary: Gets the function pointer's parameter types.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.ReturnType
member.summary: Gets the function pointer's return type. for a void-returning pointer.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.UnmanagedConventionClrTypes
member.summary: Gets the resolved System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CallConv{Name} types matching pairwise; the emitter writes these as return-type modopts. Same staleness contract as (cleared with the cache when the owning metadata load context is disposed).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionPointerTypeSymbol.UnmanagedConventions
member.summary: Gets the open-model convention short names in source order (e.g. Cdecl, SuppressGCTransition — without the CallConv prefix). Empty for the bare platform-default form and for legacy/managed pointers.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.Accessibility
member.summary: Gets the CLR visibility level for this function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.AmbientContextParameter
member.summary: Gets the parameter this function's channel operations park on (ADR-0174 D7): a Context the author declared in the signature, or the synthesized , or null when the function carries neither.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.AssociatedSymbol
member.summary: Gets the property this function is an accessor of, or null — the Roslyn IMethodSymbol.AssociatedSymbol analogue (ADR-0169, issue #4436). Set when a property's or is assigned.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.AsyncReturnsValueTask
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this async function's declared return-type clause explicitly spelled a ValueTask / ValueTask[T] wrapper (issue #1918) rather than the default (implicit or explicit Task / Task[T]) wrapper. still holds the unwrapped awaited result (T, or for bare ValueTask) — this flag only steers which BCL wrapper / async-method-builder the state machine and observable call-site return type use.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.Declaration
member.summary: Gets the declaration of the function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.EmittedParameters
member.summary: Gets the parameters as the CLR sees them: , then the hidden Context of a suspending function (ADR-0174 D7). Every emit-time consumer — signature encoding, parameter rows, argument slots, state-machine hoisting — uses this list. The context goes last, and is emitted optional, so a caller that does not know about it (C#, another G# assembly) still binds the signature it was written to call.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExplicitInterfaceClauseTarget
member.summary: Gets or sets the interface type the explicit-interface qualifier clause () resolves to, bound by once the containing type's interface list is fully known. null until resolved, and remains null if the clause's type does not bind to an interface implemented by the containing type (a diagnostic is reported in that case).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExplicitInterfaceMember
member.summary: Gets or sets the in-compilation (G#) interface member this method explicitly implements (issue #2010; property/indexer generalization: issue #2362; ADR-0149 rewrites the source-level convention that establishes this link). Set when the method carries a dedicated explicit-interface qualifier clause (func (IFoo) M(...), ADR-0149) whose bound interface type — see — declares a member with this method's own plain name and a matching signature. Unlike (which binds to an external CLR interface resolved via reflection), this points at the interface member's own within the same compilation — the emitter resolves it to a MethodDef or (for a constructed generic interface) a MemberRef/TypeSpec token and binds a MethodImpl row so the CLR routes interface dispatch to this method's own distinct body instead of relying on name-based virtual dispatch. Two explicit implementations of same-name/same-signature members from different interfaces never collide at the source level — see and for the duplicate-declaration carve-out — even though the emitter must still synthesize a CLR-unique metadata name for the MethodDef (the source/diagnostic name stays the plain declared name). Defaults to null for ordinary methods.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExplicitInterfaceSlot
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLR interface slot this method explicitly implements via a covariant-return interface bridge (issue #985). Two same-name, same-parameter methods that differ only by return type and satisfy two DIFFERENT interface slots — e.g. the non-generic IEnumerable.GetEnumerator() alongside the generic IEnumerable<T>.GetEnumerator() — form a bridge. This carries the CLR interface method the emitter must bind to with an explicit MethodImpl row. A private bridge method cannot implicitly implement an interface slot, so the explicit row is required for the resulting type to load. Defaults to null for ordinary methods.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExplicitInterfaceSlotContainingType
member.summary: Gets or sets the imported interface type that owns .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExplicitReceiverParameter
member.summary: Gets the source receiver parameter for func (r R) M methods-with-receivers; null for in-body methods and non-method functions.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExtensionReceiverType
member.summary: Gets or sets the receiver type for an extension function (Phase 3.B.6). null when is false.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExternalOverriddenMethod
member.summary: Gets or sets the imported CLR virtual method this method overrides. The emitter uses this target to write an explicit MethodImpl row, which is required for covariant-return overrides and keeps reflection/runtime dispatch tied to the external base slot.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ExternalOverrideContainingType
member.summary: Gets or sets the imported constructed base type that owns . Preserves symbolic generic type arguments when the base is inherited as Base[T].

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.HasCaptures
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this direct-call local function ( non-null; issue #4219 umbrella remainder) captures outer state. Stamped from once the literal's body (and, for a group, the #4221 fixed-point capture reconciliation) has finished binding — see StatementBinder.BindLocalFunctionLiteralGroup. Consulted by method-group/delegate conversion (ExpressionBinder.IsMethodGroupCandidateUsable): a NON-capturing direct-call local converts like an ordinary function, but a CAPTURING one has no single stable closure instance to bind a delegate to (each direct call to it materializes its own), so bare- name conversion is not offered — same limitation an existing capturing GENERIC local function already has.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.HasExplicitInterfaceClause
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this method's declaration carries a dedicated explicit-interface qualifier clause (func (IFoo) M(...), ADR-0149) — a purely syntactic fact known immediately at declaration time, before is resolved against the containing type's implemented interfaces. Members with this flag set are exempt from the ordinary duplicate-overload-signature check (ADR-0063 §11): an explicit-interface member is never expected to share the plain concrete API surface, so it may coexist with (or, once resolved, with another explicit member targeting a different interface) a same-name/same-signature member.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.HasNonGenericLexicalOwner
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a fieldless direct-call host needs no enclosing generic slots.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.HasUnscopedRef
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function carries @UnscopedRef (ADR-0184 / issue #376; ), which lifts the implicit scoped on a struct instance member's this so the member may return a reference into its own instance state.
member.remarks: Computed over rather than stored, so it is immune to the binder's construct-then-SetAttributes ordering and propagates for free through every symbol-cloning site that copies the attribute list. A property/indexer accessor is the one shape that cannot answer from its own list — accessors are built with declaration: null and never receive a SetAttributes call — so pushes the owning property's answer down onto it.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.HiddenContextParameter
member.summary: Gets the hidden leading Context parameter a suspending function carries (ADR-0174 D7), or null for every other function. It is deliberately absent from — overload resolution, arity checks, hover and signature help must never see it, and binding runs again on every keystroke in the language server — and appears only in , the list the CLR signature, slot assignment and state-machine hoisting use. It is emitted as a trailing optional parameter, so a caller written against the function's declared signature — C#, reflection with , another G# assembly — still binds.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsAbstract
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this method is abstract — issue #987. A no-body open func F() R; on an open class is the canonical G# spelling of a C# abstract method: it declares a virtual slot with no implementation that concrete derived classes must override. When true, the binder skips body binding (there is no body) and the emitter writes a MethodAttributes.Abstract | Virtual | NewSlot method with no IL body, and the containing type is emitted with TypeAttributes.Abstract. Defaults to false.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsAsync
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function is declared async (Phase 5.1 / ADR-0023). When true, callers observe the function's return as Task[T] (or Task when no return type was declared) and the body may use await.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsAsyncOrSuspending
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function's body is compiled as an async state machine — declared async, or suspending.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsAsyncVoid
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function explicitly declares async ... void. Such a function uses AsyncVoidMethodBuilder and is observable as void, while an async function whose return type is omitted remains Task-returning.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsExpressionInitializer
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether statements are being bound inside a field or constructor-initializer expression.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsExtension
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function is an extension function (Phase 3.B.6, ADR-0019). When true, the function's first parameter is the receiver and call sites x.Foo(args) bind to Foo(x, args).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsFunctionLiteral
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether a function literal's body is bound under this symbol.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsGeneric
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function declares one or more type parameters (Phase 4.1).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsInitOnlySetter
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function is the synthesized setter of an init-only property (issue #946). When true the emitter stamps the void return with the IsExternalInit modreq, and the binder treats the accessor body as an init-assignment context (so it may assign other init-only properties on the same instance).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsInstanceMethod
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function is an instance method on a user-defined class.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsLocalFunction
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this is a local function's symbol.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsOpen
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this method is declared open — overridable per ADR-0017 (Phase 3.B.3 sub-step 3).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsOverride
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this method is declared override — must shadow an open base method per ADR-0017.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsPInvoke
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function is a P/Invoke stub (ADR-0086).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsReturnTypeInferred
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function's return type is being inferred (ADR-0076 / issue #716). Set to true on the synthetic placeholder the arrow-lambda binder pushes while binding a lambda body whose return type is not declared up-front. When this flag is true, the return-statement binder must skip the usual void / declared-return-type validation and must NOT apply a target-typed conversion — the lambda binder collects the bound return expressions, computes the inferred return type from their common-type, and applies a single post-bind conversion pass. Defaults to false.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsSpecialName
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function should be emitted with MethodAttributes.SpecialName (e.g., event accessor methods).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsStatic
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function is declared inside a shared block (ADR-0053). Static functions have no receiver.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsStaticInitializer
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this synthetic function represents a type's static-constructor context.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsSuspending
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function is suspending (ADR-0174 D4).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsTopLevelEntryPoint
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this function is the synthesized top-level-statement entry point (<Main>$) introduced by ADR-0066. When true, variable declarations inside its body continue to be promoted to (matching the historical TLS shape) and a few other binder paths treat the function as a top-level context even though a non-null exists for return-type validation.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.IsUnsafe
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this (ADR-0122 / issue #1014) function constitutes an unsafe context — either because the declaration carried the unsafe modifier (unsafe func) or because its containing type was declared unsafe. When true, the signature and body may use unmanaged raw pointers () and raw-pointer operations.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.LexicalEnclosingType
member.summary: Gets or sets the nearest enclosing user-defined type whose member body lexically contains this function (issue #1335). This is set on synthetic lambda / function-literal symbols so that protected/private accessibility checks performed while binding a closure body resolve the same access context as the enclosing member — a closure nested in a member of type C has the same access to C's members as the member itself. null for ordinary methods and top-level functions (which carry their context via /).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.LocalDeclaration
member.summary: Gets the source declaration of a directly callable generic local function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.MethodKind
member.summary: Gets what kind of function this is — the Roslyn IMethodSymbol.MethodKind analogue (ADR-0169, issue #4436).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.OverriddenMethod
member.summary: Gets or sets the base method this method overrides. Set by the binder when is true and a matching open base method is found; null otherwise.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.PInvokeMetadata
member.summary: Gets or sets the resolved @DllImport metadata for a P/Invoke function declaration (ADR-0086 / issue #727). Non-null when the function is a well-formed P/Invoke stub; the emitter consumes the payload to produce the ImplMap row that points the unmanaged entry point at the runtime's native-library loader. Defaults to null for ordinary managed functions.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.Package
member.summary: Gets the package this function belongs to. null for built-in functions, which are not scoped to a user package.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.Parameters
member.summary: Gets the parameters of the function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ReceiverType
member.summary: Gets the class type that owns this function when it is an instance method (Phase 3.B.3 sub-step 2b). null for top-level functions and static methods.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.StateMachineType
member.summary: Gets or sets the synthesized state-machine type that hosts this method's lowered body, when the async state-machine rewriter has run on this method. null when the method is not async or when the rewriter has not yet visited it. The owning property is typed as to avoid a project-layer cycle (state-machine types live under Lowering.Async); callers cast to SynthesizedStateMachineType.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.StaticOwnerType
member.summary: Gets or sets the type that owns this static method (ADR-0053 for struct/class owners; ADR-0089 for interface owners). null for non-static or top-level functions.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.SuspendingKind
member.summary: Gets or sets how this function is suspending (ADR-0174 D4). A suspending function is compiled through the same state-machine pipeline as an async func but returns ValueTask[R] with the pooling builder, carries [Suspending], and is awaited implicitly by every G# call site — stays the logical R. Never set together with .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.ThisParameter
member.summary: Gets the synthesized this parameter for instance methods, or null for non-instance functions. Always at IL parameter slot 0 when emitted.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.Type
member.summary: Gets the type of the function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionSymbol.TypeParameters
member.summary: Gets or sets the generic type parameters declared on this function (Phase 4.1 / ADR-0020). Empty for non-generic functions.
member.remarks: ADR-0087 §3 R2: setting this collection flips each parameter's flag so the emitter encodes references as MVAR(idx) instead of VAR(idx) in signature blobs.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol.Arity
member.summary: Gets the number of parameters.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol.HasVariadic
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this function type declares a trailing variadic parameter.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol.IsVariadic
member.summary: Gets the per-parameter variadic flags (ADR-0102 follow-up / issue #818). Always parallel to — entry i is true iff the corresponding parameter is the trailing variadic ...T slot. All-false for a regular function type. The variadic slot's entry is the already-wrapped slice ([]T) so existing callers that just look at the parameter type continue to work; the flag is consulted at call sites to drive pack / pass-through.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol.ParameterTypes
member.summary: Gets the function's parameter types.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.FunctionTypeSymbol.ReturnType
member.summary: Gets the function's return type. void when the function returns nothing.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.GlobalVariableSymbol.Accessibility
member.summary: Gets the CLR visibility level for this global variable.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.GlobalVariableSymbol.ConstantValue
member.summary: Gets the compile-time value for an global.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.GlobalVariableSymbol.IsConst
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this global is a compile-time constant. Reads are inlined from . ECMA constants emit as literal fields; decimal uses initialized static read-only storage.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitFieldVariableSymbol.Field
member.summary: Gets the field symbol.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitFieldVariableSymbol.Receiver
member.summary: Gets the implicit receiver parameter (this) for the enclosing method.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitFieldVariableSymbol.StructType
member.summary: Gets the class that owns the field.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitPropertyVariableSymbol.Property
member.summary: Gets the property symbol.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitPropertyVariableSymbol.Receiver
member.summary: Gets the implicit receiver parameter (this) for the enclosing method.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImplicitPropertyVariableSymbol.StructType
member.summary: Gets the class that owns the property.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImportedTypeSymbol.ConstructedTypeArguments
member.summary:
Gets the type arguments this instantiation was constructed with, preferring the SYMBOLIC over the CLR ones (ADR-0169, issue #3794).
The base implementation reads ClrType.GenericTypeArguments, and for a generic constructed over a same-compilation user type the CLR form is type-ERASED — Dictionary[StructSymbol, MemberReferenceHandle] is backed by Dictionary<object, object>. A migrated analyzer walking a member's type structure (GSA0004's key/value inspection is exactly this) therefore saw System.Object for every argument and matched nothing at all — the silent under-reporting failure mode #3795 warned about. The symbolic arguments are the ones the source actually wrote, so they are what Roslyn's INamedTypeSymbol.TypeArguments corresponds to; the erased CLR list stays the fallback for a plain imported type that carries none.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImportedTypeSymbol.HasSubstitutableTypeArgument
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this symbol's symbolic type arguments should be substituted back through its when projecting member / element types (issue #939). This is broader than : it also holds when an argument is a same-compilation user class/data struct (whose is null because its CLR type is still being built and the closed shape is erased to object), or a nested constructed generic with symbolic arguments (e.g. List[List[MyGs]]). The indexer path (MapErasedIndexerElementType) and the for-in enumerable path both rely on this so iterating List[Item] recovers the member-bearing user Item symbol rather than the type-erased object.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ImportedTypeSymbol.HasTypeParameterArgument
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this symbol carries symbolic type arguments that include an in-scope generic type parameter (#313), in which case it is an open/partially-constructed generic whose emit form is type-erased to System.Object.

member.summary: Gets the constant default value declared on this parameter (ADR-0063). Only meaningful when is true. Value kinds: numeric primitive, , , , enum constant (carried as its underlying integral value), or null for a nullable/reference parameter or a value-type default(T) / T() default (issue #1182), whose all-zero value is materialized at the call site via a .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.HasExplicitDefaultValue
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter declares an explicit default value (ADR-0063). When true, callers may omit a corresponding argument and the binder substitutes at the call site.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.HasUnscopedRef
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter carries the @UnscopedRef contract, including on a source parameter clone whose attributes are intentionally not re-emitted.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.IsReceiverParameter
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter is the enclosing function's receiver (ADR-0184) — the implicit this of a member declared in a struct/class body, or the source-visible receiver of a receiver-clause function (func (r R) M()). Set once by 's constructor for whichever parameter becomes .
member.remarks: The CLR passes a struct's receiver as ref S, so the receiver's storage is WRITABLE and its value-scope (safe-to-escape) is the caller's — unlike an ordinary by-value parameter slot. alone cannot express that, because it is derived from and the receiver's is . ExpressionBinder.ReceiverVariableIsThis already carried this exemption for member WRITES; this flag makes the same fact available to the static ref-capability classifiers that have no enclosing-function context.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.IsScoped
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this parameter carries the scoped modifier (ADR-0058 / issue #376). When true, the parameter's safe-to-escape scope is restricted to the current function body and it may not be directly returned from a ref-struct-returning function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.IsUnscopedRefReceiver
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this receiver parameter's member carries @UnscopedRef (ADR-0184 / issue #376) (), lifting the implicit scoped on the receiver's REF-safe-context so the member may return a reference into its own instance state.
member.remarks: Deliberately a dedicated flag rather than promoting the receiver's to : the latter would make every lambda inside a struct member trip GS9010 ("a ref parameter cannot be captured by a closure"), which has nothing to do with this feature.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.IsVariadic
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter is variadic (Phase 4.8).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.MarshalAsMetadata
member.summary: Gets the resolved @MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.…) override for this parameter (ADR-0096 / issue #762), or null when the parameter has no such annotation. Attached by on P/Invoke declarations after per-parameter validation; consumed by the emitter to write a FieldMarshal table row and stamp on the Param row.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.RefKind
member.summary: Gets or sets the ADR-0060 by-reference passing mode of this parameter (None, Ref, Out, or In).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol.UsesUpdatedEscapeRules
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter's declaring module uses the version-11 ref-safety rules. Source parameters always do; imported parameters require the module marker.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.DeclaringSyntaxNodes
member.summary:
Gets the declaring syntax — the property's IDENTIFIER, matching what #3847 already does for a field and what Roslyn's IPropertySymbol.Locations[0] points at (ADR-0169, issue #3794).
A migrated symbol-action analyzer reports at Symbol.Location, and the whole declaration spans the accessors and the initializer, so the reported span swallowed the marked name and the verifier rejected it as not contained in the marker. The name is the construct the diagnostic is about; the accessors are not.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.ExplicitInterfaceClauseTarget
member.summary: Gets or sets the interface type the explicit-interface qualifier clause () resolves to, bound by . null until resolved.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.ExplicitInterfaceGetterSlot
member.summary: Gets or sets the imported interface getter slot explicitly implemented by this property.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.ExplicitInterfaceMember
member.summary: Gets or sets the in-compilation (G#) interface member this property explicitly implements (issue #2362, extending the #2010 convention from methods to properties/indexers; ADR-0149 rewrites the source-level convention that establishes this link). Set when the property carries a dedicated explicit-interface qualifier clause (prop (IFoo) P T / prop (IFoo) this[...] T, ADR-0149) whose bound interface type — see — declares a member with this property's own plain name and a matching accessor shape. Mirrors : the emitter resolves this property's getter/setter accessor methods to a MethodDef or (for a constructed generic interface) a MemberRef/TypeSpec token and binds a MethodImpl row per accessor so the CLR routes interface dispatch to this property's own distinct accessor bodies instead of relying on name-based virtual dispatch. An explicit property implementation never collides with a same-named public concrete property (the #2362 defect) because explicit-clause members are exempt from the plain duplicate-name check — see and . Defaults to null for ordinary properties.

member.remarks: The language server reads it to find documentation and cross-assembly definitions until handle-backed imported symbols replace it (ADR-0209 stage 6).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.IsInitOnly
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this property's setter is an init-only accessor (issue #946). An init-only setter is emitted as a set_Prop method whose void return carries the System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsExternalInit modreq, and assignment is restricted to object initialization (the declaring type's constructors, object/aggregate initializers at the creation site, and other init accessors of the same instance).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.IsVirtual

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol.MetadataIsAbstract
member.summary: Gets the abstractness read straight out of metadata for an imported property, or null when this property was declared in source (issue #2874).
member.remarks: An imported property carries no body syntax, so the source-shape inference below classified every virtual, non-overriding imported property (for example one that implements an interface member, which is emitted virtual newslot) as abstract. That propagated to and made the whole imported type unconstructible with GS0386. Metadata already records the answer exactly, so imported properties bypass the inference entirely.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceResolver.MissingTransitiveReferences
member.summary: Gets the simple names of assemblies that are referenced (transitively) by the supplied reference set but could not be resolved from either that set or the gsc host runtime. An empty array means the supplied references form a complete transitive closure. A non-empty array indicates the project is under-referenced: touching a member whose signature lives in one of these assemblies would otherwise throw deep in member enumeration, so the resolver degrades gracefully (the member is skipped) and callers may surface a diagnostic naming the missing assemblies (issue #340).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.BaseConstructorInitializer
member.summary: Gets the explicit base-constructor initializer (: Base(args)) declared on this class (issue #306), or null when the class chains to a parameterless base constructor. When non-null the emitter forwards the bound arguments to the resolved base .ctor and suppresses the auto-generated parameterless constructor.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.ConstFields
member.summary: Gets the compile-time constant fields declared with const (Issue #948). Const fields are implicitly static and read-only, and reads are inlined. ECMA constants emit as literal fields; decimal constants use static read-only storage initialized by the type constructor. Held separately from and populated by the binder.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.DataClassCloneMethod
member.summary: Gets the definition-owned symbol for the emitted data-class clone slot.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.DataEqualsBase
member.summary: Gets the compiler-owned override of a direct data base's typed equality slot.

member.summary: Gets the compiler-owned override of the nullable object equality slot.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.DataEqualsSelf
member.summary: Gets the compiler-owned self equality signature on this exact construction.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.DataPrintMembers
member.summary: Gets the compiler-owned PrintMembers(StringBuilder) slot (ADR-0199), or null when this type declares its own (which then replaces it) or is an anonymous literal.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Declaration
member.summary: Gets the declaring syntax node.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.DeclaresStaticInitializerBlock
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the declaration has a shared { init { … } } block (#5483). Unlike , this is known from the declaration pass on, before any body is bound, so a body that is bound earlier reads the same answer as one bound later.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Definition
member.summary: Gets the original generic definition when this is a constructed instance; otherwise this.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Deinitializer
member.summary: Gets the user-declared deinit { … } destructor on this class (ADR-0068 / issue #698), or null when the class has none. Populated by the binder; consumed by the emitter to materialise the CLR Finalize override.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.EffectiveExplicitConstructors
member.summary: Gets the explicit init(...) constructors visible on this symbol, looking through to the generic definition for a constructed (closed) generic type (issue #1087). A constructed produced by does not carry its own explicit constructor table (those are populated on the open definition after the constructed shell already exists), so base-constructor resolution against a constructed generic base must consult the definition's table. The returned instances are the definition's, which is exactly what the emitter keys its constructor handles by; use to obtain the type-argument-substituted parameter signatures for overload matching.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Events
member.summary: Gets the events declared on this type (ADR-0052). Populated by the binder after the symbol is constructed; defaults to empty.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.ExplicitConstructor
member.summary: Gets the standalone user-defined constructor (init(...)) declared on this class or plain struct (issues #306/#2766), or null when the aggregate has none. When non-null the emitter materializes exactly one .ctor (this constructor) and suppresses the auto-generated parameterless / primary constructor.
member.remarks: ADR-0063: when the class declares an overload family of init(...) constructors, still surfaces the first declaration so single-constructor callers keep working; the full overload set lives on .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Fields
member.summary: Gets the field declarations in source order.
member.remarks: Issue #1341: on a constructed instance, fields are substituted lazily from so a late-bound definition body is observed (order-independent member lookup).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.FixedBufferElementType
member.summary: Gets the fixed-size buffer element type for a fixed-buffer backing struct (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035), or null.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasAnonymousConstructorMembers
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the definition's constructor arguments carry anonymous-object property members.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasCompleteReifiedTypeParameterVector
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether already includes every generic parameter required by this type's enclosing type chain.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasDataConstructionPrimary
member.summary: Gets whether existing G# metadata assigns brace inputs to a primary constructor.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasDeclaredPrimaryConstructor
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this type declares a primary-constructor parameter list, including an empty list.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasPrimaryConstructor
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this type carries an explicit primary constructor (Phase 3.B.3 sub-step 2).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasStaticInitializerBlock
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the type declares a shared { init { … } } static-initializer block (ADR-0140 / issue #2131). Such a type must not be marked beforefieldinit.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.HasSynthesizedDataConstructor
member.summary: Gets whether ordinary data construction needs a compiler-owned public constructor.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.ImplementedClrInterfaces
member.summary: Gets the imported (CLR) interfaces this class implements (issue #525). Each entry's is guaranteed to be an interface type. Populated by the binder when the base-type clause names a reachable imported CLR interface; defaults to empty. When set, the emitter writes an InterfaceImpl row per entry so the resulting class is a real CLR implementer (Type.GetInterfaces() surfaces the interface and dispatch through interface receivers works).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.ImportedBaseType
member.summary: Gets the imported (CLR) base class this GSharp class derives from (issue #296), or null when the class derives from another GSharp class () or directly from System.Object. When set, the emitter writes this CLR type as the TypeDef's base type and chains the generated constructor to the CLR base's parameterless .ctor(); member lookup walks into this type so inherited CLR members are accessible on instances of the derived GSharp class.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.ImportedInterfaceAccessors
member.summary: Gets imported accessors selected by interface conformance binding.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Interfaces
member.summary: Gets the interfaces this type implements (Phase 3.B.4). Populated by the binder after the symbol is constructed; defaults to empty.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsAbstract
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this class is abstract: an explicit abstract or shared modifier (ADR-0195), an unimplemented abstract member in its effective own/inherited member set after override resolution (including imported CLR contracts), or a non-data descendant of an abstract synthesized record-clone ancestor. Such a type cannot be instantiated and is emitted with TypeAttributes.Abstract; a shared class is also sealed. Always false for value-type structs.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsAnonymousLiteral
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type is the synthesized backing type of an anonymous literal (data object { ... } or object { ... }, ADR-0146). Such a type keeps G#'s equality surface and prints as a C# anonymous type (ADR-0199); it gets no PrintMembers, copy constructor or clone.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsAttributeClass
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this class is sugar-marked as a -derived type via the @Attribute declaration sugar from ADR-0047 §5. When true, the emitter overrides the CLR base type from System.Object to and chains the class's constructors to System.Attribute..ctor().

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsClass
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a class declaration (Phase 3.B.3). Class types are reference types on the CLR; struct types (this flag false) are value types.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsConstructedNestedType
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a constructed reference to a type nested inside a generic enclosing type (issue #1521) — it carries but declares no own type arguments.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsData
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a data struct declaration (ADR-0029).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsDeclaredAbstract
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the class was declared with the abstract modifier (ADR-0195 / issue #4674). Unlike the member-derived , this is the author's explicit statement, so a class with no abstract member can still be uninstantiable (a migrated C# abstract class with only concrete members). Such a class is inheritable: the binder gives it .

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsFixedBufferBacking
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a compiler-generated fixed-size buffer backing struct (ADR-0122 §10 / issue #1035). The emitter stamps such a struct with [CompilerGenerated] and [UnsafeValueType] and an explicit ClassLayout size of N * sizeof(T).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsGenericDefinition
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a generic definition (has type parameters and no type arguments).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsInline
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is an inline struct declaration (ADR-0033).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsOpen
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this class was declared open (Phase 3.B.3 sub-step 3 / ADR-0017). Required for subclassing.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsRefStruct
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this is a by-ref-like (ref struct) declaration (issue #367). By-ref-like value types are stack-only: they cannot be boxed, stored in a field of a non-ref-struct, captured by a closure, hoisted into an async/iterator state machine, or used as a generic type argument. Derived from the declaring syntax so it is preserved across generic construction.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsSealedHierarchy
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this class was declared sealed class (ADR-0078). A sealed class participates in exhaustiveness checking: its subclasses form a closed set (Kotlin/Swift sealed-class semantics) and the switch binder requires every subclass to be covered by an arm.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.IsSharedClass
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the class was declared with the shared modifier (ADR-0195 / issue #4674): emitted CLR abstract sealed with no instance constructor, every member shared, the shape of a C# static class.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.LayoutMetadata

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol.Methods
member.summary: Gets the methods declared inside the class body (Phase 3.B.3 sub-step 2b). Populated by the binder after the symbol is constructed; defaults to empty.
member.remarks: Issue #1341: methods are erased generically (ADR-0004) and carried on a constructed instance without per-construction substitution, so a constructed instance always reflects its 's current method set by forwarding the read. This keeps member lookup on a constructed generic user type independent of the order in which source files are bound: even when the construction is materialized (and cached) before the definition's body — and therefore its methods — has been bound, reads observe the methods once they are populated rather than an empty snapshot captured at construction time.

Imported collection defaults retain their existing CLR literal path; their owning constructor cannot be synthesized in this compilation.

member.summary:
Gets the positional tuple elements as field symbols — the Roslyn INamedTypeSymbol.TupleElements analogue (ADR-0169, issue #3794).
Without this override the base returned EMPTY, so a migrated analyzer that walks a tuple's elements (GSA0004's cache-key inspection is exactly that) saw a tuple with no components and silently concluded the key mentioned nothing — reporting nothing at all. Elements are named after their declared name where ADR-0172 gives one, and Item1..ItemN otherwise, which is what Roslyn does.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.ClassConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets the base-class (non-interface) constraint, if any (issue #1056). Holds the user-declared class (a with , possibly a constructed generic such as the self-referential [T Box[T]]) or an imported reference-type class that a type argument must derive from (or equal). Mirrors C#'s where T : BaseClass. C# permits at most one class constraint; G#'s single legacy constraint slot enforces this structurally. The emitter projects this onto a GenericParamConstraint metadata row and dispatches instance members declared on the base class through a normal callvirt on the (reference-typed) type parameter — no constrained. prefix is required because the bound proves T is a reference type.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.ClrInterfaceConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets the imported CLR interface constraint, if any (issue #943). Holds an imported (possibly constructed-generic) CLR interface — e.g. System.IComparable[T] from [T IComparable[T]] — that a type argument must implement. Unlike (which models a G#-declared ), this models a BCL / reference-assembly interface. Self-referential generic constraints (the type parameter appears in its own constraint) are supported. The emitter projects this onto a GenericParamConstraint metadata row and routes instance calls on the type parameter through it with a constrained. prefix so the IL is verifiable.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.Constraint
member.summary: Gets or sets the constraint applied to this type parameter (Phase 4.2 will add comparable / sealed-interface bounds).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.ConstraintInterfaceType
member.summary: Gets the single interface bound carried by this type parameter, if any — either the G# or the imported (issue #943). Used by the emitter to emit the GenericParamConstraint row and by the binder to enforce constraint satisfaction at call sites.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.ConstraintReferenceType
member.summary: Gets the single TypeDefOrRefOrSpec bound this type parameter projects onto a GenericParamConstraint metadata row — the interface bound () or the base-class bound (, issue #1056), or the dependent bound on another type parameter (, issue #4043). At most one of these is set for a given type parameter.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.DependentBoundProvesReferenceType
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this parameter's DEPENDENT bound chain proves it is a reference type in every instantiation (issue #4062) — [TBase class, TDerived TBase], or a longer chain, whose ROOT carries class or a base-class bound. C# propagates a bounding parameter's special constraints to the bounded one, so csc accepts TDerived x = null; there; before this, G# reported GS0155.
member.remarks:
Deliberately a SEPARATE question from / rather than a widening of either slot. Roughly forty consumers read ClassConstraint != null as "this parameter is a reference type" AND as "this is the type it derives from" — the second reading drives boxing and callvirt decisions in the emitter, and a dependent bound supplies no such type. Merging the slots is #4027's defect shape; this property answers only the reference-ness half, and exactly one consumer reads it (Conversion.IsNilAssignableWithoutNullableWrapper).
Terminated by VISITED-SYMBOL cycle detection, not by a depth limit (review of PR #4088). A semantic depth cap answers "no" for a chain that is merely long — [T0 class, T1 T0, … T33 T32] proves T33 is a reference type after 33 hops, and a 32-hop cap would report GS0155 on it — so the only thing that may stop the walk is actually revisiting a parameter. #4043 already rejects and CLEARS a cyclic bound (GS0581, DeclarationBinder.Functions.cs), so this set is belt-and-braces for a chain reached before that clearing.
The set is keyed on REFERENCE identity, which is well-defined for an open type parameter and needs no name at all. That is deliberate: PR #4068's first attempt at the same replacement keyed on ClrTypeUtilities.IsSameAs, whose Type.FullName is null for an open constructed generic, so every nested List<…> compared equal and a FALSE cycle fired at the first argument — strictly worse than the cap it replaced while looking like a fix. A is a single binder-allocated instance per declared parameter, so identity is exactly the right key and no name is consulted. This is the same idiom Binder.SatisfiesClassConstraint adopted for #4091/#4102 — a DIFFERENT question (does this argument satisfy one named base class, following ClassConstraint ?? TypeParameterBound) reached independently, so the two walks stay separate but agree on how a chain is terminated.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.HasDefaultConstructorConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type parameter carries the default-constructor (init()) constraint (ADR-0097 / issue #775; spelled new() before issue #997). Type arguments must either be a value type or expose a public parameterless constructor. Maps to in emitted IL.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.HasReferenceTypeConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type parameter carries a reference-type (class) constraint (ADR-0097 / issue #775). Type arguments must be a reference type (!IsValueType at the CLR level). Maps to in emitted IL.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.HasUnmanagedConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type parameter carries an unmanaged constraint (issue #1336). Type arguments must be an unmanaged type — a non-nullable value type whose fields are recursively unmanaged (blittable primitives, enums, pointers, or other unmanaged structs). The unmanaged constraint implies the value-type (struct) and default-constructor flags at the CLR level, and the emitter additionally projects a GenericParamConstraint to System.ValueType carrying a required custom modifier (modreq) of System.Runtime.InteropServices.UnmanagedType — the exact metadata shape C# emits for where T : unmanaged. That modreq is what makes a pointer to the type parameter (*T) and sizeof(T) over it verifiable.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.HasValueTypeConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type parameter carries a value-type (struct) constraint (ADR-0097 / issue #775). Type arguments must be a non-nullable value type. Maps to in emitted IL. A struct constraint implies the init() (default-constructor) flag at the CLR level — the emitter sets both bits automatically per ECMA-335 II.10.1.7.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.InterfaceConstraint
member.summary: Gets or sets the sealed-interface constraint, if any (Phase 4.2b / ADR-0020). When non-null, type arguments must implement this interface. ADR-0089 allows late patching by the binder when the constraint is a self-referential constructed generic such as [T IAdd[T]].

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.IsMethodTypeParameter
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this type parameter is declared on a generic method (as opposed to a generic type). When true the emitter encodes it as MVAR(); when false as VAR() (ADR-0087 §3, R2).
member.remarks: Set by the binder when the type parameter is attached to a FunctionSymbol. Type-type parameters keep the default false.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.Ordinal
member.summary: Gets the zero-based ordinal of this type parameter in its declaring list.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol.TypeParameterBound
member.summary:
Gets or sets the DEPENDENT bound — another type parameter this one must derive from, satisfy, or equal (issue #4043). Mirrors C#'s where TDerived : TBase, spelled [TBase, TDerived TBase] in G#. The bound may be declared on the same list (a method's or a type's own parameters) or on the ENCLOSING type when a generic method's parameter names the class's — class Box[T] { func Accept[U T](u U) }.
Deliberately a SEPARATE slot from . Roughly forty consumers read ClassConstraint != null as "this parameter is a reference type" (nil acceptance, boxing decisions, callvirt without a constrained. prefix). A dependent bound proves nothing of the sort — TBase may itself be unconstrained, so TDerived can be instantiated with a struct — and reusing the slot would admit nil at a value-type slot, which is the #4027 unverifiable-ldnull defect one release later.
The emitter projects this onto a GenericParamConstraint metadata row whose TypeDefOrRefOrSpec is a TypeSpec naming VAR(n) / MVAR(n) — the encoding Roslyn emits for the same C# shape — through the existing TypeParameterSymbol branch of ImportedMemberRefFactory.GetElementTypeToken.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.ConstructorDeclarationSyntax.Span
member.remarks: The span starts at the ACCESSIBILITY MODIFIER when there is one. It used to start at convenience/init, which left private outside the declaration it introduces -- and a declaration whose span excludes its own modifiers is not merely imprecise, it is wrong in two places that both read Span.Start as "where this declaration begins": requires a documented declaration to start on the line after the /// block, and the ADR-0179 formatter puts its member break before that same position. Together those produced private on its own line, a blank line, then init -- and GS0227 "documentation comment is not attached to a declaration" on the migrated tree.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.ConversionIsExplicit
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this conversion operator is an explicit conversion (op_Explicit) rather than an implicit one (op_Implicit). Only meaningful when is true. Assigned by the parser.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.DeclaringPart
member.summary: Gets or sets the declaring part this node was merged from (ADR-0192). Non-null only on the synthetic node PartialMethodMerger builds from a declaring/implementing pair. The merger builds that node fresh on every bind from the untouched parsed parts; it never stores it back into the tree. The binder uses this to bind the declaring part's own signature in its own file's scope and to find its /// comment, and tooling can report both part locations. [SyntaxChildIgnore]: the declaring part's tokens already belong to their own declaration in its own file, so re-parenting them here would double-count them in child enumeration and stretch this node's across two files.

Distinct from — this is a single-type qualifier, not a name+type extension receiver. Assigned by the parser; null for an ordinary or extension function.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.ExplicitInterfaceType
member.summary: Gets or sets the interface type referenced by the explicit-interface qualifier clause (ADR-0149), e.g. the IFoo in func (IFoo) M(...). Assigned by the parser; null when no clause is present.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.ImplementingPart
member.summary: Gets or sets the implementing part this node was merged from (ADR-0192). Non-null only alongside , on the same synthetic merged node. The merged node's own tokens and body are copied from this part, but its node identity is not, and DocumentationAttacher indexes /// comments by node reference — so a comment written only on the implementing part is found through this reference. [SyntaxChildIgnore] for the same reason as .

member.summary: Gets the function's parameters.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.PartialModifier
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional partial contextual modifier (ADR-0192 / issue #4301) preceding this method's func keyword. When non-null the declaration is one part of a partial method: either the declaring part ( is true — signature and annotations only) or the implementing part ( is non-null). PartialMethodMerger collapses the two parts into a single declaration before the body binder runs, so a merged node carries this token but has a real body. Deliberately NOT [SyntaxChildIgnore]: the token must participate in child enumeration so covers it and tooling that walks the tree sees it. Assigned by the parser; null for an ordinary method.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.PartsDisagreement
member.summary: Gets or sets the GS0611 aspect the syntax-level consistency check reported for the pair this merged node was built from, or null when the parts agreed (ADR-0192). The merge proceeds either way; the binder's cross-file semantic signature check skips a pair that already disagreed, since past that point it could only add cascading diagnostics.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.FunctionDeclarationSyntax.RetiredExtensionKeyword
member.summary: Gets or sets the retired ADR-0165 extension marker token from func extension (receiver Type) Name(...), when the parser recognized that shape. ADR-0182 retired the marker (every receiver clause is unconditionally an extension now), so this token exists only to preserve full-fidelity source text for the declaration the parser reported GS0587 against; it carries no semantic meaning and binding never reads it.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.RefModifier

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.SealedKeyword
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional sealed contextual keyword (ADR-0078). Non-null marks a class as forming a closed hierarchy (subtypes confined to the same package). Always null for struct; the parser diagnoses sealed struct with GS0310.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.SharedBlock
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional shared { … } block (ADR-0053) grouping static member declarations. Null when the type has no shared block.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.SharedInitializers
member.summary: Gets or sets the static-initializer blocks (init { … }, ADR-0140) declared directly in the body of a shared class. Empty for any other aggregate (there they sit in the shared { } block). Assigned by the parser.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.SharedModifier
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional shared contextual modifier on a class head (ADR-0195 / issue #4674). Non-null marks this class shared: emitted abstract sealed with no instance constructor, every member declared directly in the body is a shared (static) member, and a shared { } block inside it is rejected. Assigned by the parser; null otherwise.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.StructKeyword
member.summary: Gets the struct or class keyword that marks this aggregate declaration. Inspect to distinguish.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.TypeKeyword

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.TypeParameterList
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional type-parameter list (Phase 4.3 / ADR-0020), e.g. [T any] in class Box[T any] { ... }. Assigned by the parser when the declaration is generic; null otherwise.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructDeclarationSyntax.UnsafeModifier
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional unsafe contextual modifier (ADR-0122 / issue #1014) contextual modifier on the aggregate declaration (unsafe class / unsafe struct). When non-null every member of the type is bound in an unsafe context, so fields, methods, and properties may use unmanaged raw pointers (*T → CLR ELEMENT_TYPE_PTR). Assigned by the parser; null otherwise.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.ChildCount
member.summary: Gets the number of children of this syntax node. Every concrete node class overrides this in SyntaxNode.Children.g.gs, which build/generate-syntax-children.py writes (issue #5136). A class that the generator did not see, or a subclass of a generated open class, uses the reflection projection instead .

member.summary: Gets the location of this syntax node.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.Parent
member.summary: Gets the parent node, or null for the root. Backed by the tree's lazily built parent index (ADR-0169) — the Roslyn SyntaxNode.Parent analogue analyzers rely on.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.PropertyChildCount
member.summary: Gets the number of children in property order. Only a node whose plan has PlanInPlace reads its properties in place; a span reads these accessors, never the sorted children (issue #5185).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.Span
member.summary: Gets the text span covered by this syntax node.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.SpanPlan
member.summary: Describes how a span and the child order of this node are computed, as the bits PlanBaseSpan, PlanSourceOrdered and PlanInPlace. A generated class returns a constant, so a span computation does not look up the type of each node (issue #5279). A class that the generator did not see, and a subclass of a generated open class, reads the plan by reflection.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxNode.SyntaxTree

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.IsMissing
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the token was inserted by the parser and doesn't appear in source.
member.remarks: Issue #3332: this was previously derived from Text == null. It is now carried explicitly, so a missing token can hold text without losing the distinction that CodeLens, semantic lookup and function declaration all rely on.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.IsSynthesized
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the parser made this token to complete a desugared form (the braces of a body-less type, the return of an expression body, the parentheses of T{...}). It carries text for the consumers that read it, but occupies no source.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.Position
member.summary: Gets the position of this syntax token.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.Span
member.summary: Gets the text span associated to the token.
member.remarks: Issue #5277: a synthesized token (see ) has text but is not written in source, so its span is zero-width at . It then never overlaps the real token that happens to start there, and never widens the span of the node that holds it.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.Text
member.summary: Gets the text seen by the lexer that created this syntax token.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.Value
member.summary: Gets the value of this syntax token, if any.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxToken.ValueText
member.summary: Gets the semantic name text of this token (ADR-0170 / issue #3610): for an escaped identifier $name this is the unescaped name the lexer stashed in ; for every other token it is . Semantic consumers (binder, symbols, lowering, emit) read identifier names through this property so an escaped spelling and its plain form denote the same name; syntactic consumers (printers, formatters, contextual-keyword commitments) keep using for source fidelity.

The array is always non-default; it is when the clause is not a function-type clause or carries no variadic.

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.TypeClauseSyntax.FunctionParameterTypes

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this array/slice clause is itself a nullable array reference ([]?T), spelled with a ? right after ] (issue #1212).

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this clause uses the canonical arrow-form spelling (...) -> R? (ADR-0075).

member.name: P:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.TypeClauseSyntax.ParenthesizedQuestionToken
member.summary: Gets the ? that followed the closing ) of a parenthesized type clause (issue #3315 / ADR-0159 addendum). Grouping parens are otherwise transparent — (T) parses to T's own clause — but their trailing ? marks the WHOLE inner type nullable, giving the composite types whose own trailing ? binds tighter an explicit whole-type-nullable spelling: (chan int32)? is a nullable channel of int32, whereas chan int32? is a channel of nullable elements. Set by the parser via immediately after the inner clause is built (the sanctioned parser-time mutation pattern, see ).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.BoundBodyAnalysisContext
member.summary: The context passed to bound-body actions — the counterpart of Roslyn's OperationBlockAnalysisContext (ADR-0169, issue #4436). A body action runs once per declared function body and sees the whole bound body at once, so a rule can relate nodes to each other (a local's initializer to its later uses, say) without walking up a parent chain, which bound nodes do not have.
member.remarks: Function literals and local functions are bound inside the body that declares them, so they are part of that body, as they are part of their containing method's operation block in Roslyn. A field's initializer is a body of its own, owned by the field, as a Roslyn field-initializer block is. Top-level statements have no owning symbol and are not dispatched to body actions.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.BoundNodeAnalysisContext
member.summary: The context passed to bound-node actions — the counterpart of Roslyn's OperationAnalysisContext, with standing in for IOperation (ADR-0169). may be null for synthesized nodes; report locations against the nearest anchored ancestor via when it is.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.CompilationAnalysisContext

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.CompilationStartAnalysisContext
member.summary: The context for callbacks: exposes the compilation and the same registration surface, plus compilation-end registration, so per-compilation state can be shared between actions (Roslyn's CompilationStartAnalysisContext).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.DiagnosticSuppressionMap
member.summary:
ADR-0175 (issues #3820 / #3824): the source-level, scoped analyzer suppressions declared by @SuppressDiagnostic("ID", …) annotations in a compilation's syntax trees.
A suppression's scope is the span of the syntactic construct it annotates — a declaration for the attribute form, the {..} of the block form. A diagnostic is suppressed when its primary location falls inside a scope naming its ID; the same diagnostic reported anywhere else in the same file still surfaces.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpAnalyzerDriver
member.summary: Runs s over a bound compilation (ADR-0169). Dispatch order: initialize → compilation-start actions → syntax-tree actions and a kind-bucketed syntax walk per tree → symbol actions over declared symbols → a kind-bucketed bound-tree walk per function body → semantic-model actions per tree → compilation-end and compilation actions. Execution is sequential; an analyzer that throws is disabled for the rest of the run (GS9300), and one that exceeds the optional time budget is disabled with GS9302.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpAnalyzerDriver.DispatchingBoundTreeWalker
member.summary: Walks a bound body dispatching bound-node actions from the registry's kind buckets.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpAnalyzerDriver.DispatchingSyntaxWalker
member.summary: Walks a syntax tree dispatching node actions from the registry's kind buckets.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpAnalyzerHost
member.summary: Loads analyzer assemblies (gsc's /gsanalyzer:, the language server's project analyzer set) and runs them through (ADR-0169). Each assembly loads in its own whose resolution unifies GSharp.Core (and anything already loaded in the default context) to the host's copies, so analyzer-declared types are identity-compatible with the driver's.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpAnalyzerHost.AnalyzerLoadContext
member.summary: A collectible load context that resolves any assembly already loaded in the default context (GSharp.Core, the BCL) to the host's copy and probes next to the analyzer assembly for its private dependencies.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers.GSharpDiagnosticAnalyzer
member.summary: Base class for G# diagnostic analyzers (ADR-0169). The counterpart of Roslyn's DiagnosticAnalyzer: implementations declare the rules they can produce via and register callbacks in . Concrete analyzers must also carry and expose a parameterless constructor to be discoverable by the host.

member.summary: Marks a concrete for discovery by the analyzer host (ADR-0169). The counterpart of Roslyn's [DiagnosticAnalyzer(...)]; G# has a single language, so there is no language argument.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.AccessPath
member.summary: ADR-0069 addendum / issue #1180: the key the smart-cast flow analysis uses to record a narrowing. It identifies the storage location whose runtime type a successful test has proven, generalising the original key to also cover a stable member-access path — a chain of immutable members read through a stable receiver (for example x.shape or this.box.lid).
member.remarks:
An is the pair (, ). The root is the variable the chain starts at (a local, parameter, the receiver/this parameter, or a read-only top-level let); the members are the immutable field / property symbols or imported CLR members read in order, outermost last. A path with an empty list denotes a plain variable narrowing and is equivalent to the historical key — hence the implicit conversion from so the existing variable-keyed call-sites continue to compile unchanged.
Equality is structural: two paths are equal when they share the same root symbol and equal member identities. This lets analysis re-derive an equal key every time it re-binds the same access expression.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.AliasDerivedSnapshot`1
member.summary: One immutable value derived from a scope's type aliases, together with the inputs it was derived from. A scope stores the pair behind one reference, so a reader never sees a value that belongs to different inputs.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.AnonymousTypeCache
member.summary: Per-compile-pass cache of synthesized anonymous-class types (issue #2224, per the repo owner's design comment on that issue). Mirrors Roslyn's anonymous-type cache: two anonymous-class literals (object { let ... }) with the same member names, in the same order, and the same member types unify to the SAME synthesized within one compile pass, so their instances share a single synthesized backing type exactly like two new { ... } expressions of the same shape share one <>f__AnonymousType in Roslyn.
