member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BackwardJumpSpan
member.summary: The backward-jump span of a function (ADR-0213 section 11): the run of consecutive statements, in one statement list, from the statement that holds the earliest label that a later goto targets through the statement that holds the last such goto.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BackwardJumpSpans
member.summary: Computes the backward-jump span of a function body from syntax alone (ADR-0213 section 11). Slice L0 computes the span and counts it. Nothing consumes it yet.
member.remarks: Participants follow rule J8. A goto at an unreachable point (after an unconditional exit with no label between, in the same statement list) is not a participant. A goto that leaves a try whose finally ends in an unconditional exit, with the label outside that try, is not one either. A goto that the walker cannot rule out counts, which only adds kills. A nested function literal has its own labels and is not walked. The function returns one span for the body, from the lowest statement list that holds every participant (disjoint spans may be merged, section 11).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BackwardJumpSpans.Step
member.summary: A statement list on the path from the function body to a node, with the index of the statement that leads to the node.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Binder.PendingUserGenericConstraintCheck
member.summary: Issues #4089/#4090: one G#-declared generic TYPE-CLAUSE construction whose constraint check has been recorded but not yet answered, because at the construction site the definition's own type-parameter constraints may not be resolved yet.
member.remarks: The is captured rather than looked up at flush time: a binder's bag is its own, and a type clause bound inside a field initializer or a lambda during the declaration phase belongs to a different bag from the root binder's.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BinderContext
member.summary: Cross-cutting state shared across a single instance and (in subsequent extraction PRs) the components a composes — MemberLookup, ConversionClassifier, OverloadResolver, and so on.
member.remarks: PR-B-1 introduces this type as the foundation for the Binder decomposition described in the repository-level decomposition plan. No methods are moved in this PR; only the cross-cutting state that downstream extractions will need to consume via constructor injection is centralised here. State that is deliberately not on : the per-binder (it is per-binder, not cross- cutting), the pending interface-implementation checks list (declaration- specific; moves in PR-B-8), and the static readonly attribute-target hashsets (they are constants).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BindingServices
member.summary: State that is keyed by the binding pass (the reference set, the imports and the referencing syntax tree) and not by one body (ADR-0203 section 4, issue #5140).
member.remarks:
One instance lives on the root of a binding pass and is reached through . Every built over that scope chain, one per body, shares it, so a view computed for one body is reused by the next body with the same key instead of being rebuilt per body.
Each cache keeps exactly one entry and the same validation key that it had when it lived on the per-body : a different key recomputes the entry, so a body never sees an import view built for another file or another import list. Nothing here is enumerated in hash order. An independent-body worker scope owns its own instance (see ) and never touches the coordinator's. Only one thread binds against a given root scope.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BlittableDetector
member.summary: Recursively determines whether a G# type is "blittable" — has the same bit-for-bit representation in managed and unmanaged memory — using the rules defined in ADR-0093 §2 (issue #759). The result drives the PInvokeBinder decision to accept a struct or class in a P/Invoke signature without a per-field @MarshalAs.
member.remarks: Primitive integers / floats / nint / nuint and raw pointers (*T) are blittable. A user struct is blittable iff every instance field is blittable. A class is blittable iff it carries an explicit @StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential|Explicit) annotation and every field is blittable; this matches the CLR's "formatted class" concept and is the prerequisite for marshalling a class instance by-reference across the P/Invoke boundary. Imported CLR struct types are classified from their metadata layout and instance fields. This works for both runtime types and types loaded through a , and avoids treating marshalable structs containing managed references as blittable.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BodyFacts
member.summary:
Issue #5131: facts about one bound body, computed once per body object. Each fact is a pure function of the immutable bound tree, so every consumer of the same body object reads one answer instead of walking the tree again. A body is keyed by reference; a rewritten body is a new object and is computed on its own.
An entry lives as long as its body. A slot is filled under the entry's lock, so concurrent callers compute a fact once, and a walk that throws leaves the slot empty. The measurement counters bodyfacts.*-walks and bodyfacts.*-reuses report which happened.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundAwaitExpression
member.summary: Bound await expression (Phase 5.1 / ADR-0023). At runtime the operand is a (or ); the expression yields the unwrapped result type.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundAwaitForRangeStatement
member.summary: Phase 5.8 / ADR-0023: bound form of await for v := range stream { ... }. The stream operand is an IAsyncEnumerable[T]; the value variable is typed as T. The interpreter realizes the loop by reflection on GetAsyncEnumerator/MoveNextAsync/Current/ DisposeAsync, blocking on each underlying ValueTask via GetAwaiter().GetResult() (the same synchronous-await idiom Phase 5.1 uses for plain await). The async-aware lowering and emit are deferred.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundAwaitSequencePoint
member.summary: Hidden sequence-point marker emitted around async await suspension points. Emits a single nop opcode, giving a future PDB writer a definite IL offset to anchor a hidden (0xfeefee) sequence point on.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBaseClassCallExpression
member.summary: Issue #986: a base-class call expression of the form base.Method(args) (and the bracketed base[BaseClass].Method(args) form). Lets an override delegate to the nearest base class's virtual implementation non-virtually — exactly like C# base.M(...). The emitter lowers this to ldarg.0 + a non-virtual call instance R BaseClass::Method(...); the interpreter dispatches directly to the base method body without re-entering the derived type's v-table (which would recurse infinitely).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBaseInterfaceCallExpression
member.summary: ADR-0091 / issue #757: an explicit-base interface call expression of the form base[IFoo].Method(args). Lets a class member delegate to a specific interface's inherited default method (DIM) body, either to disambiguate a diamond (ADR-0085 GS0318) or to augment a default from inside an override. The emitter lowers this to a non-virtual call instance R IFoo::Method(...); the interpreter dispatches directly to the interface method body without re-entering the implementer's v-table.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBinaryExpression
member.summary: Bound binary expression.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBinaryOperationExpression
member.summary: The shape shared by every bound node that applies a BINARY OPERATOR to two operands (ADR-0169, issue #3920).
member.remarks:
G# binds a == b to two different nodes depending on where the operator comes from: when it is one of the language's built-in operators, and when it resolves to an op_Equality-style operator method on a CLR or same-compilation type. Both are "a binary operation" to anything reasoning about the program rather than about codegen — Roslyn models the pair as one IBinaryOperation.
Without a shared shape an analyzer registered for binary operations has to know the split and cast twice, and one that does not know it silently sees half the program: GSA0002 police reflection comparisons, whose operands are IMPORTED by construction, and so matched exactly none of the code it exists for. This base is the analyzer-facing answer; the concrete nodes and their values are unchanged, so nothing in lowering or emit is affected.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBinaryOperator

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBinaryPattern

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBodyCache
member.summary: ADR-0105 (Phase 1) — a per-project cache of lowered member bodies keyed by a stable, content-addressed identity rather than by symbol object reference, syntax-node reference, or source span.
member.remarks: The cache key is conceptually (stableMemberId, bodyHash): stableMemberId is position-independent: source file path, owning package, containing-type path (if any) and the member's name + parameter-type signature (via ). It deliberately depends on none of: a symbol object reference, a reference, or a — all of which shift when earlier text changes. bodyHash is a content hash (SHA-256) of the member body's source text. Any change to the body — including whitespace — produces a different hash and therefore a miss. This is intentionally conservative: over-invalidation only costs a re-bind, whereas under-invalidation would be a correctness bug. Soundness gate (critical — read ADR-0105 "Stable symbol identity" and "Determinism"). A lowered body references symbols drawn from a particular : the member's own parameters and locals, the sibling functions/types it calls, and so on. Splicing such a body into a different compilation is only sound if those referenced symbol instances are the exact instances that compilation uses (the emitter and binder key members by reference identity, not by signature). ADR-0105 Phase 2 establishes that identity: a body-only, single-file edit produces a new that reuses the prior compilation's symbol instances (the edited file's declarations are re-pointed at the freshly-parsed syntax via ; every other file's symbols flow through unchanged). Because the symbol instances survive across the edit, the soundness gate is the symbol identity of the member: a cached body is reused only when the member symbol presented on lookup is the same instance that produced the stored body () on the member). On the from-scratch / full-rebuild path every member is a fresh instance, so the gate correctly forces a re-bind there (a stale-symbol splice can never occur). This replaces Phase 1's -reference gate, which never hit across compilations because each one allocated fresh symbols. The cached entry carries both the lowered and the per-body diagnostics, so reuse reproduces diagnostics exactly. This type is thread-safe. A compilation chain owns one cache (ADR-0212 §8): creates it and the successor factories pass it on. A one-shot snapshot compilation never shares it, because its symbols are new objects and every lookup would miss the identity gate while every store would evict the live entry.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundBodyCacheKey
member.summary: ADR-0105 (Phase 1) — the stable, content-addressed key of a cached member body: a (position-independent member identity) paired with a (content hash of the body's source text). Equality and hashing are value-based and use only these two strings, never a symbol or reference, so a key is identical across re-parses of byte-identical text and differs whenever the body changes.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCallExpression
member.summary: Bound call expression.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCallOperationExpression
member.summary: The shape shared by every bound node that CALLS a method (ADR-0169, issue #3920).
member.remarks:
G# binds a call to a different node for each callee provenance — same-compilation static and instance, imported static and instance, constrained static-virtual, base-interface, and raw CLR static. Roslyn models all of them as one IInvocationOperation.
The split is a codegen distinction, not a program-meaning one, and an analyzer that does not know it silently sees a fraction of the calls in the program. Covering only the first three left receiver.Method() — the most ordinary call there is, a BoundUserInstanceCallExpression — invisible to every migrated invocation rule (PR #3968 review). The concrete nodes and their values are unchanged.
Two call shapes deliberately stay outside this base because they have no callee symbol to report: BoundIndirectCallExpression invokes a delegate VALUE, and BoundBaseClassCallExpression's property-accessor form carries neither a FunctionSymbol nor a MethodInfo. Constructor calls are excluded by design — Roslyn models those as ObjectCreation, not Invocation.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundCatchClause
member.summary: Bound catch clause attached to a .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrBinaryOperatorExpression
member.summary: User-defined binary operator resolved to a public static operator method, identified by C#-style operator name (e.g. op_Addition, op_Equality). Stream C lets GSharp source write a + b against operator-bearing CLR types such as TimeSpan, BigInteger, or System.Numerics.Vector2, resolved via (a reflection ).
member.remarks: Issue #2388: this node is ALSO reused for the nullable-lifted form of a same-compilation struct's Stream D user-defined operator (func (a T) operator ==(b T) bool) when one or both operands are a value-type Nullable<T> — that scenario has no reflection available at bind time (the declaring struct is still -backed), so carries the same-compilation instead. Exactly one of / is non-null. Sharing one node type lets the nullable-lifting machinery in SlotPlanner / MethodBodyEmitter.Operators (LiftedBinarySlots / EmitLiftedNullableClrBinary) drive both the imported-CLR-type and same-compilation-struct cases uniformly.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrConstructorCallExpression

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrConversionCallExpression
member.summary: User-defined conversion resolved to a public static op_Implicit or op_Explicit, carried by either for imported CLR types or for same-compilation user types. Stream E lets GSharp source assign across types that carry CLR conversion operators (e.g. System.Numerics.BigInteger ↔ int, System.Half ↔ float).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrEventSubscriptionExpression
member.summary: Stream B′: adds (+=) or removes (-=) a delegate handler from a CLR . When is null, the event is static; otherwise it is dispatched against the receiver value. The expression evaluates to .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrIndexAssignmentExpression
member.summary: Assigns through a CLR indexer (Phase 4 exit). Example: d["key"] = 42 where d is a Dictionary[string, int]. Interpreter-only — the evaluator calls Indexer.SetValue(target, value, args). The target is either a simple variable reference or, after closure-boxing lowering, an arbitrary expression (issue #618).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrIndexExpression
member.summary: Reads a value through a CLR indexer (Phase 4 exit). Example: d["key"] where d is a Dictionary[string, int]. Interpreter-only — the evaluator calls Indexer.GetValue(target, args).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrMethodGroupExpression
member.summary: Issue #337: a bare reference to a CLR member method (a method group on an imported static type — e.g. Console.WriteLine, Int32.Parse — or on a CLR instance receiver — e.g. sb.Append) used in a value context. Unlike a named G# function group (), the target overload cannot be selected until the expected delegate signature is known, so the binder first produces the unresolved form carrying every name-matching overload, then BindConversion picks the single best against the target delegate's Invoke signature and produces the resolved form. The emitter materializes the resolved form as ldnull/ldftn (static) or [dup] ldftn/ldvirtftn over the captured receiver (instance), followed by a newobj of the target delegate.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrPropertyAccessExpression
member.summary: Reads a public or on a CLR receiver. When is null, the member is static; otherwise it is dispatched against the instance receiver. Examples: lst.Count, sb.Length, kvp.Key, Console.Out (static, since Stream B).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrPropertyAssignmentExpression
member.summary: Writes a public or on a CLR receiver. When is null, the member is static; otherwise it is an instance member dispatched against the receiver. Stream B parity for imported-type member writes; mirrors the read-only .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrStaticCallExpression
member.summary: Represents a call to a CLR static method resolved at compile time via . Used by synthesized code (state-machine bodies) where no user-facing symbol exists.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundClrUnaryOperatorExpression
member.summary: User-defined unary operator on an imported CLR type, resolved to a public static (op_UnaryNegation, op_UnaryPlus, op_LogicalNot, op_OnesComplement). Stream C companion to .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundConditionalAddressExpression
member.summary: ADR-0061: bound representation of a call-site-only conditional lvalue address-of expression of the form <cond> ? <lvalue> : <lvalue>. Produced by the binder from a at the payload of a ref-kind modifier (ref/out/in) or as the operand of &. The result type is T& (a ) where T is the common pointee type of the two branches. Lowered to a CIL branch around two address-of forms feeding a single managed pointer onto the evaluation stack.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundConditionalExpression
member.summary: ADR-0062: bound representation of a general two-arm conditional (ternary) expression of the form <cond> ? <ifTrue> : <ifFalse>. Only one arm is evaluated at runtime. The result type is the common type chosen by the binder using identity / implicit conversion / numeric tie-break rules; both arm values are already converted to that result type.

member.summary: ADR-0089 / issue #755: a constrained static-virtual interface call site of the form T.Method(args) where T is a generic type-parameter constrained to . member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundFixedStatement

Lowers in the emitter to the CLR pinned-local pattern, mirroring C# fixed (T* p = expr) { … }; the pin is released (the pinned local is nulled) on normal block exit.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundInterpolatedStringExpression
member.summary: ADR-0055 (Phase 2): a first-class bound node for an interpolated string literal. Carries an ordered list of — each either literal text or a { value, alignment, format } hole — so that the tree-walk interpreter and the IL emitter can render the string correctly and identically from one representation.
member.remarks:
The node's static type is always . Lowering happens late, not in the binder:
the historical tree-walking evaluator (deleted in ADR-0156 Phase 3c) rendered the node directly
via composite formatting (alignment + format, current culture), and
the IL emitter lowers it (issue #368) to the C# 10
System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler pattern: construct the? handler, call AppendLiteral/ AppendFormatted<T> in order, then ToStringAndClear(). Routing lowering late (rather than the legacy eager binder +-chain) also fixes the #366 memory-unsafe-IL crash class.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundStackAllocExpression
member.summary:
ADR-0124 / issues #1024, #1057, #1041: a bound stack-allocation expression in G#-style array grammar stackalloc [n]T. Lowers to a CIL localloc over n * sizeof(T) bytes. The result is either a System.Span<T> constructed over the allocated memory (the safe form, = false) or the raw T* pointer to that memory (the unsafe form, = true, only produced inside an unsafe context with an unmanaged-pointer target type).
When an initializer is present (stackalloc [n]T{a, b, …} or the count-inferred stackalloc []T{a, b, …}), is the initializer length and carries the (element-typed, conversion-bound) values that are stored into the block via scaled indirect writes (issue #1041).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.BoundTreeWalker
member.summary: Abstract bound-tree visitor that, by default, recurses into every child of every node — mirroring the coverage of . Subclasses override VisitX methods to observe nodes of interest; calling base.VisitX(node) continues the traversal into the node's children. Issue #418 (P1-3): pre-emit allocator walkers were bespoke switch statements with default: return branches, which silently dropped many kinds (tuple literals, map literals, null-conditional access, CLR calls/indexers/properties, indirect calls, switch expressions, etc.). Any literal/append nested inside a dropped context reached EmitStructLiteral without a pre-allocated slot and threw at emit time. Using this default- recurse walker eliminates the entire class of bug.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ByRefStorageMatching
member.summary:
Issue #4422: decides whether the storage behind a by-reference argument (&x at a ref, out or in parameter of a G# callee) has the parameter's type.
A by-reference argument passes the storage location itself, so its type must be the parameter type, with no conversion. Reference nullability is the one exception: []?int32 and []int32, or List[string?] and List[string], are one runtime type, and C# accepts such an argument with only a nullability warning. A value-type int32? is Nullable<int32>, a different runtime type, and is never accepted for int32.
This replaces ) at the by-ref gates. The shared comparer answers a boolean equivalence question for declarations, inference, overload identity, and related signature decisions. This matcher additionally records the direction and nesting of reference-nullability differences for GS0612, and normalizes equivalent imported-array and native-slice storage views.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.CallCandidateRecorder
member.summary: Collects the candidate sets that overload resolution considers while one call binds, so that the bound call can carry them (ADR-0212 slice S4, SemanticModel.GetMemberGroup).
member.remarks: One frame per call being bound. The resolver stores a set it has already built, so no candidate is copied during binding. A frame ends with the call: the call keeps the widest set that holds a candidate of the called method's name, the later one on a tie. A probe (a lambda parameter inference, a conversion operator search) names other methods or holds fewer candidates. A thread owns its frames, so parallel body binding needs no lock.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ChannelRuntimeBinder
member.summary: Lowers channel operations onto the Gsharp.Runtime.Channels runtime (ADR-0174 D1/D2/D12) as ordinary imported calls and constructions, so the proven imported-member emit path handles metadata, symbolic type arguments, and load contexts, and no channel IL is hand-rolled.

item.description: chan[T](n) → new Gsharp.Concurrency.Chan<T>(n), typed as the runtime class so
<-ch → ChannelOps.Receive<T>(ch, default) (zero on closed, no exception);
let v, ok = <-ch → ChannelOps.Receive2<T>(ch, default), a (T, bool) tuple;
close (member Close() on a chan[T]) → ChannelOps.Close<T>(ch).

remarks.para: The overload is chosen by the handle's direction: a chan[T] or a constructed Chan<T> uses the Channel<T> overloads, an in chan[T] the ChannelReader<T> ones, an out chan[T] the ChannelWriter<T> ones. The runtime dispatches the fast path versus the documented foreign-channel fallback (D2's matrix).
The blocking Receive/Send forms are the Phase 2 target; Phase 3's suspension rewriter swaps them for the …Async forms and awaits.

Element types are projected onto the reference set exactly as an explicit generic type argument is (issue #320): a CLR-backed element is mapped into the resolver's load context; a same-compilation or type-parameter element closes the generic over an object placeholder and travels as a symbolic type argument the emitter re-encodes.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ClosureCaptureLegalityChecker
member.summary: PR #4273 (Copilot review, on the fix for issue #4271): the single legality check that decides whether a captured variable may be hoisted into a heap-allocated closure environment at all. Originally inline (and duplicated) at 's two function-literal capture call sites; extracted here so and the go-statement closure path (StatementBinder.BindGoStatement) apply the exact same rules — the review's own request ("apply the same capture-legality validation to BoundGoStatement closures, ideally through a shared validator").
member.remarks: Every rejection here shares the same root cause: the CLR gives no way to keep a managed pointer, a ref struct, or an unmanaged fixed pointer alive inside a heap-allocated (or, for go, thread-pool- scheduled) display class once the capturing closure may run after the enclosing statement/call returns.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ClrIndexerResolutionOutcome

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ClrOperatorResolution
member.summary: Stream C helper: resolves binary and unary operator values to CLR operator method names (op_Addition, op_Equality, op_UnaryNegation, ...) and performs the actual public-static lookup across the two operand types. The "better function member" tie-break is delegated to so user-defined operators participate in the same conversion ranking as method calls and constructors (Stream A).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ConditionalReturnNarrowing
member.summary:
Issue #3802: applies the [return: NotNullIfNotNull(nameof(p))] conditional post-condition of an imported (CLR) method at a CALL SITE.
The BCL declares members such as [return: NotNullIfNotNull(nameof(path))] static string? ChangeExtension(string? path, string? extension). The declared return type really is nullable — narrowing it in the declaration reader would restore the imported-nullability unsoundness that #3705 family 2 removed — but at any call whose path argument is known non-null, the result is known non-null too. That makes this a FLOW FACT about one call, which is why it lives here and is applied to the bound call node's type rather than to .
The narrowing is deliberately conservative: it fires only when the argument bound at the named parameter's position has a statically non-nullable type. A nullable argument (including one that has not been flow-narrowed to non-null) leaves the declared nullable return in place, so Path.ChangeExtension(maybeNil, ".gs") is still rejected where a non-nullable string is required.

member.summary: PR-B-3: the binder-side facade that wraps the pure ) type-pair classifier in the diagnostic-emitting BindConversion family, and owns the CLR-parameter conversion, method-group → delegate resolution, ref-kind validation, default-value attachment, optional-argument appending, conditional-ref argument shaping, and user-defined implicit-conversion lookup that previously lived directly on .
member.remarks:
This type is the binder-side wrapper: it consumes for the diagnostics bag and reference resolver, and for delegate-type / member shape probes. It never back-references ; the few callbacks it needs (re-binding a sub-expression, the interpolated-string / function-literal adapters) are injected through narrow seams in the constructor.
The pure value-shaped type in Conversion.cs is unchanged and continues to expose the static ) entry point. This class merely wraps that classifier with the diagnostic emission and bound-tree shaping previously embedded in .
The slice-conversion-set-equals-array-conversion-set rule (#570) landed in Conversion.Classify (PR 6.5) via a dedicated arm and the ClrTypeUtilities.ImplementsInterfaceByName cross-context helper. The lifted T → T? conversion (#571) and the related Wave-3 architectural fixes from ~/gsharp-bug-overview.md will land in this class in a follow-up PR after the full Binder decomposition is complete.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.DefiniteAssignmentAnalyzer
member.summary:
Definite-assignment analysis. Two consumers share the same forward "must be assigned" data-flow:
ADR-0060 items #4 and #5 (ref-kind parameters; formerly the RefKindDefiniteAssignmentAnalyzer):
GS0238 — every out parameter must be definitely assigned on every path that reaches a return (or falls off the function end for void bodies); GS0239 — a variable passed via ref (NOT out) at a call site must be definitely assigned at that point.
ADR-0159 / issue #3316 (no-zero-value locals): GS0522 — a local whose type has no usable zero
value (today: a bare chan T slot, see ) may be declared without an initializer, but every USE reachable by a path without a preceding assignment is an error — C#'s CS0165 model. Locals whose types have sound zero values (ints, maps and the other magic collections post-ADR-0159, structs, …) keep their documented zero-value initialization and are deliberately NOT flow-checked. The analyzer builds a for the function body (and, recursively, for the body of every try/catch/finally, select case, scope, fixed, and await-for-range block it contains — issue #1642: the outer CFG treats those as single opaque statements, see 's BasicBlockBuilder) and runs a forward "must be assigned" data-flow with intersect-meet over predecessors. Reads are checked before writes apply within a basic block, so a single statement that both writes and reads the same variable is classified using the set at the start of that statement.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.DefiniteAssignmentAnalyzer.ExpressionFlowContext

member.summary: One entry of : the result of probing one region from one input state.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.DefiniteAssignmentAnalyzer.TrackedLocals
member.summary: The no-zero-value locals of one function analysis, which also owns that analysis's cache of nested-region probes (issue #5284). A probe is a diagnostics-free re-analysis of a try, catch, finally, switch-arm, fixed or await-for body; an enclosing region's fixed point repeats the probe with an unchanged input state on later iterations. One instance serves one call on one thread, so nothing here is shared between threads.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.EnumOperatorTable
member.summary: Single declarative source for every C# §11.10 enum operator rule. Adding a new operator group is a one-row change in this table — no new arm in BoundBinaryOperator.cs or BoundUnaryOperator.cs.
member.remarks: Issues #534 (bitwise), #574 (comparison), and bug-overview item 6.6 (architectural unification + §11.10 arithmetic gaps) are all serviced through this table. The emit-side signed-vs-unsigned dispatch () is also co-located here so the connection between "binder accepted enum1 < enum2" and "emitter chose clt_un" lives in one place. Why this pattern is NOT extended to user-defined operators (issue #613 investigation): The EnumOperatorTable is a closed-world static ruleset — all enums share the same §11.10 operator set, so a declarative dictionary is ideal. User-defined operators (Streams C and D) are open-world dynamic dispatch: each type declares its own operator set via CLR op_* methods or GSharp receiver-form operator declarations. They resolve through method lookup (reflection for imported CLR types in ; symbol-table lookup for GSharp types via StructSymbol.TryGetMethodIncludingInherited), not through type-shape predicate matching. Both paths are already centralized at single call sites in ExpressionBinder.Operators.cs and produce different bound node types (BoundCallExpression / BoundClrBinaryOperatorExpression) than the built-in operators this table feeds. A shared base class or generic OperatorLiftTable would add abstraction without reducing duplication, since no duplication exists to consolidate.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.IncrementalGlobalScopeReuse
member.summary: ADR-0105 Phase 2 — establishes stable symbol identity across a language-server edit so a body-only change to a single file re-binds only that file's member bodies while every unchanged file's bodies are served from the .
member.remarks:
The reuse vehicle is the previous compilation's itself: when exactly one file changed and that change is a body-only edit (package, imports, type aliases, fields, enum members, delegate signatures, and every declaration signature are byte-identical; only the statement blocks of body-bearing members differ), the new compilation reuses the prior wholesale. Every symbol instance therefore survives the edit, which is exactly the identity the 's soundness gate and the emitter (which keys members by reference) require. The edited file's reused symbols are re-pointed at the freshly parsed syntax tree so that re-binding their bodies binds the new text and reports diagnostics at the new spans, and so language-server navigation resolves to current source. This covers every body-bearing member kind: top-level functions, struct/class instance and static methods, interface default / static-virtual / private helper methods (), constructors (), destructors (), computed-property accessor bodies (), and explicit event accessor bodies (). The owning struct and interface type symbols are re-pointed too (, ), as are source field declarations (), enums (), and delegates (). Re-binding of every re-pointed body is forced by passing the edited tree as a dirtyTree to ); because each body's backing syntax now belongs to the dirty tree, the per-body cache read is bypassed and the body binds fresh. Explicit imports and aliases are also re-pointed, so the binder's per-file import filter sees the edited tree (). Structural identity is proven by a skeleton diff: blanking the body blocks of every body-bearing member and requiring the remaining text to be byte-identical guarantees that the only change is inside bodies and that the set and order of every declaration is unchanged — so each reused member can be re-pointed by positional mapping. Anything that is not a member body — a field initializer, an auto-property, an enum member, a delegate signature, any member signature, an import, a type alias, the package clause — stays in the skeleton, so any change to it makes the skeletons differ and forces a full rebuild (correctness-preserving over-invalidation). The single remaining outright bail is a file containing top-level statements (the synthesized
$ entry-point body): that body is bound from rather than from a member-declaration node, so it is not member-addressable for re-pointing. Such a file falls back to a full rebuild.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.MagicCollectionZeroValue
member.summary: Issue #3310 / ADR-0159: sound zero values for the magic collection types. A declared-without-initializer slot of type map[K, V], []T, [N]T, [,]T, or sequence[T] binds an empty instance instead of a null reference, making the bare (non-?) spelling's non-null promise true (the #2262 NRE class). The synthesized expressions reuse the existing literal machinery — with zero entries (symbolic Dictionary2 ctor MemberRefs per #1481/#3306 for open K/V) and (cref:BoundArrayCreationExpression) (symbolic newarr element token for open element types) — so generic contexts are covered by already-verified emit paths. chan T is deliberately NOT synthesized here: an auto-created channel has no sensible default (buffer size, ownership), so channel slots have no zero value at all (see (cref:RequiresExplicitInitializer)). Globals and fields must initialize explicitly (GS0520); locals may declare freely and are instead flow-checked at use sites by (cref:DefiniteAssignmentAnalyzer) (GS0522, issue #3316). Issue #3319: a value-type struct slot (local, global, or field) recurses into its OWN declared fields — and transitively into any struct-typed field's fields — synthesizing a that carries a for every field whose type (directly or through nested struct composition) needs a sound empty-instance default. This is a NEW bound-tree node per call (never a shared/reused instance — see the aliasing guard in MethodBodyPlanner's struct-literal slot planner), so it composes safely with every existing consumer of : the bare var s S declaration path (StatementBinder.BindVariableDeclaration), and the struct/class field-default probes in DeclarationBinder.Structs.cs. Deliberately does NOT run any of the nested struct's own EXPLICIT field initializers — matching the existing "value-struct default bypasses ctors" honesty clause, generalized: a bare declaration only ever gets CLR defaults plus sound magic-collection zero values, at any nesting depth, never arbitrary initializer side effects. Class-typed fields are reference-typed and are NOT recursed into here — a null class reference is the correct, unchanged CLR default; only a nested VALUE-type struct's fields are embedded by value and need this treatment. Inline structs (ADR-0033's fixed synthesized-member layout, see #3219) are excluded from recursion for the same reason #3219 excludes them from ctor synthesis. Issue #3329: the same-assembly recursion above depends on being reachable and fully bound — true for a struct declared in THIS compilation, but not for a struct symbol rebuilt from reflection over an ALREADY-EMITTED type in another assembly (or, for the REPL, an earlier submission): that reconstruction (see ImportedTypeSymbol.BuildSemanticAggregate) resolves each field's type via raw CLR reflection (TypeSymbol.FromClrType), which cannot by itself distinguish a slice from a same-CLR-shaped fixed array, or know that a nested struct-typed field needs its own zero-value probe at all. / and the GSharp.MagicCollectionFields assembly-metadata marker (see ) close that gap: the DECLARING compilation records, per struct, which fields (magic-collection OR struct-typed-and-recursively-magic) need synthesis, so an IMPORTING compilation's struct literal can reconstruct the identical zero value without ever needing the declaring compilation's own bound tree.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingComparison
member.summary: The comparison mode of ADR-0208 section 19, PR 1. When the environment variable GSHARP_NARROWING_COMPARE names a file, the binder compares the shadow join of the narrowing flow state with what the current passes lifted, and records every disagreement. The mode reads the binder state and never changes it, so the compiler output is the same with and without it.
member.remarks: Bodies bind in parallel, so entries collect under a lock. The file is written once, at process exit, with the entries sorted by their text. That order does not depend on thread timing. The join report goes to the named file. The read report goes to the same name with the extension .reads. A join line has the fields file:line, path, old type, new type and row. A read line has the fields file:line, path, declared type, shadow type and kind. A tab character separates the fields. A test can capture entries in memory instead: is local to the calling context.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingConstructTable
member.summary: The closed construct table of ADR-0208 section 8. Each concrete type has one entry. A type that the table does not list has the effect Call, the conservative default. A test in Core.Tests enumerates every concrete BoundNode type of the assembly against this table, so a new kind cannot be added without choosing its effect.
member.remarks: Some kinds have two effects, which depend on facts that the type does not carry. The table gives the more destructive one. Examples: is Call because a conversion can be user-defined, and is MemberWrite while a setter with user code is also a Call. The post-lowering kinds (spill sequences and state-machine helpers) never reach the binder walkers and are Call. is Join because it carries &&, || and ??.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingEffectClass
member.summary: How one kind of bound node changes the narrowing state (ADR-0208 section 8, construct table).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingFrame
member.summary: One frame of the narrowing stack: a map from access path to narrowed type (ADR-0208 section 2). A frame behaves like the dictionary it wraps, and tells the stack that holds it about every write, so that the stack can keep a in step with the frames.
member.remarks: A frame that is not on a stack has no owner and notifies nobody. The same frame can be on a stack more than once.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingFrameStack
member.summary: The stack of narrowing frames of one binder (ADR-0208 section 2), and the that it keeps in step with the frames.
member.remarks: The state holds, for each path, the type of the innermost frame that has the path. Each push, pop and frame write updates the state for the paths it touches, so the state is threaded beside the frames and is not computed on demand. compares it with a fresh projection.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingParity
member.summary: The parity assertion of ADR-0208 section 19, PR 2 slice 1. When it is on, every narrowed-type query compares the state that the frame stack threads with a fresh projection of the frames, and with the answer of the frame walk, and throws when they differ. A difference means that a write reached a frame without being seen.
member.remarks: The environment variable GSHARP_NARROWING_PARITY set to 1 turns it on for a process. and turn it on in the calling context for a test.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingSpeculation

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NarrowingState
member.summary: The narrowing facts that hold at one program point (ADR-0208 sections 6 and 7).
member.remarks: The state is a value. Each operation returns a new state, so a branch can keep the state it started from. Entries keep insertion order, and no result depends on hash order. Equality is structural and ignores entry order. A state holds two kinds of fact: a narrowed type for each access path, and the set of variables that definitely hold an external callable. Both kinds join the same way. Nothing in the binder consumes this type yet (ADR-0208 section 19, PR 1).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NativeSliceSuspensionAnalyzer

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.NumericWideningLattice
member.summary: Issue #1482: the single authoritative source of truth for the implicit numeric-widening lattice (ADR-0044 / C# §6.1.2 numeric promotions). Keyed by source CLR → set of target CLR full names that the source implicitly, losslessly widens to.
member.remarks:
Previously this lattice was hand-copied into three places — the conversion classifier (), the overload "better conversion" ranker (), and the binary-operator binder. The copies had already DIVERGED: the overload-resolution copy was missing every native-width integer (nint/nuint = System.IntPtr/ System.UIntPtr) row, so Conversion.Classify and overload "better conversion target" ranking disagreed about native-int widening.
All consumers now query this one table so the relation cannot drift again. The data mirrors C# §6.1.2 plus the ADR-0044 inclusion of decimal as a widening target for every integral source, and the C# native-integer rules: nint widens to int64/single/double/decimal; nuint widens to uint64/single/double/decimal; and the narrower integral and char sources widen into nint/nuint exactly as they do in C#.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ObliviousScope
member.summary: ADR-0186 §9: declaring obliviousness in G# source. T! is unspellable, so a source declaration cannot write a platform type. It does not need to: obliviousness is a property of a scope, exactly as in C# ( plus #nullable), rendered in G#'s idiom — the compilation switch --nullability=oblivious plus the compiler-intrinsic @Oblivious / @NullabilityEnabled annotations. The nearest enclosing annotation wins; with none, the compilation switch answers. So a parameter's annotation beats its function's, a function's beats its type's, and any declaration-level annotation beats the compilation default. Which positions a scope reaches. ADR-0186 open question 12 is the reason this is one rule applied in one place rather than a list of declaration kinds. An oblivious scope makes the top-level position of every type written inside it as the type of a slot a value lives in T!, when that position is an unadorned reference type: the declared type of a field, property, event, parameter (including a receiver and a lambda parameter), function or lambda return, local (var/let), for-range variable, and inline out declaration. Nested positions stay as written (owner decision, 2026-09-25, amending step 5's answer to open question 12): a type argument, an array/slice/map/channel element, a tuple element, and a function type's parameters and return keep exactly the nullability they are spelled with, in declarations and in expressions alike. So List[string] in an oblivious scope is List[string]!, not List[string!]!, and []string is []!string. ADR-0186 §3 rule 3 gives C[T] and C[T!] no conversion in either direction, so wrapping nested positions made every container handed between an oblivious scope and an enabled declaration an error (the ADR-0186 §9 note records the measurement). Imported oblivious metadata is not affected: its nested positions still read T! per §2. The top level of a type written for any other reason is left alone, because it is not a slot: a construction target, a cast, as, typeof, sizeof, default, an attribute type, a type alias. So is the top level of a test-introduced binding — a type pattern, a catch variable, an if let / guard let / while let binding: ADR-0186 §4 is explicit that such a binding is non-null because the test succeeded, not because anything was checked, so T! there would state less than the language already knows. Two places are exempt outright, nested positions included (see IsExempt): a conformance clause — a base-type or interface list, a generic constraint, or an explicit-interface qualifier — and the signature of a native-interop function (@DllImport / @LibraryImport). The mapping goes through , the single cell of ADR-0136's table that ADR-0186 changes: T! in every platform-types mode, and ADR-0136's T? under --nullability=enabled, where nothing constructs a . An oblivious G# declaration therefore reads, inside its own compilation, exactly as its emitted metadata reads back from another one (ADR-0186 §8) — the "two readers disagreeing about one declaration" defect (#3705 family 2) cannot open between them.

member.summary: Helpers for validating and extracting P/Invoke metadata from a function declaration. member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PartialMethodMerger
member.summary: ADR-0192 / issue #4301: collapses the declaring and implementing parts of each partial func into a single , so the rest of the compiler sees one ordinary method. This is the member-level analogue of , and it runs immediately after it, over the declarations that pre-pass returns. The division of labour is what makes the feature cheap: ADR-0144's type merge has already concatenated every part's member list into one node, so the two parts of a partial method — which may come from different files — are simply two entries in the same Methods (or SharedBlock.Methods) array by the time this runs. Collapsing them to one entry means the ~2 000-line body binder, every Set* installer, FunctionSymbol, and the emitter are untouched: one node yields one symbol yields one MethodDef. The merged node is built from the implementing part, so its — and therefore the file-scoped import scope its body and signature bind in — is the implementing part's file. The declaring part contributes its annotations (whose own child nodes retain their own tree, so they bind against the declaring file's imports, exactly as ADR-0144 §E establishes for composed children) and any modifier it alone states.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PartialMethodMerger.MethodKey
member.summary: The identity of a partial method for grouping purposes: its name, its generic arity, and its parameter TYPES. Parameter types are part of the key because two partial methods of the same name may be distinct overloads — partial func F(x int32); and partial func F(x string) { … } are two unmatched declarations, not one mismatched pair, and keying on the name alone would pair them and then report a signature conflict the user never wrote.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PartialTypeMerger
member.summary: ADR-0144 / issue #2201: pre-pass that merges multiple partial declarations of the same type (same package + name) into ONE synthetic declaration node before the two-phase shell/body binder runs. Grouping, deterministic part ordering (ADR-0066), and head-consistency validation (GS0475-GS0483) all happen here; the existing DeclareStructShell/BindStructDeclarationBody (and interface equivalents) then run once per merged node, exactly as they do for a lone declaration. This keeps the body binder, installers, symbols, and emitter untouched: one merged node yields one shell, one symbol, and one TypeDef.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PatternBinder
member.summary: PR-B-5: the binder-side facade that owns the per-pattern-kind binding methods. Routes to the appropriate per-kind binder and produces the corresponding . Wraps , , , , and that previously lived directly on .
member.remarks:
This type is the binder-side wrapper: it consumes for the diagnostics bag and the (mutable) Scope used by to declare the bound variable, and for the relational-pattern argument conversion. It never back-references ; the callbacks it needs (re-binding a sub-expression for constant patterns, binding a type clause for type patterns, and the nil-literal test for nullable constant patterns) are injected through narrow seams in the constructor — the same pattern established by in PR-B-3 and in PR-B-4.
Switch-statement / switch-expression glue (binding the discriminant, walking the arm list, exhaustiveness reporting via , narrowing-frame management, per-arm result conversion) deliberately stays on for this PR and will land in PR-B-7 (StatementBinder) and PR-B-9 (ExpressionBinder). This class focuses strictly on per-pattern binding so its surface area stays small.
The discard-pattern case is inlined in the pattern-dispatch method's dispatch — it has no logic beyond constructing a BoundDiscardPattern with the discriminant type, so it leaves with the dispatch method rather than warranting a per-kind helper. is already a separate file and is not touched.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PatternVariableSymbol
member.summary: ADR-0166: a read-only local introduced by a designation in a boolean is pattern (value is string text, value is { } item, value is var captured, values is [..rest]). The pattern assigns it exactly once, and the binder makes it visible only in regions the match dominates, so every read observes the assigned value. Closure lowering relies on that invariant to capture the variable by value instead of hoisting it into a heap cell.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PatternVariables
member.summary: ADR-0166: the flow facts of pattern variables introduced by boolean is expressions. A pattern variable is definitely assigned exactly when its pattern matched, so the binder scopes it to the regions where the enclosing condition is known to be true (or false, through negation). This helper computes those "when true" / "when false" sets structurally over a bound condition, mirroring C#'s definite-assignment rules for &&, ||, !, and pattern matches, and mirroring the smart-cast classifiers (ClassifyTypeTestNarrowing) that already walk the same shapes.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.PlatformCoercion
member.summary: ADR-0186 §4: the runtime nil check inserted wherever a platform value T! is coerced into a destination whose declared type is a non-null reference type. One rule, one implementation. §4's specification is a single sentence, and the ADR is emphatic that the list of concrete sites beneath it is consequence, not an additional list. Keeping the insertion in one helper is how that stays true: a second copy is how ADR-0136's carve-out predicates began, and failure mode 1 of the catalogue is literally "the read path and the call path drifted". The check reuses the existing !! lowering (dup; brtrue; pop; newobj NullReferenceException; throw) rather than inventing a node kind, which is deliberate: it inherits every lowering stage, spiller and rewriter the operator already passes through, and the exception type stays the one existing catch clauses in both G# and interop code already expect. The whole improvement over an unattributed NRE is the message.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.ProtectedReceiverDiagnostics
member.summary:
Issue #4453: enforces the C# CS1540 receiver rule for protected source instance members (fields, properties, methods and events) over a bound body. A derived class may reach such a member only through a receiver of its own type or a subtype; a base- or sibling-typed receiver is reported as GS0379.
The binder has many member-access paths (reads, writes, compound assignment, calls, method groups, event subscriptions, object initializers, …), and each already runs the class-level check. Rather than thread the receiver through every one of them, this walker visits every node that references an instance member through a receiver, so a new binder path cannot skip the rule. The decision itself is , which reports nothing the class-level check already rejected.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefKind

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefStructAsyncLivenessAnalyzer
member.summary: Issue #2350: replaces the coarse, syntax-only rejection of a by-ref-like (ref struct) local declared anywhere in an async function (the original issue #367 rule in ) with a sound per-local dataflow analysis. A by-ref-like local is legal in an async function as long as it is never live across an await suspension point: never hoists a by-ref-like local into the generated state machine's fields (the CLR forbids a by-ref-like field), so such a local is reset to its CLR default on every fresh MoveNext call. A value that survives a suspension therefore silently loses its contents unless it can never actually be observed live across one — which is exactly what this analyzer proves before allowing the declaration. This is a backward ("may be live") dataflow, dual to the forward "must be assigned" analysis in , over the same infrastructure: loops are fully expanded into real graph edges (so a per-iteration local's liveness is checked correctly across back-edges), while try, select, scope, fixed, and pattern-switch bodies are opaque to the outer graph and are recursively re-analyzed here, mirroring 's ProcessTryStatement/ProcessFixedStatement/etc. shape. try/finally gets special "ambient live" treatment: an exception can transfer control from any point inside a try body straight to its catch clauses or finally block, so whatever is live entering those handlers is folded into an ambient live set applied to every block of the try body — not just its formal exit — catching the "unsafe finally interaction" case where a local assigned before an await in the try body is later read in finally. Capture (a closure capturing a by-ref-like variable) and general escape (returning/storing a by-ref-like value beyond its safe scope) are already covered by pre-existing, unrelated machinery ('s unconditional by-ref-like capture rejection and 's ADR-0058 escape-scope tracking) and are untouched by this analyzer. Issue #4222 reuses this same machinery for native let ref/var ref alias locals ( other than , tracked separately from by-ref-like locals since the two have different symbol shapes — see ) and extends the suspension concept from "await" to "await or yield", so it now also runs for (non-async) iterator functions. Two differences from the by-ref-like treatment: an alias is "interesting" regardless of function kind (an alias in a plain iterator is in scope for #4222; a by-ref-like local in a plain iterator remains the pre-existing blanket rejection in , untouched here — see ), and an assignment *through* an alias (alias = 42) is a use of the alias, not a kill of it, unlike overwriting a by-ref-like value local outright.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefStructAsyncLivenessAnalyzer.AsyncLambdaScopeFinder
member.summary: Finds every async or iterator function-literal expression (lambda or local function) nested anywhere in a bound tree — regardless of whether the enclosing scope itself is async/iterator — and runs an independent for each one's own body. A function literal is an opaque leaf to the base (its body is a separate lexical scope), so this walker must manually continue into to discover further-nested async/iterator lambdas/local functions.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefStructAsyncLivenessAnalyzer.InterestingLocalCollector
member.summary: Collects every local declared directly within a scope that this analyzer must track: always a native ref-alias local (issue #4222), and — only when says the enclosing scope is async — a by-ref-like (ref struct) local too (issue #2350; a by-ref-like local in a plain, non-async iterator stays out of this analyzer's scope, since it remains the pre-existing blanket rejection in ). Does not recurse into nested function-literal bodies, since those are a separate lexical/hoisting scope with their own, independently analyzed liveness — see .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RefStructAsyncLivenessAnalyzer.ReadAndAwaitCollector
member.summary: Collects reads (restricted to a fixed "interesting" set of variables) and whether an await occurs anywhere within one expression subtree. Relies on 's default recursion for everything except assignment targets (correctly not a read) and function-literal bodies (a separate scope, opaque by design).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RegionEffectScanner
member.summary: The region walker of ADR-0213 section 7 (rules W1 to W7). It maps each syntax kind to its effect class through and composes the effects of a region from syntax alone, before the region is bound. It resolves no name: the consumer resolves the names of a record at the entry scope of the region.
member.remarks: Slice L0 only measures with the walker. Nothing in the binder consumes a record yet. A scanner serves one function body: it caches the record of each loop statement, so a nested loop is walked once (section 7, composition and cost). member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.RendezvousBatchAnalyzer
member.summary: ADR-0174 D10 / GS0562: a batch operation on a rendezvous channel.
member.remarks: chan[T]() means one value in flight by definition, so ReceiveBatch on it degenerates to that many sequential rendezvous transfers. That is correct and pointless — the whole point of the batch surface is to amortize one lock acquisition and one park across many elements — so it is worth saying out loud. The check runs over the bound bodies rather than at the call site because a batch call reaches the binder through several paths (an extension on a directional handle, an instance method on Chan[T]) and the question is about the receiver's declaration, not the call.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SharedClassNormalizer
member.summary:
ADR-0195 / issue #4674: hands the binder a shared class in the one shape it already binds. The author writes the members directly in the class body (shared class Helpers { func Twice(x int32) int32 { … } }) and every one of them is shared; the binder has a single path for a type's shared members, which reads them from the type's . So this pass returns a copy of such a declaration whose body members sit in a shared block (built from the class's own shared modifier and braces) and whose instance member lists are empty. It never mutates its input: the parsed tree is reused across compilations and read by the language server, formatter and analyzers, which all see the source as written.
It also rejects what a shared class cannot hold: an init(…) constructor, a primary constructor, a deinit, a shared { } block of its own (GS0617) and a base class or interface (GS0619).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SmartCastStability
member.summary: ADR-0069 addendum / issue #1180: the Kotlin-parity stability rules that decide whether a member-access chain may participate in smart-cast flow narrowing. A narrowing on a member path is only sound when every link is guaranteed not to change between the test and the use — i.e. an immutable member (no settable setter, no custom getter, not overridable) declared in the current compilation, read through a stable receiver chain.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SubmissionBindingOptions
member.summary: ADR-0156 Phase 2: options that put a compilation into interactive submission mode — prior-submission metadata binding, a per-submission default package, replayed session imports, and trailing-expression value capture for the REPL echo.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SubmissionGlobalTypeProjection
member.summary: Issue #3308 / ADR-0156 Phase 2: reverse projection for prior-submission globals whose declared G# type is a compiler-magic wrapper kind. Later cells bind a prior cell's top-level global through its emitted CLR field (the #3186 submission-as-metadata seam), so the field's type surfaces as the CLR projection of the declared type — e.g. a chan T global surfaces as imported System.Threading.Channels.Channel[T]. Kinds whose operations type-check against the magic symbol itself ( for <-/select/close, / for len/cap/append) lose those operations cross-cell unless the CLR projection is mapped back to the magic symbol. The reverse projection is steered by the declaring submission's source-side type (recorded in its ), which settles otherwise-ambiguous CLR shapes (a T[] field is a slice or a fixed array depending on the declaration, and the fixed length exists only source-side); component types are rebuilt from the CURRENT compilation's metadata view of the field (never from the prior compilation's symbols, whose CLR identities belong to a different resolver). Kinds that already round-trip correctly through the seam are intentionally left on their existing paths: maps bind through the erased IDictionary2 member family, sequences through the duck-typed enumerable probes, and function-typed globals through the delegate-shape mapping in the call binder (#3184).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SubmissionImports
member.summary: ADR-0156 Phase 2: the ordered (newest-first) set of prior interactive submissions a REPL submission binds against. Each prior submission is a real emitted assembly reachable through the compilation's ; its top-level functions and globals live as static members of its per-package <Program> container and its user types as ordinary CLR types under the submission's package namespace. Name lookup walks submissions newest-first so a redefinition in a later cell shadows earlier cells, matching the historical evaluator scope-chain semantics.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SubmissionReference
member.summary: One prior interactive submission: its emitted assembly identity, the package (namespace) its members were emitted under, and the source-side global scope recording what it declared (names, kinds, and read-only flags — used to steer metadata lookup without reflection scans).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Suspension.LockRegions
member.summary: Shape predicates the suspension passes share.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Suspension.SuspendingCallRewriter
member.summary: The rewrite half of . Inside one body it (1) retypes every call to a function the pass just marked suspending from R to ValueTask[R] and completes it — an implicit await when the containing function suspends or is async, the blocking root bridge otherwise; (2) turns a bridge the binder emitted into an await when the containing function turned out to suspend; and (3) reports GS0558 for every bridge that remains outside the synthesized entry point and outside go operands. Function-literal bodies are rewritten with the literal's own function as the container.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Suspension.SuspensionInference
member.summary: ADR-0174 D4: the coloring is inferred. After every body is bound, this pass finds the functions that perform a suspension point — a channel operation, or a call to a function that suspends — and marks them , iterating to a fixed point over the call graph so mutual recursion converges. It then rewrites every body so a call to a newly-suspending function is typed ValueTask[R] and completed the way the binder completes a call to a declared suspend func: an implicit await inside a suspending or async body, a blocking root bridge (GS0558) elsewhere.
member.remarks:
Inference stops at the ADR's boundaries: the synthesized entry point (the root that blocks once), async functions (their task is observable), virtual, abstract and overriding methods, interface members and their implementations, constructors, accessors, operators, P/Invoke stubs, unsafe functions and bodies containing a fixed pin (raw pointers cannot live in a state machine), iterators, Dispose, and function literals. A suspension point inside one of those keeps the blocking lowering; GS0558 names the residual blocking bridges. A go operand does not color its caller, and a channel operation inside a lock body does not either (the monitor is thread-affine).
Discrimination witnesses (ADR-0154): a mutant that runs a single pass instead of iterating breaks SuspensionInferenceTests.MutualRecursion_Converges; a mutant that colors through a go operand breaks SuspensionInferenceTests.GoOperand_DoesNotColorTheCaller; a mutant that skips the lambda-body rewrite breaks Adr0174InferredSuspensionEmitTests.Lambda_CallingAnInferredFunction_Runs.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Suspension.SuspensionPointCollector
member.summary: Collects one body's suspension facts for : whether it performs a suspension point directly — a channel operation bound onto the blocking facade, or a blocking bridge to a suspending callee — and which same-compilation functions it calls. A go operand is skipped (the goroutine, not the caller, suspends), a lock body is skipped (its operations stay blocking), and a function literal is a leaf (it is its own function).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.Suspension.SuspensionPointCollector.Facts
member.summary: One body's suspension facts.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SyntaxAnchoringWalker
member.summary: Fills the anchor of every statement, expression, and pattern that construction and the bind dispatchers left unanchored, inheriting the nearest anchored ancestor's syntax (ADR-0169). Runs once per member body at the end of Binder.BindProgram, so the pre-lowering-visible guarantees a non-null anchor on every dispatchable node — synthesized lowering nodes report at their enclosing construct, mirroring how the emitter anchors hidden sequence points. Idempotent: an existing anchor is never replaced.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.SynthesizedRefDelegateCache
member.summary: Issue #3501 A2: per-compile-pass cache of compiler-synthesized delegate types backing native function types with ref/out/in parameters. System.Func/System.Action cannot carry by-ref type arguments, so a function type spelled (ref int32) -> void (or the natural type of a literal func(ref n int32) { … }) lowers to a sealed MulticastDelegate TypeDef with the matching by-ref Invoke signature — the exact shape ADR-0059 named delegates already emit and every call/conversion path already supports. Two spellings of the same shape (same ref kinds, parameter types, and return type) unify to the SAME synthesized symbol within one compile pass, mirroring .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.TupleElementNameValidation

Reports GS0540 for a name used more than once and GS0542 for reserved names — ItemN at any position other than N (the correct-position spelling is allowed, matching C#), and Rest (used by the CLR encoding for arity ≥ 8 nesting).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Binding.VariadicCarriers
member.summary: ADR-0173 / issue #3627: generalized variadic carriers. A variadic parameter name ...X now mirrors C#13 params collections: when the type written after ... is itself a supported COLLECTION shape, it is the parameter's CARRIER type (the exact type the callee receives and the CLR signature declares) and its single type argument is the element type — ...List[int32] ≡ C# params List<int>, ...ReadOnlySpan[int32] ≡ params ReadOnlySpan<int>, ...[]T ≡ params T[]. Any other type keeps the ADR-0101 meaning: it is the ELEMENT type and the implicit carrier is the slice (...int32 ≡ params int[]).
member.remarks: Supported non-array carriers (exactly the shapes cs2gs's call-site lowering has historically allowlisted, plus the two span types): List<T>, IEnumerable<T>, ICollection<T>, IList<T>, IReadOnlyCollection<T>, IReadOnlyList<T>, Span<T>, ReadOnlySpan<T>. The array family emits [ParamArrayAttribute] as before; every other carrier emits C#13's [ParamCollectionAttribute].

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Documentation.AssemblyDocumentationProvider
member.summary: Loads and indexes the companion .xml documentation file for a single resolved assembly, exposing a DocID → lookup (ADR-0057 §6).
member.remarks: Instances are obtained through , which caches one provider per so a given assembly's (potentially large) xml is discovered and parsed at most once per process. Parsing is lazy — the file is read on the first lookup, not at construction — and XXE-safe (DTD processing prohibited, no external resolver, bounded size). Any failure (missing file, malformed xml, oversize) degrades silently to "docs unavailable": ingestion never fails a hover or a build. Thread safety: all lookup state is immutable after construction. The per-assembly cache is documented thread-safe for concurrent callers, and the wrapping the index uses so concurrent first-time lookups produce exactly one instance. That dictionary is read-only after publication: writes to a local result before publishing it through the Lazy, and only performs reads — which are safe for concurrent readers when no writer is present. The provider is therefore safe to share across concurrent hover requests.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.AsyncMethodSteppingInfo
member.summary: ADR-0174 P3-8: the IL offsets a debugger needs to step through an async or suspending state machine's MoveNext — the Portable PDB "Async Method Stepping Information" blob (kind 54FD2AC5-E925-401A-9C2A-F94F171072F8). Each await contributes the offset where the method yields (the hidden marker before the state save and AwaitUnsafeOnCompleted) and the offset where it resumes (the hidden marker after the resume dispatch); the catch handler offset is the start of the outermost catch that routes a fault to the builder, or -1 when there is none.
member.param: IL offset of the outermost catch handler, or -1.
One (yield, resume) offset pair per await, in state order.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.BclMember
member.summary: Reflection lookups for members of well-known BCL types the emitter lowers against — Channel<T>, Task, ValueTask<T>, CancellationToken, the async-method-builder shapes, and so on.
member.remarks:
Every lookup here asserts rather than returns null. The member's absence would mean the target framework's core library does not declare a member the language's own lowering is defined in terms of — malformed metadata, not a condition any emit path can recover from. Asserting at the lookup states that once, instead of at each of the ~50 emit sites that consume a result.
This is deliberately NOT the right tool for a lookup that can legitimately miss: a record's protected copy constructor (invisible to the public-only )), or an imported type that may or may not declare a parameterless constructor. Those keep their own null test and their own diagnostic.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ClosureEmitter
member.summary: Closure-environment orchestration and display-class synthesis. Owns the metadata that describes every lambda / go capture environment emitted into the assembly, and owns the rewriter that lowers a captured- variable read inside a lambda body into a this.field access against the synthesized display class.
member.remarks: PR-E-9 introduces this component. Per the decomposition plan, the closure-emit surface is split between two host types in the pre-refactor source — exactly as PR-E-5 handled the conversion-emit surface: Stateless, top-level orchestration on (SynthesizeClosures, SynthesizeGoClosures, SynthesizeDisplayClass) plus the nested helper classes (, , ) and the closure-state caches (, , , , ). These move here. Body-emit-internal closure methods inside BodyEmitter (EmitFunctionLiteral [two overloads], EmitMethodGroup, EmitFunctionToDelegateConversion, EmitFunctionToNamedDelegateConversion, EmitFunctionLiteralToNamedDelegate, EmitMethodGroupToNamedDelegate, EmitClrEventSubscription, EmitUserEventSubscription, EmitCapturedVariableLoad) that reference BodyEmitter's private il, outer, locals, parameters, enclosingClosure fields and call back into EmitExpression / EmitLoadVariable for every captured value and method-group target. These are deferred to PR-E-11 MethodBodyEmitter, where BodyEmitter is promoted to its own top-level type with its own partials (including MethodBodyEmitter.Closures.cs). Moving them in PR-E-9 would require widening BodyEmitter's private surface to expose all of those collaborators through an IBodyEmitContext interface, only to take it apart again in PR-E-11. This is the same Option B playbook PR-E-5 used for the same reason. Future home of the #567 / #503 unifying fix. The plan calls this PR out as "the structural home for the eventual #567 + #503 unifying fix" — closure-environment emission unified with display-class emission. The fix itself is deferred until PR-E-11 promotes BodyEmitter to MethodBodyEmitter, because the fix needs to span both the synthesis side (here) and the emit-time side (EmitCapturedVariableLoad / EmitFunctionLiteral). Putting the synthesis side in its own type today is the prerequisite that lets PR-E-11 land that cross-cutting fix in one focused diff without rummaging through the root emitter. What stays on : The lambdaBodies dictionary. It is cross-cutting (populated by closure synthesis here AND by every state-machine synthesizer in E-10), and the root emitter walks it from EmitFunction. Keeping it on the root means E-9 and the future E-10 both write into it via the constructor-injected dictionary reference, and the root keeps its existing read paths unchanged. The plan explicitly nominates this option ("Pick (a) for this PR — it keeps the diff minimal"). RegisterConstructedTypeAliases. It is a single-use caller of that walks the root's program-function bodies and lambda bodies and writes into the ; it is not closure orchestration in its own right. The collector type moves here (it is closure-emit-side per PR-E-4's deferral note); the caller stays. The state-machine synthesizers (SynthesizeIteratorStateMachines, SynthesizeAsyncIteratorStateMachines, SynthesizeAsyncLambdaStateMachines) and their nested classes (IteratorStateMachineInfo, IteratorEmitContext). These move with PR-E-10 StateMachineEmitter. They share the field and append to from the root; both are exposed publicly here so the still-on-root SM methods (and, once moved, the future StateMachineEmitter) can mutate them directly. Like every other PR-E-* component, is internal sealed and constructor-injected. It receives the same , , and trio as its peers, plus the for go-statement capture discovery and a shared reference to the root's lambdaBodies dictionary so it can register every synthesized closure-Invoke body without taking a hard back-reference to .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ClrInterfaceClosure
member.summary: The imported CLR interfaces a G# type's metadata lists: every declared CLR interface followed by its transitive base interfaces, as csc emits them (issue #4601). It is the single source for both the type's InterfaceImpl rows and the MethodImpl rows of the interfaces' static-virtual slots (issue #4614), so the two can never disagree about which interfaces the type implements.
member.remarks: Each interface is keyed on its emitted metadata identity, so it appears once and two distinct interfaces are never conflated. Concrete interfaces use the assembly-qualified comparer the emitter's own TypeRef/TypeSpec token caches use (a same-named interface from another assembly is a different interface). Symbolic generic ones (IList[Shape], IList[T]) use the bytes of their TypeSpec signature (a display name would conflate Shape with Outer.Shape).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.CustomAttributeEncoder
