member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.EmbeddedAttributeSource
member.summary:
Issue #4922: the compiler-embedded copies of NullableAttribute and NullableContextAttribute.
A target framework that publishes neither attribute (netstandard2.0, .NET Framework) can only carry nullability metadata if the emitted assembly declares the two attribute types itself, as csc does: internal (and, being closed classes, CLR-sealed) types in System.Runtime.CompilerServices, marked with Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.EmbeddedAttribute and CompilerGenerated. Binding the metadata to a type in the assembly keeps it loadable on every runtime, where a reference to the host's System.Private.CoreLib (issue #4921) is not.
The copies are produced as ordinary G# source in a synthetic syntax tree that joins the binding of the compilation, so they flow through the normal declaration, member-row planning and emission pipeline. then binds the nullability stamps to the declared constructors, exactly as it would to a copy the user wrote. Nothing is added when the target publishes the attribute, when the source already declares it, or when the target is not a downlevel framework.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.EmitContext
member.summary: Cross-cutting state shared across a single instance and (in subsequent extraction PRs) the components a composes — MetadataTokenCache, WellKnownReferences, SlotPlanner, and so on.
member.remarks: PR-E-1 introduces this type as the foundation for the decomposition described in the repository-level decomposition plan. No methods are moved in this PR; only the cross-cutting state that downstream extractions will need to consume via constructor injection is centralised here. State that is deliberately not on yet: the per-emitter handle/cache dictionaries (move in PR-E-2 MetadataTokenCache), the lazily-resolved BCL member references (move in PR-E-3 WellKnownReferences), the closure/state-machine bookkeeping (move in PR-E-9 / PR-E-10), and the async/iterator rewriter plans (logically per-emitter, set once via the static entry point).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.EmitDiagnosticException
member.summary: A typed exception that the emit pipeline wraps around internal failures so that the ) catch boundary can anchor the resulting GS9998 diagnostic at the offending source construct rather than a hard-coded (1,1,1,1).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ExplicitInterfaceMetadataNaming
member.summary: ADR-0149: an explicit-interface qualifier clause (func (IFoo) M(...) / prop (IFoo) P T) keeps its declared, source-visible name plain — diagnostics, reflection Name lookups by the ordinary member name, and hand-authored G# source never see anything but M / P. But the CLR metadata name of the emitted MethodDef/PropertyDef row (and, for a property, its get_/set_ accessor MethodDefs) DOES need to be collision-free: two explicit implementations of DIFFERENT interfaces that share a member name (the entire point of the feature) would otherwise emit two MethodDefs with the identical name and signature in the same type — legal at the raw metadata level, but indistinguishable to reflection APIs that look a member up by name (and needlessly fragile). This helper synthesizes a qualified, C#-explicit-impl-style metadata name (Interface.Member, or Package.Interface.Member when the interface has a package/namespace) that is unique per (interface, member) slot — the same uniqueness key (GS0495) already enforces at the source level, so within a single valid compilation this synthesized name can never collide with another such synthesized name, nor (since it always contains at least one ., which no plain G# identifier can contain) with any ordinary member's name.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MaxStackTracker
member.summary: Computes the .maxstack value (maximum evaluation-stack depth) for an emitted method body so that ) no longer falls back to the format default of 8 (issue #1490).
member.remarks: The naïve default of 8 produces invalid IL for any body whose evaluation-stack peak exceeds eight slots (a call/constructor with many arguments, a deeply nested arithmetic expression, an async MoveNext state machine, …). ilverify rejects such bodies with StackOverflow because the computed depth exceeds the declared .maxstack. A precise peak cannot be recovered from the emitted IL bytes alone: call/callvirt/newobj/calli are varpop — their pop count depends on the callee signature, which is not encoded in the opcode stream. gsc emits these instructions from ~40 scattered sites (some via il.Call(handle), some via il.OpCode(Callvirt)+il.Token(handle)), so threading the per-call argument count through every site would be invasive and error-prone. Instead this helper computes a provably-correct upper bound on the peak that is independent of control flow and of the (unknown) call pop counts: the sum, over every emitted instruction, of the number of values that instruction pushes. Because every IL instruction has a net stack delta of at most +1 (even dup, which pops one and pushes two), and verifiable IL has a single, path- independent stack height at each offset, the height at any reachable offset equals the sum of net deltas along a simple (acyclic) path to it, which never exceeds the total number of pushes in the body. The bound is therefore guaranteed to be ≥ the true peak and is never an under-estimate, so the emitted .maxstack is always valid. varpop call instructions are counted as pushing one value (their maximum), which keeps the bound conservative without needing the callee argument count.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataRowInterner
member.summary: Adds MemberRef, TypeSpec and MethodSpec rows to one and returns the existing row when an identical row was added before (issue #5172).
member.remarks:
The emitter's token caches are keyed by symbol or reflection identity, so two equal references that arrive as separate objects each used to add a row; about three quarters of those rows repeated an earlier row. A row is identified by its encoded form: the parent, name and signature handles of a MemberRef, the signature blob of a TypeSpec, and the method and instantiation blob of a MethodSpec. MetadataBuilder.GetOrAddString and GetOrAddBlob already return one handle per distinct content, so equal handles mean equal rows.
Determinism: the first occurrence keeps its row number and later occurrences return it. The dictionaries are only probed, never enumerated, so no output order depends on hash iteration order.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodBodyEmitter.UnconstrainedNullableLiftPlan
member.summary: Issue #3226: the per-call plan for lifting an unconstrained generic instantiation to Nullable<X>. A user generic function with an UNCONSTRAINED type parameter T and a parameter declared T? (e.g. the receiver of func (self T?) MyOrElse[T](fb T) T) encodes every T/T? slot as the bare MVAR !!T ( models unconstrained T? as a metadata-only reference annotation). That erasure is only sound for reference instantiations: a value-type call site would push a live Nullable<X> into an X-typed slot (invalid IL for primitives, silent nil-loss for user structs). The lift instead instantiates the MethodSpec at Nullable<X> — so the T? slot really holds a nullable, and the body's box-probe nil checks work because boxing a Nullable<X> yields a null reference for the empty value — wrapping bare-X arguments (newobj Nullable<X>::.ctor) and unwrapping a bare-T return (box + unbox.any, loud on the impossible nil).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MethodNullabilityPlan
member.summary:
Issue #4988: the single decision of how a method signature's declared types become [NullableContext] / [Nullable] metadata.
The per-position byte arrays come from ; this type adds what only a whole signature can decide, the way csc does: the method-level context byte (the most common byte across the return and the parameters), and which positions still need their own attribute under it. It also says whether the return position needs a sequence-0 Param row, which a MethodDef only has when something is attached to it.
Every MethodDef gsc mints plans its signature here, whatever declaration produced it: a method with or without a body, an interface slot, a property or event accessor, a delegate's Invoke, a constructor, or a member the compiler synthesizes. Before #4988 each of those paths made the decision itself, and the paths that never created a return row (an interface method without a body, a delegate's Invoke, an auto-property getter) exported Task[Token?] as Task[Token].
member.remarks: Fields, properties and events have no member-level context: their rows read the enclosing type's [NullableContext(1)], so they use against .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.MvidPEBuilder
member.summary: A subclass that adds a .mvid PE section to the output assembly. MSBuild's CopyRefAssembly task uses a lightweight reader (MvidReader) that looks for this section to quickly extract the module version identifier without loading full metadata. Without it, the task cannot determine whether the public API surface has changed between builds and falls back to always copying, defeating incremental build gating for downstream consumers.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.NullableFlagsBuilder
member.summary:
Issue #834: computes the C#-compatible [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.NullableAttribute] byte array (DFS pre-order) for a GSharp . The bytes use the well-known encoding:
0 — oblivious (no nullability information), including a non-Nullable closed generic value type's
leading placeholder and a struct-constrained generic parameter's slot.
1 — not-annotated (non-nullable reference / open type parameter).
2 — annotated (nullable reference / nullable open type parameter).
Layout mirrors the C# compiler: byte 0 belongs to the outer type when that type occupies a reference-type position. Closed generic value types contribute a leading oblivious placeholder byte before their arguments, except metadata-transparent Nullable<T>, which contributes only T's subtree. Struct-constrained generic parameters contribute one oblivious slot. Non-generic value types contribute none (matches )).
Per-position attributes are intentionally narrow — they only describe what C#'s nullable flow analysis needs to see at a parameter / return slot. They do not depend on whether the receiver, declaring type, or assembly has its own NullableContextAttribute; the per-slot byte array overrides any surrounding context.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.PinningShapes
member.summary: Issue #3755 (issue #3705, family 3 — the load-context family; the remedy is #3754's): the two well-known members the fixed / pointer lowering emits calls to, resolved from the compilation's reference closure rather than from the SDK hosting gsc. Both sites used to read their member off a live host typeof — typeof(System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe).GetMethods(...) and typeof(string).GetMethod("GetPinnableReference", ...) — so they answered for the framework gsc is running on, never for the framework it is compiling against. #3755 ranked them as hygiene on the grounds that "none of the types involved is plausibly absent from a target framework". Measured against the targeting packs that ship in the .NET SDK, that ranking does not hold for either of them: System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe is absent from NETStandard.Library.Ref/2.1.0 altogether — it is a NuGet package there, not part of the framework. #3729's ImportedMemberRefFactory.GetTypeReference projection therefore had nothing to project onto and fell back to the host type, so every fixed statement compiled against a netstandard2.x closure emitted a TypeRef scoped to the host's System.Private.CoreLib and the compile reported success. That is #3730's defect exactly, on a different member. System.String is present in every target, but String.GetPinnableReference() is not: it arrived in netstandard2.1's successors and is absent from NETStandard.Library.Ref/2.1.0. A member-level absence is invisible to the "is the type absent?" reasoning #3755 ranked by, and no type projection can repair it — the emitted MemberRef named a method the target does not declare, and the failure surfaced as a MissingMethodException at the target's runtime. Resolution goes through ) and member probes compare with rather than host typeof identity, because the resolved members are MetadataLoadContext types on every real /reference: compile. A target that provides neither is reported as GS0546 instead of emitting a reference its runtime cannot resolve.

The internal analyzer rule GSA0004 (EmitCacheKeyRemapScopeAnalyzer, ADR-0147) enforces the invariant: any Dictionary/ConcurrentDictionary field or property in this namespace whose key mentions a symbol type and whose value is a scope-sensitive handle must include a in its key.

member.summary: One loan of a pooled item. Release it once the item is no longer used.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.ScratchPool`1
member.summary: A small thread-safe free list of reusable scratch objects. One pool belongs to one emitter, so no state is shared between compilations.
member.remarks: Rent gives out a . Only the first Release of a lease resets the item and makes it free again, so a second release (even after another caller rented the same item) does nothing. The item is reset while its releaser is the only owner, before it is published to the free list. An item that reset rejects (for example one that kept too much storage) is dropped. An item whose lease is never released (for example after an exception that skips the caller's cleanup) is simply collected; the pool never holds a partly used item.

It receives the same , , and trio as its peers, plus the (for the shared synthesized-class counter and class-list it appends every SM class onto) and a shared reference to the root's lambdaBodies dictionary so synthesis can register the rewritten MoveNext / get_Current / etc. bodies without a hard back-reference to .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.TupleElementNamesBuilder
member.summary: ADR-0172 Phase B: computes the C#-compatible [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TupleElementNamesAttribute] string[] for a G# — a DFS pre-order walk of the type tree in which every tuple occurrence contributes its arity of entries (declared name, or null for an unnamed position) before its element subtrees are visited. member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.TypeIdentityComparer
member.summary:
Issue #420 (P3-9): compares instances by structural identity (assembly-qualified name) rather than reference equality.
The emitter resolves CLR objects through . The same logical type can be returned as two distinct instances when it is reached through different reference paths (e.g. via different MetadataLoadContext lookups for the same assembly identity, or when the same type is observed both from a directly loaded assembly and from a transitively loaded one). Reference-equality-keyed caches then mint a duplicate TypeRef row for each occurrence, producing valid but bloated metadata that tools like ILSpy render as separate rows.
Using assembly-qualified name as the identity key collapses these duplicates into a single cache entry — and therefore a single TypeRef row — without affecting types that genuinely differ.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.UserTokenResolver
member.summary: PR-E-19 (#1361): the user-type token-resolution band. Owns every method that renders a reference to a user-declared (same-compilation) generic type, interface, delegate, field, method, property accessor, or constructor into the correct ECMA-335 token — a bare TypeDef/MethodDef/ FieldDef for a non-generic declarer, or a TypeSpec-parented MemberRef (over the constructed or self-instantiation) for a generic one. Covers the user struct/interface/delegate TypeSpec producers and their memoization caches, the field/method/ctor MemberRef factories, the property-accessor and static/instance/interface method-token resolvers, the constructed-base ctor-token resolvers, the generic-user-call MethodSpec builder and its structural type-argument unifier, the non-capturing generic-lambda promotion and its ldftn token, and the symbolic-substituted-return trio the erasure-widening short-circuits on.

This is the consolidation commit the Wave-1 emitter decomposition built toward: it resolves the temporary couplings PR-E-17 (SignatureEncoder) and PR-E-18 (ImportedMemberRefFactory) left pointing into this band. Those siblings now reach the user-token resolvers directly through the root's field, and the two PR-E-17 widenings (ResolveUserStructTypeSpecArguments / ResolveDelegateTypeArguments) that had been promoted on the root are relocated / restored here.
Wired with a back-reference to the root emitter (the MethodBodyEmitter / SignatureEncoder / ImportedMemberRefFactory idiom) because the band reaches , , , the extracted and , and a few root-owned surfaces that stay put (the shared static predicates / , the async-return encoder , FindImportedMethod, and the state-machine plans / well-known refs). Direct convenience fields hold the shared / / / / read off the back-reference. Method bodies are verbatim moves; emitted PEs are byte-identical with the pre-E-19 baseline.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Emit.WellKnownReferences
member.summary: Owns every well-known BCL / that the threads through code generation — System.Object / System.ValueType TypeRefs, the Object..ctor() MemberRef, String.Concat, String.Equals, Object.Equals(object, object), Object.ToString(), Object.GetHashCode(), the System.HashCode family (Combine, Add, ToHashCode), Convert.ToString(object, IFormatProvider), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, Delegate.Combine/Remove, Interlocked.CompareExchange<T>, NotImplementedException..ctor(), NullReferenceException..ctor(), System.Attribute..ctor(), the IsReadOnlyAttribute / IsByRefLikeAttribute / ObsoleteAttribute ctors, and the stateless lookups for String.get_Length / String.get_Chars / Type.GetTypeFromHandle / Array.get_Length / Array.Copy / Nullable<T>.get_Value / Nullable<T>.get_HasValue.

PR-E-3 extracts this type as the third step of the decomposition described in the repository-level decomposition plan. The class consumes for Metadata/References/Core* access and small hooks for the dedup-cached resolvers GetTypeReference(Type) and GetMethodReference(MethodInfo) that still live on (and which themselves route through ).
Eager refs (, , ) are populated by the constructor — the emitter's EmitCore resolves the BCL Core* types onto first, then instantiates exactly once. member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Execution.EmittedProgramHost
member.summary: Shared execution host for the evaluating drivers (ADR-0156 Phase 1): compiles a with the real emitter into a , loads the PE bytes into a collectible , invokes the entry point in-process, and maps the outcome onto the drivers' exit-code protocol. Framework dependencies resolve through the default load context; user-supplied reference assemblies (/r:) resolve from their explicit paths.
member.remarks:
The program's console is the host process's console — output and input stream straight through, exactly as under dotnet exec, and callers that need capture use the process-global ) as they always have.
Cancellation is best-effort and matches the historical evaluator drivers: the token is only observed before the entry point is invoked, so an already-running program cannot be interrupted, and Ctrl+C keeps its process-default behavior in the CLI drivers.
In-process execution inherits the same hazards the tree-walking evaluator had: ) in user code terminates the driver, and threads the program spawned may outlive its entry point.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Execution.EmittedProgramResult
member.summary: The observable outcome of compiling a program to memory and executing it in-process via (ADR-0156): the emit diagnostics, the entry point's exit code, and any unhandled exception the program surfaced. Standard output and error are not captured here — the program writes to the process console exactly as an emitted executable would, so drivers stream them through unchanged.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Invariant
member.summary: Asserts a nullability invariant the compiler cannot see, in place of the null-forgiving operator.
member.remarks:
ADR-0155 requires a comment beside every ! naming the invariant that makes it safe. That works where the invariant is local and easy to state ("the enclosing if tested this"), and those sites should keep using !. It works badly where the invariant is real but non-local — a reflection result narrowed three frames up, or a value established by a sibling constructor — because an honest comment is long and a short one is the laundering the rule exists to prevent.
makes the invariant an artifact instead of a comment: it is stated once, in code, and if it is ever violated the failure names it. That turns a bare some frames later into an at the assertion, with the offending expression and the reason — which the compiler driver surfaces as a GS9998 internal error, matching how the rest of Core reports a broken invariant.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncBoundTreeQueries
member.summary: Lightweight read-only queries over a bound subtree that the async lowering passes share. None of these methods mutate the tree.
member.remarks: These helpers are intentionally implemented on top of rather than a separate visitor: the rewriter's overrides return the same node when nothing changes, so no allocation is triggered when a query merely observes nodes. This avoids adding yet another tree-walking infrastructure to the codebase while still letting each query short-circuit cheaply (see )).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncBoundTreeQueries.AwaitDetector
member.summary: Walks a subtree looking for an await, optionally memoizing per-node results (reference-keyed) so overlapping queries over the same tree reuse work instead of re-walking already-visited subtrees (issue #1625). and are the sole dispatch entry points every recursive descent in funnels through, so overriding them here is sufficient to intercept — and memoize — every node in the walk.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncCaptureWalker
member.summary: Computes the set of variables that the async state-machine rewriter must hoist into fields on the synthesized state-machine type (see ~/roslyn-async.md §5). Roslyn's production implementation runs a definite-assignment pass to hoist only locals that are live across a suspension point. GSharp's V1 takes the simpler conservative rule used by Roslyn's Debug-mode build: every parameter and every referenced user-declared local in an async method body is hoisted, regardless of live-range analysis. This may over-hoist (a strictly intra-statement scratch local that never crosses an await still becomes a field) but is always correct, never under-hoists, and avoids pulling in a full data-flow framework before the state machine itself works.
member.remarks:
Spill temps are collected into a separate, ordered field group. Rectangular-array dimensions and indices can be captured before a later suspension, so these synthesized values must survive like user locals.
Spill-temp detection is by name prefix () because GSharp does not (yet) carry a synthesized-kind tag on .
For this capture: the bound tree does not currently distinguish instance-member field access from local access at the rewriter level, so the rewriter treats every instance method as capturing this. The walker itself does not need to detect receiver references — the orchestrator sets the corresponding flag based on the kickoff method's receiver.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncCaptureWalker.HoistResult
member.summary: The set of variables to hoist onto the synthesized state-machine type for one kickoff async method.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncCaptureWalker.LambdaCaptureCollector
member.summary: Collects the set of outer-scope variables that a lambda literal — or any lambda transitively nested inside its body — captures, using only the binder-computed metadata on each literal it visits (never a lambda's own local declarations or parameter reads). Mirrors CaptureBoxingRewriter.CaptureWalker's defensive recursion (see #567) for the same reason: the binder already flattens transitive captures onto every enclosing literal (#503), so the recursion below is normally a no-op, but keeps this collector correct if that invariant ever changes.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncEmitPrecheck
member.summary: Safety-net gate that prevents the emitter from crashing on async functions whose state-machine synthesis failed (e.g. the awaitable's method-builder type could not be resolved). When state-machine synthesis succeeds — the normal path — this pass is a no-op.
member.remarks: The gate inspects which is populated by the async rewriter. A null value indicates synthesis failure and triggers a clean compile-time diagnostic rather than a runtime InvalidProgramException.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncExceptionHandlerRewriter
member.summary: Rewrites try/catch and try/finally statements whose handlers contain await into pending-exception forms that can be processed by the subsequent and passes.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncExceptionHandlerRewriter.Rewriter.DispatchArm
member.summary: One captured Pattern C exit: a discriminator value paired with the statement to re-emit (a return of the pending-return-value, or a goto to the original target) when the dispatch after the lifted finally observes that value.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncExceptionHandlerRewriter.Rewriter.ExitFunneler
member.summary: Rewrites the try body of a finally-with-await, replacing every non-fall-through exit that leaves the try (a return, or a goto/conditional-goto whose target label is outside the try) with a pending-branch capture followed by goto finallyTail. The captured exits are surfaced via so the caller can re-emit them after the lifted finally body. Implements Pattern C (issue #1484) symmetrically with the pending-exception machinery.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncExceptionHandlerRewriter.Rewriter.LabelCollector
member.summary: Collects every label DEFINED inside a statement subtree (the targets of ). The Pattern C exit funneler uses this set to decide whether a goto/conditional-goto leaves the protected region: a branch whose target label is in this set stays inside the try and must NOT run the lifted finally, whereas a branch to any other label (or a return) exits the try and is funneled.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncExceptionHandlerRewriter.Rewriter.RethrowLifter
member.summary: Replaces a lifted catch handler's own rethrow statements with ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(e).Throw() (ADR-0176).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncIteratorDetection
member.summary: Single source of truth for "is this an async iterator?" detection and element-type extraction across the async/iterator lowering pipeline.
member.remarks: Issue #1489: the async-iterator pipeline historically carried three divergent copies of this predicate. The recognised the symbolic form (issue #798) and the open form (issue #1002), while and keyed off a closed CLR IAsyncEnumerable1 / IAsyncEnumerator1 return type only. For a GENERIC async iterator (async func gen[T](x T) sequence[T]) the return type is an over an open type parameter whose is null, so the CLR-only copies failed to recognise it. The function was then mis-routed into the plain-async state-machine pass (where the method builder could not be resolved) and ultimately reported as GS0190. Routing every site through this helper keeps the three checks in lock-step so the symbolic open-generic form is recognised consistently. Issue #2786: an explicitly async iterator remains an iterator when its body has no yield; plain-async lowering would spuriously change its runtime return type to Task>.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncMethodBuilderInfo
member.summary: Resolved metadata for the BCL "async method builder" associated with an async method's declared return type. The async state-machine rewriter consumes one of these per async method to emit the kickoff body and the per-await sequence inside MoveNext.
member.remarks:
The selection rules mirror Roslyn's AsyncMethodBuilderMemberCollection.TryCreate (see ~/roslyn-async.md §1, §11 corner case 18, and Roslyn's Lowering/AsyncRewriter/AsyncMethodBuilderMemberCollection.cs):
If the method itself carries a [AsyncMethodBuilder(typeof(T))] attribute, T is the builder
(the method-level attribute takes precedence).
Otherwise, if the return type carries [AsyncMethodBuilder(typeof(T))], T is the builder. For
generic task-likes the builder is constructed with the result type via builder.MakeGenericType(resultType).
Otherwise the builder is one of the four well-known BCL types: <list type="bullet">
<item><description><c>System.Void</c> → <c>AsyncVoidMethodBuilder</c>.</description></item> <item><description><c>System.Threading.Tasks.Task</c> → <c>AsyncTaskMethodBuilder</c>.</description></item> <item><description><c>System.Threading.Tasks.Task<T></c> → <c>AsyncTaskMethodBuilder<T></c>.</description></item> <item><description><c>System.Collections.Generic.IAsyncEnumerable<T></c> / <c>System.Collections.Generic.IAsyncEnumerator<T></c> → <c>AsyncIteratorMethodBuilder</c>.</description></item> </list>
This class is a pure resolution helper. It performs no lowering and produces no diagnostics; callers that need diagnostics should check and route errors through their own diagnostic bag.
Every resolved member is declared nullable because member binding is a best-effort reflection lookup against whatever builder type the target framework supplies: a builder that does not declare the member yields null rather than an exception, and that is precisely what reports. carries for the four members every valid builder has, so a caller that checks it first needs no further guard for those; the kind-dependent members ( and the Set* methods) still need one, because which of them are required depends on .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncMethodBuilderKind
member.summary: Categorises the BCL async method builder selected for an async method (see ~/roslyn-async.md §1).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncStateMachineFieldMap
member.summary: Maps user variables and synthesized control slots to the fields on a materialized async state-machine aggregate.
member.remarks: The state-machine rewriter needs to replace local/parameter reads with field reads against the generated this receiver. This helper is the bridge between the pure model and the existing bound-tree nodes, which are keyed by .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncStateMachinePlan
member.summary: Captures the synthesized artifacts for one async kickoff method.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncStateMachineRewriteResult
member.summary: Result of running the async state-machine rewriter scaffold.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncStateMachineRewriter
member.summary: First-stage async state-machine lowering orchestrator.
member.remarks: This scaffold wires together the already-landed async emit building blocks: it creates the synthesized state-machine type, materializes the field map, allocates deterministic await resume states, and links the kickoff method to its state machine. It intentionally does not rewrite the kickoff body or relax yet; later slices consume the returned plans to build the kickoff stub and MoveNext body.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AsyncStateMachineTypeBuilder
member.summary: Pure factory that composes the foundation pieces (, , , ) into a fully populated state-machine type for one async kickoff method. The returned type carries every field the state-machine rewriter and the emitter will read: control fields (<>1__state, <>t__builder), the optional <>4__this proxy, parameter proxies (one per parameter, named after the parameter itself per Roslyn convention), and hoisted user-local proxies (<name>5__N).
member.remarks:
This builder produces the type only — it does not generate MoveNext, SetStateMachine, the constructor, or the rewritten kickoff body. Those are the state-machine rewriter's responsibility and will plug into this type as a follow-up step.
Builder selection follows Roslyn:
Declared inner return type Void ⇒ caller observes System.Threading.Tasks.Task, builder is
AsyncTaskMethodBuilder.
Declared inner return type T ⇒ caller observes System.Threading.Tasks.Task<T>, builder is
AsyncTaskMethodBuilder<T>.
Return type carries [AsyncMethodBuilder(typeof(T))] ⇒ custom builder T (or T<TResult>).
Iterator producers (async IAsyncEnumerable<T>) take the class container; everything else takes struct.
Returns null if the BCL types Task / Task<T> cannot be resolved through the supplied (e.g. an exotic TFM without the standard libraries) or if the kickoff's declared inner return type lacks a CLR projection (e.g. a pure GSharp type that cannot yet be wrapped as Task<T> — see ADR-0023 Phase 5.1 limitation). Callers route such cases through a diagnostic rather than dereferencing the null.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AwaitResumePoint
member.summary: Planned labels for one suspending await in MoveNext.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.AwaitableShape
member.summary: Resolved per-call-site shape of an awaitable expression. Encapsulates the duck-typed GetAwaiter / IsCompleted / GetResult triple and the awaiter's ICriticalNotifyCompletion flag, which the per-await codegen uses to select between AwaitOnCompleted and AwaitUnsafeOnCompleted (see ~/roslyn-async.md §1, §6.4, §12 corner case 2).
member.remarks:
Resolution is strictly nominal — it searches for instance methods and extension methods named GetAwaiter on the awaitable type, then for an instance IsCompleted property and an instance GetResult method on the awaiter type. This matches the C# language rule: any type exposing those members in the right shape is awaitable, regardless of whether it implements Task.
This class does not perform conversions or emit diagnostics; it returns null from when the shape does not match, and the caller is responsible for reporting the error.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.ChannelOperationRewriter
member.summary: ADR-0174 D4 (Phase 3-1): inside a state-machine body, a channel operation parks the state machine instead of a thread. The binder lowers every <-ch, two-value receive, and ch <- v onto the blocking ChannelOps.Receive / Receive2 / Send facade calls; this rewriter, run before the async pipeline's exception-handler rewrite and spiller, replaces each with an awaited ReceiveValueAsync / ReceiveTupleAsync / SendAsync call of the same type. The spiller then lifts the new awaits to statement level exactly as it does for a user-written await.
member.remarks:
The one region left on the blocking lowering is a lock body: Monitor is thread-affine, so an await that resumes on another thread would make the lowered Monitor.Exit throw. A channel operation inside a lock keeps blocking here (Phase 3-3 adds the GS0558 warning for it).
Discrimination witness (ADR-0154): a mutant that rewrites inside the lock region breaks Adr0174ChannelAwaitInAsyncFuncEmitTests.ReceiveInsideLock_KeepsBlocking (a SynchronizationLockException at Monitor.Exit); a mutant that leaves the blocking facade in place breaks …ParkedReceives_DoNotHoldThreads, which parks more receives than the thread pool has threads.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.GeneratedNames
member.summary: Deterministic mangled-name generator for compiler-synthesized async state-machine members. The naming scheme intentionally mirrors Roslyn's generated names so PDB tooling and the debugger surface familiar identifiers.
member.remarks:
Per ADR-0023 and the Roslyn-async spec (see ~/roslyn-async.md §4), the CLR does not care about these names; they only matter for debugger experience and (future) Edit-and-Continue stability. GSharp does not support EnC, but adopting Roslyn's scheme keeps the diff visible to users who decompile the produced PE.
The generator is stateful per-method: state machine kind suffixes (e.g. d__N) and per-type awaiter slot indices (u__N) are allocated by the caller, which threads its own counters through. All methods on this class are pure.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.KickoffBodyBuilder
member.summary: Plans the kickoff stub for an async state machine.
member.remarks: The kickoff stub is the original async method after state-machine lowering: it creates the state-machine local, initializes the builder and state fields, copies parameters into hoisted fields, calls builder.Start(ref sm), and returns builder.Task for task-returning methods. This slice records that canonical sequence without replacing the bound body yet.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.KickoffBodyPlan
member.summary: Planned kickoff-stub operations for one async method.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.KickoffOperation
member.summary: One ordered operation in the planned kickoff stub.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.KickoffOperationKind
member.summary: The kind of a planned kickoff-stub operation.

member.remarks: The output is a that the existing BodyEmitter in ReflectionMetadataEmitter can lower directly to IL. No nodes survive. member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.RefInitializationHoister
member.summary: Lowering pass that eliminates ref locals (managed pointer locals) from async method bodies so they do not require hoisting into byref fields — which the CLR forbids on heap-allocated or state-machine types.
member.remarks: A ref local is identified by its type being and its initializer being a . The hoister recomputes the managed pointer at every use site: *refLocal (dereference read) → replaced with the underlying lvalue expression. refLocal (bare pointer usage, e.g., passed to ref parameter) → replaced with &lvalue. To avoid duplicating side effects (issue #418 / P1-12), any non-trivial sub-expression of the original ref initializer (call receiver, index expression, etc.) is evaluated once into a hoisted temporary local at the ref-initialization site. The reconstructed lvalue then refers only to those temporaries and other side-effect-free leaves (variables, parameters, literals), making it safe to inline at every use site. The constituent variables are themselves later hoisted into state-machine fields by if they cross an await. A reconstructed field or element address is also probed once at the original declaration site. This preserves null and bounds exceptions before a later suspension while still avoiding an illegal managed-pointer state-machine field. This pass runs after and before in the async pipeline. Opaque borrowed addresses remain MoveNext locals only when the shared suspension-liveness analysis proves they do not cross a suspension.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.ResumableStateAllocator
member.summary: Allocates deterministic state numbers for resumable async state-machine points.
member.remarks: Await resume states and async-iterator yield resume states live in separate numeric ranges. Await states count upward from 0; async-iterator yield states count downward from -4. This mirrors Roslyn's state numbering and keeps -1, -2, and -3 reserved for the non-resumable states in .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.SpillSequenceSpiller
member.summary: Rewrites an async method body so that every appears only at statement top-level — either as a or as the RHS of a (or assignment to a spill temp). Sub-expressions whose values must survive an await are lifted into spill locals. After this pass, can process every await as a simple top-level statement without concern for evaluation order of siblings.
member.remarks:
This implementation handles:
Binary expressions (arithmetic/comparison) with await in either operand.
Short-circuit operators (&&, ||) with await on the right.
Method calls (user, imported, imported-instance, CLR static/instance/ctor, indirect,
function-pointer) with await in the receiver/target and/or arguments.
Variable declarations and return statements with nested await.
Conversion expressions wrapping an await.
Ternary/conditional expressions with await in the condition and/or an arm (issue #1619) — only the
taken arm's await actually runs, via an if/else expansion mirroring the short-circuit logical-operator spill.
Index expressions, array/tuple/struct/map literals, stack-alloc, append, len/cap, is/as,
field/property access and assignment, and CLR interop operators/indexers with await in any operand (issue #1619) — each spilled left-to-right like a call's argument list.
Switch expressions with await in the governing expression and/or an arm value (issue #1619
completion) — spilled via an index-selecting rebuild of the switch (so pattern-matching/guard semantics run unmodified against a spilled discriminant) followed by an if/else-chain expansion keyed off the selected arm index, so only the taken arm's await runs, mirroring the ternary spill.
Null-conditional access (?.) expressions with await in the receiver and/or the when-not-null
continuation (issue #1619 completion) — the receiver is spilled once into the capture local/field and the continuation runs only on the non-nil path, via an if/else expansion when the continuation itself contains await.
Conditional address-of expressions with await in a conditionally-selected operand (ADR-0061; issue
#1619 completion) — each operand's nested await is spilled behind a conditional-goto guard so only the selected branch's side effects run, then the original node is rebuilt from the (now await-free) operands so the existing branch-and-take-address emitter performs the final, correct addressing — no byref-typed value is ever carried across the branch join.
Deferred cases (emit a diagnostic if encountered):
Ref/out arguments containing await.
Value-type receivers of instance methods containing await in arguments.
A switch-expression arm when guard containing await (issue #1619) — guards must be re-evaluated
for every candidate arm during dispatch, so an await inside a guard would need to re-run (and re-suspend) for each pattern tried; this requires a fuller per-guard suspension protocol that is out of scope here, so it remains diagnostic-gated.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.SynthesizedStateMachineType
member.summary: A compiler-synthesized CLR type that hosts the lowered state machine for an async method (see ~/roslyn-async.md §5). It carries all hoisted control fields (<>1__state, <>t__builder), the this-proxy field, parameter proxies, hoisted user locals, and the per-type pooled awaiter fields.
member.remarks: The type is emitted by as a nested type on the containing type (or top-level for the script entry-point's async helpers). Its kind — struct vs class — is fixed at construction: struct by default for async void / async Task / async Task / custom task-likes; the no-alloc fast path on synchronously-completing awaits depends on this. class for async-iterators (always), and as the fallback when EnC stability is needed (not currently supported by GSharp). This class is a thin data container. Field population happens in AsyncStateMachineRewriter (todo: state-rewriter), which decides hoist set, allocates awaiter slot indices, and registers the synthesized type with its kickoff .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.TryDispatchEntry
member.summary: One entry in a user try's internal state dispatch.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.TryDispatchPlan
member.summary: Result of : per-state outer dispatch routing, per-try entry labels, and per-try internal dispatch entries.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.TryDispatchPlanner
member.summary: Pre-pass walker that builds a from the lowered async body by locating each await within the lexical nesting of user try statements.
member.remarks: The CLR forbids branching br/brtrue/brfalse into a protected (try) region from outside. The outer MoveNext state dispatch therefore cannot jump directly to a resume label that lies inside a user try. Instead, a synthesized entry label is placed immediately before each user try with awaits, and the outer dispatch routes there. Inside that try a second dispatch then either routes further (to a nested try's entry label) or to a resume label for an await directly in that try. For nested user trys, dispatch chains through each level: outer dispatch → outermost try's entry → outermost try's internal dispatch → next-deeper try's entry → ... → resume label. Implementation note (6.3): the traversal subclasses instead of using a bespoke switch. The walker's recurse-by-default behavior means every node kind — including kinds added in the future — is automatically traversed. Only and need custom handling; everything else inherits the walker's depth-first walk. This eliminates the silent-default-drops-unknown-nodes bug class.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Async.TryDispatchPlanner.WalkVisitor
member.summary: subclass that records await-to-try nesting during a depth-first walk. All node kinds not overridden here are traversed automatically by the walker's base implementation.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.BaseCallForwarderRewriter
member.summary: Issues #1467 and #2667: routes base.M(args) calls that appear inside async / iterator / suspending method bodies, or inside a function literal or a go operand nested in any instance member, through a synthesized non-virtual forwarder method on the containing class.
member.remarks:
A base-class call lowers to a non-virtual call instance R Base::M(...). The CLR verifier requires the this argument of such a non-virtual call to a (virtual) base method to be the calling method's own this (ldarg.0). Inside an async / iterator state machine the original this is hoisted into a <>4__this field, so the base call's receiver is a field load — producing an ilverify ThisMismatch error. A function literal is emitted as a method of a closure class that holds the captured this in a field, so a base call inside it has the same problem (ADR-0192 follow-on 2: a translated C# local function calling base.Crawlpos()). Roslyn forwards those calls the same way.
Mirroring Roslyn's <>n__N forwarders, this pass synthesizes a private instance method on the containing class whose body is return base.M(args); (emitted with a real ldarg.0 receiver, so it verifies) and rewrites the base call inside the state-machine body to an ordinary instance call on that forwarder. The forwarder is non-async, so it flows through normal class-method emit.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.BoundNodeForm
member.summary: Reads the members of a bound node that only one of the node's construction forms omits, from a pass that has already excluded that form.
member.remarks: Several bound nodes are discriminated unions over their constructors, and a member one form omits is declared nullable for that reason alone. BoundFieldAccessExpression.StructType is null only in the interface static-field form (ADR-0089 / #1030), which also has no receiver; BoundIndexAssignmentExpression.Target is null only in the expression-target form (#2488), which sets TargetExpression instead. The two nulls in each pair always travel together, but the compiler cannot correlate two properties, so a pass that has already excluded one form still sees the other's member as maybe-null. Every lowering pass hits this, so each invariant is stated once here rather than re-argued at a dozen call sites (ADR-0155 amendment A7). Use these helpers only after excluding the other form — by testing the receiver, the target expression, or InterfaceType itself. A pass that rebuilds a node without making that distinction is a different matter, and these helpers are the wrong tool for it: it must branch and reconstruct through the matching constructor, or it silently drops the discriminator. Three rewriters that did not are issue #3333.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.CaptureBoxingRewriter
member.summary: Issue #523: a function literal that captures a value-type local of its enclosing scope must observe subsequent writes to that local — both Go and C# capture closures over the variable cell, not its value at construction time. The historical emit pipeline snapshotted captured values into closure-class fields, so an outer reassignment was invisible to the lambda.
member.remarks:
This pass hoists every captured local / captured parameter into a synthesized single-field reference class (<>__Box_<name>_<n>), inserts the allocation at the local's declaration site (or at function entry for captured parameters), and rewrites every read and write of the captured variable — including reads/writes inside the lambda body — to go through the shared box.
Because the box is a reference type, the lambda's existing snapshot-by-value emit (which copies the captured variable into the closure class's field at newobj time) now copies a *reference* to the box. The outer scope and every lambda that captures the variable therefore share the same cell. Multiple lambdas in the same scope share state automatically; nested lambdas continue to work via the existing transitive-capture propagation (CapturedVariableCollector.RewriteFunctionLiteralExpression).
Globals () are excluded as a side fix: they are already addressable as static fields, so capturing them into a closure field would just re-introduce the snapshot bug; the pass instead rewrites the lambda's capture list to omit them, leaving the lambda body to read the static field directly at every use.
For-range key/value variables are boxed at the start of each iteration. This preserves foreach-style fresh-variable semantics when closures escape while still sharing one cell among closures from the same iteration.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.CaptureBoxingRewriter.OutVarBoxIntroductionScanner
member.summary: Issue #1453: finds captured locals that are introduced (rather than declared) by an out/ref address-of within a single statement — i.e. inline out var x captures that have no . The scan is shallow: it stops at nested s (those are handled when the rewriter recurses into them, so a loop body gets a fresh box) and at function literals (already opaque to ).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandlerShape
member.summary: Issue #3730 (issue #3705, family 3 — the load-context family): the System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler surface that lowers onto, resolved from the compilation's reference closure rather than from the SDK hosting gsc. The lowerer used to hold static readonly Type HandlerType = typeof(DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler) and reflect the constructor, AppendLiteral, ToStringAndClear and the four AppendFormatted overloads off it. That is a live host typeof, so it answers for the framework gsc is running on, never for the framework it is compiling against. Two silent divergences follow, both of the kind #3705 catalogues: an overload present on the host but absent from the target is accepted, and the emitted call cannot resolve at the target's runtime; when the target closure does not declare the handler at all (any netstandard2.x target, for instance), #3729's ImportedMemberRefFactory.GetTypeReference projection has nothing to project onto and falls back to the host type — so the compiled assembly silently acquired a TypeRef scoped to System.Private.CoreLib, 10.0.0.0, the very leak #3729 closed, and the compile reported success. Resolution therefore goes through ) — the established funnel for "give me a well-known type in this compilation's reflection context" — and every member probe compares parameter types with rather than reference identity against a host typeof, because the resolved members are types on every real /reference: compile.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.ExpressionTreeLowerer
member.summary: Issue #2130: lowers lambda-to-Expression<TDelegate> conversions into ordinary bound calls to System.Linq.Expressions.Expression factory methods.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.FinallyExitRewriter
member.summary: Lifts a finally body out of its CLR handler when it contains a branch that exits the handler. CLR forbids leave from finally, so exits from the protected body are funneled through the lifted body and dispatched after it.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.InterpolatedStringHandlerLowerer
member.summary: Emit-time (IL-only) lowering of to the C# 10 interpolated-string-handler pattern, or to composite formatting when the target framework does not provide that handler (issues #368/#3769, ADR-0055).
member.remarks: When the target provides the default handler, each interpolation node is rewritten into a that does the following. declares a System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler value-type local and constructs it with (literalLength, formattedCount). calls AppendLiteral(string) for each literal run and AppendFormatted(value[, alignment][, format]) for each hole. yields ToStringAndClear() as the block's result. The handler is a ref struct; in metadata it is an ordinary value type (the IsByRefLike marker does not affect the local signature), so the existing value-type local / instance-call emit paths handle it directly. Value-type holes do not box: AppendFormatted is closed over the hole's concrete CLR type (or, for user-defined types lacking a reflection , over an object placeholder while the real type-argument symbol is encoded into the emitted MethodSpec), so the hole value is passed by its natural representation. When the target does not provide the default handler, ordinary string interpolation instead lowers to String.Format(string, object[]). That target-compatible path boxes value-type holes and preserves composite formatting, alignment, evaluation order, and literal-brace escaping. User-defined interpolated-string handlers are unaffected. This rewrite is applied only on the emit path; the tree-walk interpreter renders directly.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.Iterators.IteratorTryDispatchPlanner
member.summary: Pre-pass walker that builds a from the user iterator body by locating each yield within the lexical nesting of user try statements.
member.remarks: The CLR forbids branching br/brtrue/brfalse into a protected (try) region from outside. The outer MoveNext state dispatch therefore cannot jump directly to a resume label that lies inside a user try. Instead, a synthesized entry label is placed immediately before each user try with yields, and the outer dispatch routes there. Inside that try a second dispatch then either routes further (to a nested try's entry label) or to a resume label for a yield directly in that try. The plan also captures, for each user try that has a finally block and contains yields, the set of yield states inside it (innermost-first). The Dispose synthesizer uses the per-try yield-state sets to emit a finally walk that runs each pending finally when an in-progress enumerator is disposed.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.NestedFunctionBodyRewriter
member.summary: Shared helper for emit-pipeline rewriters whose transforms are lexical-scope agnostic and therefore must run inside hosted nested bodies too.
member.remarks:
intentionally does not recurse into or generic local-function bodies because many callers model lexical scopes. Emit-time lowering passes such as interpolated-string rewriting and side-effect spilling are scope neutral, though: if a top-level body gets the transform, a nested hosted body must get that exact same transform before the emitter sees it.
This base class provides that shared descent so the emit pipeline does not fork between ordinary bodies and lambda/local-function bodies.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.SideEffectAnalyzer
member.summary: Issue #452: classifies bound expressions by whether re-evaluating them could produce an observable side effect or a different result. Used by the lowering pass to decide which sub-expressions inside a "duplicating context" (compound index / property assignments, etc.) must be hoisted into a temp before the emit phase walks them.
member.remarks:
The analyzer is intentionally conservative: any expression whose kind is not explicitly recognised as side-effect-free is reported as side-effecting. This means the spiller may occasionally introduce a redundant temp for an expression that is in fact pure, but it will never miss an expression that could re-fire observable behaviour. The IL optimizer / JIT can fold away redundant copies of variable reads at no runtime cost.
"Side effect" here covers more than just method calls. It includes:
Method / constructor / delegate invocations.
Assignments (which themselves return the new value).
Property reads (a user property getter can do anything).
Indexer reads (a CLR or user indexer is also a property getter).
await and yield-style suspensions.
Allocations (new T(), struct literals) and array / map literals.
Block / spill-sequence expressions (already contain effects).
Anything the analyzer does not recognise.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.SideEffectSpiller
member.summary: Issue #452: a general lowering pass that spills side-effecting sub-expressions into fresh temp locals at every bound-tree context that would otherwise re-emit the sub-expression more than once.
member.remarks:
Side-effect duplication has been a recurring class of emit bugs: short-circuit operators (P0-1), array / map / CLR-indexer assignments (P1-1), user and CLR property assignments (P1-2), and ref-local hoisting across await boundaries (P1-12) all had emit-site bugs where a sub-expression with observable side effects (a counter increment, a Console.Write, a property getter that mutates state) fired twice instead of once. Each was patched at the emit site; this pass closes the door on the entire bug class by guaranteeing that the bound tree the emitter sees never contains a side-effecting expression in a position that the emit pipeline duplicates.
The pass runs once, after binding / interpolated-string lowering and before the async / iterator state-machine rewriters and IL emission. For each "duplicating context" (currently: assignments through an array index, a CLR indexer, a user property, or a CLR property), it inspects each sub-expression that the emit pipeline historically re-emitted. When a sub-expression has observable side effects per ), the entire assignment is rewritten into a  of the form:{
            var $tmp0 = <side-effecting receiver / index>
            var $tmp1 = <side-effecting value>
            ...
            <original assignment with $tmpN substituted in>
            }
The emit pipeline sees only  reads in the substituted positions, so any subsequent emit-site duplication is a no-op (loading a local twice has no observable effect). The pre-existing emit-site spill code (which dups the stored value into a slot to recover the assignment expression's result) remains as defense in depth.
The pass is intentionally additive: it only inserts wrappers and never alters the meaning of existing expressions. Expressions that are already side-effect-free (literals, variable reads, pure arithmetic on pure operands) are left untouched, so the lowered tree size grows only where duplication risk was real.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Lowering.SideEffectSpiller.ReceiverSubstitutionRewriter
member.summary: Issue #1688: rewrites a bound expression tree, replacing every reference-equal occurrence of a shared receiver node with a replacement expression (typically a read of the temp local it was just spilled into). Used to keep the nested read embedded in a compound assignment's value in sync with the receiver copy the assignment itself was rewritten to use.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.AccessibilityChecker
member.summary:
Issue #950 / issue #2044: bind-time accessibility checks for the protected and private modifiers. A protected member is accessible within its declaring type and within the bodies of types that derive from the declaring type; a private member is accessible only within its declaring top-level type's body (including nested types of that type, but not derived types). Either is inaccessible from unrelated external code (e.g. the synthetic <Program> host or a sibling type).
Unlike internal — which G# leaves to the CLR to enforce at runtime via the emitted IL accessibility — protected/private add a compile-time check so that external access is reported as a clean diagnostic (GS0379 / GS0472) rather than surfacing only as a runtime /. The emitted IL still carries the matching CIL accessibility, so the CLR independently enforces the same rule.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.AsyncLetVariableSymbol

member.remarks: Every read is spelled await name, and the compiler turns that into a read of . Any other mention of the name is GS0569: the value may not have arrived, and D4's discipline is that suspension is visible at the point it happens.

The override-matching and interface- satisfaction comparisons must use the effective return type so an async method validly overrides / implements a base declared with the explicit Task / Task[T] return type.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.BaseConstructorInitializer

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ChannelDirection
member.summary: The direction of a channel type clause (ADR-0174 D2): chan[T] is bidirectional and binds to Channel<T>; in chan[T] is receive-only and binds to ChannelReader<T>; out chan[T] is send-only and binds to ChannelWriter<T>. The keywords are the language's existing variance keywords: in is what you read from, out is what you write to.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ChannelTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a channel type clause: chan[T], in chan[T], or out chan[T] (ADR-0174 D1/D2).
member.remarks: The type stays identity-transparent to its BCL backing — chan[T] is System.Threading.Channels.Channel, in chan[T] is ChannelReader, out chan[T] is ChannelWriter — so every foreign channel from C# or NuGet is assignable to it. What the expression chan[T](…) constructs is the runtime's Gsharp.Concurrency.Chan, a subclass that carries the Go-exact machinery; that constructed type is an ordinary imported symbol, and is the one place that recognizes every channel-shaped type. Instances are cached per (element type, direction) so identical channel types compare by reference.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ClrLoadContext
member.summary: Issue #3705 (family 3): the single place that answers "does this CLR type — which may have been materialised through a — satisfy a well-known shape the compiler cares about?". gsc creates one MetadataLoadContext per compilation () and never normalises the s it hands back to host RuntimeTypes. A typeof(X).IsAssignableFrom(importedType) in the binder, lowerer or emitter is therefore not merely imprecise: it is unconditionally false, silently, for every program compiled with /reference: — which is every production compile. That is what produced #3708 (a for loop over an imported enumerable emitted no Dispose) and the Delegate arm of #3697. The rule this type exists to enforce: a load-context-crossing question is asked here, never hand-rolled at the call site. The guard-rail test Issue3705LoadContextFunnelGuardTests fails the build when a new typeof(X).IsAssignableFrom(…) appears in Binding/, Lowering/, Emit/ or Symbols/.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ClrMemberVisibility
member.summary:
Issue #3705: the single place that decides whether an imported CLR member is visible to the compilation currently being bound.
Member-lookup probes across the binder each hand-rolled their own and nonPublic: arguments, and the result was a family of "inconsistent sibling probe" defects (#3693, #3702, #3703): a friend assembly's internal method was a candidate while its internal property was not, an internal setter was readable but not writable, and so on. Every probe that participates in member lookup should ask these helpers instead, passing the one bit that decides the answer — whether ) holds for the declaring assembly.
General member lookup admits only public and friend-visible assembly members. The explicitly derived-type helpers additionally admit the CLR family accessibilities available from a subclass; private members remain invisible.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ClrNullability
member.summary:
Phase 3.C.5 / ADR-0001 / issue #209: helpers for reading C# nullable-reference-types metadata ([NullableAttribute] / [NullableContextAttribute]) from members loaded through a .
Both top-level and inner-position (generic argument or array element) nullability are surfaced. Inner positions are carried via so that code paths such as for range iteration and CLR indexer access can recover element nullability at bind time.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ClrNullability.DecodedSignature

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ClrNullabilityState
member.summary: ADR-0186 §2: what one C# nullable-metadata byte actually says about a reference position — the three-state successor to ADR-0136's two-valued IsFlagNonNull. The names are C#'s own, deliberately: these are readings of metadata, not G# types. The mapping from a state to a G# type is a separate decision and lives in exactly one place (), which is what lets ADR-0186's pivot change one cell of ADR-0136's table without touching the readers. ADR-0186 spells this NullabilityState. It is named ClrNullabilityState here because System.Reflection already declares a NullabilityState — the BCL's own reading of the same metadata, which this repository's emit tests use heavily via NullabilityInfoContext. Under the ADR's spelling, every file that imports both System.Reflection and this namespace stops compiling with CS0104, and several already do.

member.summary: ADR-0068 / issue #698: a user-declared destructor (deinit { … }) on a GSharp class. Each wraps a synthesized named Finalize whose receiver is the owning class. The emitter materialises that function as a CLR Finalize override whose body is wrapped in try { … } finally { base.Finalize(); }, byte-for-byte identical to what the C# compiler emits for a ~Type() destructor.

The emitter, however, ignores the standard method-emission path for this function and routes through a dedicated EmitClassDeinitializer that establishes the try/finally region and the chained base.Finalize() call.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.LoadContextSensitiveTypeComparer
member.summary: Issue #3826 (the #3705 load-context family): compares instances the way does — by structural identity — but ADDITIONALLY requires that every assembly the type is built from is the same INSTANCE.
member.remarks:
keys on . Two copies of the same file loaded into two different s have the SAME assembly-qualified name, so that comparer treats them as one type. That is exactly what #420 wanted for the emitter (collapsing duplicate TypeRef rows for one logical type reached by several paths inside ONE context), and exactly what a process-wide symbol cache must NOT do: it makes a from one compilation answer a later compilation's lookup.
The dangerous case is a constructed generic whose DEFINITION lives in a shared assembly but whose ARGUMENTS come from a private reference context — ImmutableArray<SyntaxNode>, say. ImportedTypeSymbol's outer cache bucket is keyed by type.Assembly, which for both constructions is the one host System.Collections.Immutable; only the inner comparer separates them, and a name-only comparer does not. The resulting cross-context symbol is silently wrong: closing a generic method over an operand from each side makes throw, overload resolution drops the candidate per C# §7.5.2, and the call reports "Cannot find function <name>" about a method that plainly exists (#3818).
Equality therefore keeps the structural check and adds a walk over the type's constituents (element type, generic arguments) requiring reference-equal assemblies at every position — the same "hash is a bucketing hint, equality is the real test" shape as . Two instances of one logical type reached by different paths inside a single context still collapse, because a load context returns one instance per identity.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.LocalVariableSymbol

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MapTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a G# map type map[K,V].
member.remarks: ADR-0104 (supersedes Phase 3.A.4 Go-flavored map[K]V) — backing representation is the CLR System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<K, V>. The literal form map[K,V]{k: v, …} populates a freshly allocated dictionary; m[k] indexes it; the delete(m, k) built-in removes a key; len(m) returns Count. Instances are cached per (K, V) pair so identical map types compare by reference.

member.remarks: One instance is attached by when the parameter carries a well-formed @MarshalAs annotation; the emitter consumes it to set and to add a row to the FieldMarshal table via MetadataBuilder.AddMarshallingDescriptor. The attribute is pseudo-custom — its data lives entirely in the dedicated metadata table, so the emitter does NOT also write it as a CustomAttribute row (see ).
