member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataSignatureDecoder
member.summary: Decodes the type structure of a signature blob into type symbols (ADR-0209 section 5, "One decoder").
member.remarks: The result holds no nullability: the funnel of ADR-0193 applies it later, once, from the attribute blobs. This stage covers the structure that a base type, a constraint and a field type need. Tuple canonical forms come with the nullability stage.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataTypeKeys
member.summary: The identity text of a type, spelled for a symbol and for a reflection type by one set of rules.
member.remarks: The comparison mode (ADR-0209 section 10) compares these texts. A definition is its assembly and full name; the built-in types are their System names; a construction, an array, a pointer and a by-ref add their parts. Both spellings share the same primitive list and the same separators, so the two cannot drift apart.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataTypeKinds
member.summary: The kind flags of a type definition. One function computes them, so no consumer decides them again.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataTypeNameReader
member.summary: Reads the full names of the types of an assembly from its metadata tables. No is created.
member.remarks: The defined names are the names that Assembly.GetTypes() reports through a . They follow the type-definition table without the <Module> row. A nested type is spelled Outer+Inner. The forwarded names are the top-level exported types that forward to another assembly. Reflection reports a forward only when its target loads. It then adds the public nested types of the type that the forward resolves to. The caller checks the target and adds the nested types (see ). refuses an image with a name that reflection escapes. The caller then reads that assembly through reflection. spells such a name as reflection does and never refuses (ADR-0209).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataTypeParameters
member.summary: The rules that turn generic parameter rows into objects (ADR-0209 section 6).
member.remarks: Each rule is decided here once. The legacy constraint slots of the symbol hold the first constraint of each kind. The owner keeps every constraint row, in table order.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MetadataTypeSymbol
member.summary: A type definition of a as a symbol (ADR-0209 section 5, "Definitions").
member.remarks: A module creates one symbol for each type definition row. A race publishes one winner. The symbol has no CLR type: its ClrType is nil. This stage holds the name, the nesting, the kind flags, the generic parameters and the base definition. Members, signatures and constraints come with the decoder in the next stage.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MethodKind
member.summary: What kind of function a is — the Roslyn MethodKind analogue for the analyzer surface (ADR-0169, issue #4436). The member names match Roslyn's so a migrated analyzer's comparisons translate by name. G# constructors are s, not functions, so there is no Constructor member.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MissingTypeKey
member.summary: The key of an interned missing type.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.MissingTypeSymbol
member.summary: The type that a type reference names when no assembly of the reference set supplies it.
member.remarks: A interns one symbol for each pair of assembly identity and full name. A missing type is equal to itself and to no other symbol (ADR-0209 section 6).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ModelDisagreement
member.summary: One question on which the MetadataLoadContext model and the handle model gave different answers.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NativeSliceTypes
member.summary: Nominal recognition of ADR-0190 descriptors. They use the ordinary imported generic representation, never the array-backed .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityAnnotatedTypeSymbol
member.summary: A that wraps an imported CLR generic or array type and carries the full [NullableAttribute] byte array so that inner-position nullability (issue #209) can be recovered when the type is later used as a collection element, dictionary value, etc.
member.remarks:
The array follows the C# compiler's DFS pre-order layout: byte 0 belongs to the outer reference/array position or is the leading zero placeholder for a closed generic value type. Subsequent bytes belong to array elements and generic arguments in DFS order; non-generic value types contribute no position, and Nullable is transparent. Example — Dictionary:
flags = { 1 (Dictionary non-null), 1 (string key non-null), 2 (string? value nullable) }.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityFreeReason
member.summary: ADR-0193 §3 (GSA0007): why a call to has no declaration nullability to lose. Every nullability-free conversion states one, so a reviewer (and the analyzer) can see the claim at the call site.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityFunnelAttribute
member.summary: ADR-0193 §3 (GSA0007): marks a member that is part of the producer funnel, and so may call the conversion doors (, the MemberLookup.MapOpenClrTypeToSymbolic overloads, ), and 's ReadNullableFlags / ClassifyFlag / ClassifyPosition). The exemption is per member, never per type: other members of the same type are checked like any other code. Adding this attribute is the reviewed exception issue #4363 asks for. The analyzer's tests pin the full list of attributed members, so a new one fails a test until that list is updated. Inside a funnel member other than 's, a direct or call is still reported: classified positions resolve through the rule. Lambdas and local functions inside an attributed member are part of it.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityImportRule
member.summary: ADR-0193 §1 — the producer choke point: the single decision "a position whose declaration is classified as S, substituted (or not) with argument A, gets which reference nullability?". The decision (, ) takes and returns no type-model value, so gsc's walkers and cs2gs's GTypeReference applier share it. gsc's appliers (, , and the byte-level the projection reader needs) are the only places a Layer 1 walker turns a classified position into a wrapper. Platform-types semantics only (ADR-0193 owner decision 2). There is no branch in this class and none may be added: the legacy --nullability=enabled reading is retired by #4372, and the walkers keep their own legacy arm until then.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityMode
member.summary: ADR-0186: how a compilation reads nullability-oblivious imported reference positions. Selected by --nullability= (equivalently /nullability:). This is modelled as a named mode rather than a boolean because ADR-0186 §9 adds a third value, — a declaration-scope switch for cs2gs — to the same switch (step 5). It is a third value rather than a second axis because the combination an axis would add, "ADR-0136's T? import reading plus oblivious source declarations", has no consumer: an oblivious declaration exists to be read as T!, and only a mode that reads T! can say so. Spelling, reconciled with ADR-0186 §9. §9 names the switch's values enabled|oblivious, default enabled, where "enabled" means "source declarations are nullability-enabled". Steps 1–3 had already given enabled a different meaning on this switch — ADR-0136's import reading — so §9's "enabled" is spelled platform-types here (the default), and enabled keeps its step-1 meaning.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityOptions
member.summary: ADR-0186: the ambient for the compilation currently being bound. Why ambient, and why temporary. This repository threads compilation options explicitly (Compilation.ImplicitSystemImport reaches Binder.BindGlobalScope as a parameter), and that is the right shape. It is not available here: the metadata reader that must consult the mode is ClrNullability.SymbolFromFlagsOffset, a static leaf reached from , MemberLookup, NullableFlagsBuilder and the importer, none of which carry a Compilation. Threading one down would touch far more of the compiler than the pivot this flag gates. The mode is therefore scoped with an for the duration of a bind, which makes it flow into the whole logical call — across the Task.Run hops the language server uses — while staying invisible to a concurrent bind of a different compilation, and to sibling xunit tests. It is set once at the start of a bind and never mutated mid-flight, so the same-thread reentrancy hazard recorded in ClrOverloadResolution's "install/clear around the call" note does not arise: there is no window to clear out from under a nested caller, only a value that is uniform for the whole compilation. Step 1 said this type was scaffolding to delete at step 3. It is kept, deliberately. Step 3 flipped the default to , but the mode does not stop being a choice there: has to stay selectable for two concrete reasons. ADR-0136's Issue3705MemberKindNullabilityDifferentialTests asserts both columns off one piece of real csc-emitted metadata — that differential is the standing uniformity gate, and it cannot express "the other reading" without a switch. And --nullability=enabled is the escape hatch the release note points at for source the flip breaks. Issue #4356 deleted the old member-lookup carve-out, so under this mode an oblivious member chain (Environment.Version.Major) reports on its T? link exactly as ADR-0136 always said it should, and needs !!, narrowing or ?.. Retiring the mode is a separate decision.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullabilityOptions.Scope
member.summary: The restore token returned by . A struct rather than a class so an always-taken using on the hot bind path allocates nothing.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullableLifting
member.summary: Bug-overview §6.1 / phased Nullable<T> unification: single seam for every Nullable<T> probe and constructor-projection helper that the binder and emitter need. PR N-1 is a pure refactor that gathers the previously scattered helpers in one place; subsequent PRs (N-2/N-3/N-4) plug their fixes into this facade rather than into N separate call sites.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullableSequenceSpecializationKind
member.summary: Identifies compiler-generated CLR-representation variants of an unconstrained nullable sequence iterator.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.NullableTypeSymbol
member.summary: Phase 3.C.1 / ADR-0001: wraps an underlying to indicate that values of this type may be the absence-of-value (nil).
member.remarks: In Phase 3.C.1 the wrapper is purely a binder-level annotation: emit and the evaluator treat as the runtime type. The nil literal, null-safe operators, and smart casts follow in Phase 3.C.2–4.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PInvokeMetadata
member.summary: The resolved attribute knobs for a P/Invoke function declaration — either the classic @DllImport form (ADR-0086 / issue #727) or the source-generator-shaped @LibraryImport form (ADR-0092 / issue #758). One instance is attached to a by the declaration binder when the function carries a well-formed annotation; the emitter consumes it either to write a single ImplMap row (DllImport) or to generate an explicit managed marshalling stub that calls a hidden blittable P/Invoke inner method (LibraryImport).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PackageSymbol
member.summary: Represents a package symbol in the language.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ParameterSymbol
member.summary: Represents a function declaration parameter symbol in the language.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PinnedTypeSymbol
member.summary: ADR-0125 / issue #1026: a synthetic marker type for the pinned CLR local introduced by a fixed statement. It wraps the local's real storage type () — either the managed array type T[] (array-pin form) or a managed by-ref T& (, string-pin form) — and signals the emitter to set the pinned flag on that local's signature (.locals init ([n] … pinned)) so the GC cannot relocate the buffer.
member.remarks: This wrapper is attached only to a synthetic local that the emitter touches directly (via its IL slot); it never flows through expression binding, so no general is/equality checks elsewhere observe it. The only consumer is ReflectionMetadataEmitter.EncodeLocalVariableType.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PlatformTypeSymbol
member.summary: ADR-0186 §1: the platform type T! — a reference position whose nullability nobody stated. A means "the declarer said this may be nil". A bare means "the declarer said this is never nil". is the third answer, and the only honest one for a position imported from nullability-oblivious CLR metadata: the declarer said nothing. ADR-0136 collapsed that third answer onto T?, which is what forced every use site to discharge a proof obligation about a fact the compiler does not have — and what bound-node carve-out predicates were reconstructing for oblivious receivers, one node kind at a time. With this symbol an oblivious receiver no longer depends on any of them. (The last such predicate on main, CanBindClrInstanceMember's BoundClrPropertyAccessExpression disjunct, outlived step 4 because it also carried member chains through stated-nullable imported reads; issue #4356 deleted it.) The wrapper is deliberately a distinct symbol rather than a flag on (ADR-0186 alternative 2). The sites that must not treat a platform value as nullable — member lookup, overload resolution, GS0159 — simply never match is NullableTypeSymbol, and they do so by construction rather than by each remembering to ask a predicate. It is equally deliberately not an erasure to T: T! must still admit == nil, if let, ?. and !!, and erasing it would reinstate verbatim the hole ADR-0136 closed. It is never writable in source. No syntax produces one; it is produced by exactly one mechanism (ADR-0186 §2 — ClrNullability's three reading paths, for a position whose nullability byte is oblivious) and appears only in diagnostics, hover text and DisplayFormat output, spelled T!. Like the wrapper is purely a binder-level annotation: is the underlying type's, and emit erases the wrapper to T.
member.remarks: ADR-0186 step 1 built the symbol and its read path behind --nullability=platform-types; step 3 made that mode the default (), so an ordinary compilation constructs these wrappers for every oblivious imported reference position. --nullability=enabled restores ADR-0136's reading, and under it nothing constructs one.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PointerTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents an unmanaged raw pointer type *T (CLR ELEMENT_TYPE_PTR, the faithful mapping of C# T*). Distinct from , which models a managed by-ref pointer (ELEMENT_TYPE_BYREF, T&). Unmanaged pointers are only legal inside an unsafe context (ADR-0122 / issue #1014); unlike managed by-refs they may be stored in fields, declared as locals, and passed as plain (non-ref-kind) P/Invoke parameters.
member.remarks: Instances are interned per pointee type for identity equality, mirroring .

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.PropertySymbol
member.summary: Represents a property declared on a user-defined type (ADR-0051).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.RectangularArrayTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a CLR rectangular array type such as [,]T or [,,]T.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceImage
member.summary: One assembly image that a is built from.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceImageSet
member.summary: The immutable set of reference images that handle-backed symbols read (ADR-0209 section 5).
member.remarks: The set owns one for each image, in reference order. It resolves type references through forwards, interns the missing types and holds the name index and the well-known types. The modules that the name index covers come first, in reference order. A later module is a dependency. A type reference can reach a dependency, but a name lookup does not search it. This is the partition that the MetadataLoadContext has today between the loaded assemblies and the resolver closure. When two modules have the same simple name, the first one owns the name (ADR-0209 section 9).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceInfo
member.summary: Per-reference metadata record used to emit a CompilationMetadataReferences CustomDebugInformation blob per the Portable PDB spec § "CompilationMetadataReferences".

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceMetadataIndex
member.summary: A serializable snapshot of the full-type-name → declaring-assembly index that derives from a reference set. It exists so the language server's cross-session cold-start cache (ADR-0107) can persist the expensive metadata enumeration (Assembly.GetTypes() / Assembly.GetForwardedTypes() over the project's whole reference closure) and replay it on a subsequent process start instead of recomputing it.
member.remarks: The index is a pure function of the (ordered) reference set: it carries no source-derived state, so it is safe to fingerprint on the references alone. It stores only type-name strings plus each assembly's identity — never CLR objects, which are bound to a live and cannot survive a process exit. A consumer re-creates the load context, validates the recorded assembly identities and content fingerprints against the freshly-loaded ones, then materialises individual instances lazily by name (see ). Because the recorded names are exactly those the eager enumeration produced, warm resolution is a superset of cold resolution (with an order-preserving scan fallback), so it can never silently resolve fewer or different types than the cold path. ADR-0107 (revised) persists the index as a human-readable text section () inside the single .lscache descriptor: newline-delimited type names grouped per assembly. On the Oahu closure (~25 000 names, ~1.3 MB) this parses in ~4 ms — indistinguishable in practice from a binary encoding (~2 ms) and far below the ~120 ms enumeration it replaces — so there is no reason to maintain a separate binary blob.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceNullabilityKind
member.summary: ADR-0193 §2: the answer to "what is this type's reference nullability?" for one top-level position. A separate enum from , which is the import rule's decision (its fourth value is "leave the input as it is"). This one is a query result, and its fourth value says the question does not apply: a value type, including Nullable, has no reference nullability. Value optionality (ADR-0001) is a different question.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceResolver
member.summary: Resolves imported types by name across a configurable set of referenced assemblies.
member.remarks:
This is the seam that import statements use to find CLR types, and the source of well-known primitive types (System.Object, System.String) consumed by the emitter when materialising type references.
When the resolver is constructed with explicit reference paths (), those paths are loaded into a . The instances returned by ) then carry the target framework's assembly identities (e.g. System.Console, Version=8.0.0.0 when the reference paths point at the net8.0 reference pack). Without this indirection, the emitter would write type references bound to the gsc host's runtime version, which fails to load on lower target frameworks.
falls back to the gsc host's loaded assemblies and is intended for in-process interpreter scenarios and the existing test suite where cross-targeting is not relevant.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceResolver.FallbackMetadataAssemblyResolver
member.summary: A that resolves from a supplied set of images indexed by their metadata assembly names and, when that fails, degrades gracefully: instead of allowing the to surface an exception for an unresolved transitive dependency, it records the offending simple name and returns null so the caller can skip the affected member (issue #340). The recorded names feed the diagnostic surface.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ReferenceTypeNameIndex
member.summary: The full-type-name index that a builds over its assemblies. Each name maps to the index of the first assembly, in search order, that defines or forwards it.
member.remarks: The resolver reads an assembly with no image (a host runtime assembly) through reflection. keeps the types that this read found. A lookup returns them as they were found.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.ResolvedTypeReference
member.summary: The answer to a type reference or a type name: a type definition in a module, or a missing type.
member.remarks: Forwards are already followed. The facade that forwarded the type never appears here. This is the name-level result of ADR-0209 PR 1. The type symbol of a definition comes with the decoder in a later PR.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SequenceTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a sequence type sequence[T] — alias for IEnumerable<T> (ADR-0040).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SliceTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a variable-length slice type []T.
member.remarks: Phase 3.A.2 / ADR-0016 — backing representation is the CLR single-dimensional zero-based array T[]. len(s) and cap(s) both return s.Length; append(s, v) allocates a new array of length +1, copies, and writes the new element. Full Go slice header semantics (independent length/capacity, aliased backing array) are intentionally deferred. Instances are cached per element type so identical slice types compare by reference.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SpecialType
member.summary: Tags the types that the compiler names itself (ADR-0209 section 5, "Well-known types"). A table resolves each tagged type by name in the reference set.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructLayoutMetadata
member.summary: The resolved -derived layout for a user struct or class declaration (ADR-0093 / issue #759). The binder attaches one instance to a when the type carries a well-formed @StructLayout(LayoutKind.…) annotation; the emitter consumes it to pick the right layout flag and to write a ClassLayout row when or is specified.
member.remarks:
Only and are accepted in v1; is rejected with GS0346 because Auto-layout types are not portable across the P/Invoke boundary (the CLR is permitted to reorder Auto-layout fields). See ADR-0093 §1 for the full rationale.
When this metadata is null, the emitter falls back to the historical defaults: for struct and for class.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol
member.summary: Represents a user-defined aggregate type (Phase 3.B). Structs are CLR value types; classes are CLR reference types. Methods may be declared inside class bodies or added later through same-package receiver declarations.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SuspendingKind
member.summary: How a function came to be suspending (ADR-0174 D4): compiled as a state machine returning ValueTask[R] with no observable task, and awaited implicitly at every G# call site.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.Symbol
member.summary: Represents a symbol in the language.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolContainment
member.summary: Fills in for the members of a user-defined type (ADR-0169). G# binds members into per-kind collections on rather than threading a containing-type back-link through every symbol, so the Roslyn ISymbol.ContainingType analogue is anchored fill-once when symbols surface on an analyzer-facing surface.
member.remarks: Issue #3795: this used to run only on the analyzer driver's SYMBOL-action path, which a syntax-node analyzer never reaches. Such an analyzer obtains the same symbols through and saw ContainingType == null where Roslyn always populates it, so every rule keyed on containment (a base-type walk, a "declared on type X" test) silently reported nothing rather than failing. Anchoring is idempotent and never overwrites containment the binder already set, so calling it from both surfaces is safe.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolEqualityComparer
member.summary: Symbol identity comparer — the Roslyn SymbolEqualityComparer analogue (ADR-0169). G# symbols are reference-unique within a compilation, so identity is reference equality; the type exists so migrated analyzers' SymbolEqualityComparer.Default usage carries over verbatim.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolKind
member.summary: Represents the kind of symbol in the language.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolPrinter
member.summary: Symbol printer.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolSourceOrderComparer
member.summary: The compiler's one deterministic order over symbols (issue #4663).
member.remarks:
Symbols do not override , so every hash-ordered collection keyed by them (ImmutableDictionary, ImmutableHashSet, a Dictionary after removals) enumerates in identity-hash order. CoreCLR identity hashes come from a per-thread generator: they repeat for the same compiler binary fed the same inputs, and change as soon as anything shifts allocation — an unrelated input file, a different file order, or a differently-built compiler. Any name, counter or emission order derived from such an enumeration is therefore not deterministic, even under /deterministic.
This comparer orders by source facts only, never by input order: the declaration's span start, name and parameter signature (the emitter's MethodDef order since issue #456, kept as the primary keys so existing output does not move), then the declaring file name, the position of any other declaring node (local functions), and the containing type.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SynthesizedClosureReifier
member.summary: Issue #1477: shared helper that makes a synthesized closure / capture-box class generic over the enclosing generic type / method type parameters its members reference. When a lambda inside a generic type (or generic method) captures a value whose type references an enclosing type parameter (a T-typed value, or this of G<T>), the synthesized display / box class must declare its OWN type parameters that mirror those enclosing parameters 1:1; otherwise its capture field's VAR slot has no generic parameter in scope, producing an illegal field type (System.TypeLoadException at load) and unverifiable IL.
member.remarks: The reification mirrors the iterator / async state-machine treatment (RegisterStateMachineEnclosingGenerics): the synthesized class is reified over fresh class-level type parameters that clone each referenced enclosing parameter, and the original parameters are recorded on so the emitter can build the outer-TP → own-TP-ordinal remap that routes every member signature through a valid VAR(idx) slot. A constructed instance carrying the original parameters as type arguments is returned for use at the capture site (so the newobj / field stores reference DisplayClass<…enclosing args…>).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TupleElementNamesReader
member.summary: ADR-0172 Phase B: decodes System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TupleElementNamesAttribute from an imported parameter / return / field / property and applies the flattened name array onto the already-mapped , rebuilding each tuple occurrence as a named . The walk consumes names in the same DFS pre-order the C# compiler (and gsc's emit-side TupleElementNamesBuilder) uses: every tuple contributes its arity of entries before its element subtrees; non-tuple composites are traversed transparently. Application is best-effort — a cursor/shape mismatch (foreign compiler quirk) leaves the remaining tree unnamed rather than failing the import.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TupleTypeSymbol
member.summary: Represents a tuple type (T1, T2, ...) (Phase 4.5).
member.remarks: Backed by the CLR System.ValueTuple<...> family. Instances are cached per element-type sequence so identical tuple types compare by reference. Arity 8 and higher use the CLR's canonical ValueTuple<T1,...,T7,TRest> nesting.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeArgsKey
member.summary: Issue #1621: dictionary key for constructed-generic caches (, , ) that compares a vector of type arguments by REFERENCE identity, not by a stringified . TypeSymbols are reference-identity throughout the codebase, so a hash-only key risks silently aliasing two distinct constructions whose type arguments' identity hashes collide (the hash is at most 31 bits and is not guaranteed unique). ) performs the real, correct-by-construction comparison; is only a bucketing hint.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeArgumentKind
member.summary: ADR-0193 §1: what is known about a type argument's kind at the point the rule runs. Deliberately three-valued: an unconstrained type parameter is neither a reference nor a value type, and folding it into either neighbour is the PR #4362 round-1 regression (Min() on an unconstrained T becoming T?).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeMemberModel
member.summary:
ADR-0112: the single canonical member-resolution layer for user-defined G# types ( for class + struct, , and ).
This type is deliberately pure — it has no BinderContext dependency and returns only existing instances (FunctionSymbol / FieldSymbol / PropertySymbol / EventSymbol / EnumMemberSymbol) — so both the binder and the language server can consume it without behavioral drift, and emit / overload resolution / conversion are unaffected by the layer itself.
CLR / imported member reflection is intentionally out of scope and remains behind MemberLookup; this layer covers user-symbol member tables only.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterConstraint
member.summary: Constraint kind for a (Phase 4.1 / ADR-0020; widened in Phase 4.2).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterSymbol
member.summary: A generic type-parameter declared on a generic function or type (Phase 4.1 / ADR-0020). At the binder level it behaves like a stand-in ; at call sites it is substituted with a concrete type argument either from an explicit type-argument list or via inference from value arguments.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.TypeParameterVariance
member.summary: Variance kind for a (Phase 4.3 / ADR-0021).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.VariableSymbol
member.summary: Represents a variable symbol in the language.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.WellKnownTypes
member.summary: The types that the compiler names itself, resolved by name in one .
member.remarks: A type that the set does not supply is a . The table does not fall back to a host type (ADR-0209 section 5). The table holds definitions only. A construction such as Func<int> is a construction over the definition. The order of the names is fixed, so the table never depends on hash order.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.AssignmentTargetSyntaxFacts
member.summary: Shared syntax shaping for assignment targets.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.CollectionElementSyntax
member.summary: Issue #479 / ADR-0117: the base class for a single element of a . The concrete shapes are (a bare element expr, including ...source), (a key/value entry key: value), and (an indexed entry [key] = value), and (an explicit receiver member .Member: value, ADR-0180).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.DocumentationAttacher
member.summary: Implements the position-based documentation attachment pass (ADR-0057 §7). Groups consecutive s into blocks by line-adjacency, then attaches each block to the nearest documentable declaration whose start follows immediately after.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.ExpressionSyntax

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.NullConditionalChain
member.summary: Structural helpers over a G# null-conditional access chain (?. / ?[), written for a migrated Roslyn analyzer (issue #4173) that used to walk Roslyn's ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax / MemberBindingExpressionSyntax / ElementBindingExpressionSyntax shapes and needs the G# equivalent at analysis time. Shape. G# gives a?.b and a.b the SAME node (), told apart only by ; a?[i] is with its own . A "hop" below always means one such flagged node — the G# counterpart of one Roslyn ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax (one ?./?[ operator). Nesting is NOT a mirror image of Roslyn's, and it is not uniform. An earlier draft of this file assumed G#'s postfix chain nests via LeftPart the way a naive left-to-right reading of Parser.Expressions.cs's current = new X(current, …) pattern suggests. Empirically that is wrong for ./?.: parsing the right-hand side of a dot recurses back into the full postfix grammar (ParseMemberContinuation → ParseNameOrCallExpression → its own ParsePostfixChain) BEFORE the enclosing loop iteration finishes, so that recursive call already swallows every following ./?./[/(. The result is that a dotted chain nests through — right/ suffix-nested, exactly like Roslyn's own ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax.WhenNotNull chain — while [/?[/( continuations still nest the ordinary iterative way, through / (left-nested, the receiver-so-far). ) already relies on this same right-nesting for member-access chains and is a second, independent confirmation. Because of that split, "does node n have a further hop wrapping it" is not one simple parent check: an inner ./?. hop is a DESCENDANT of the chain's outer node (reached via RightPart), not an ancestor. Every method here is built on two primitives that stay correct regardless of which way a given link nests: ) (walk up through every kind of chain link to the outermost node) and an internal left-to-right token-order scan of the hops underneath that top (rather than a literal parent/child walk) for "next hop" queries.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.Parser.DottedTypeNameTail
member.summary: Issue #526 / #1506: the decomposed tail of a dotted type-clause name (everything after the first identifier). The last segment's type-argument list is stored in the Trailing* fields (the historical single-trailing representation); the per-segment lists of every earlier (outer) segment are stored in the OuterSegment* arrays, aligned to the segment sequence (index 0 = the first identifier).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.StructLiteralElementSyntax
member.summary: ADR-0180: the base class for a single ordered element of a 's list. The two concrete shapes are (a member initializer Field: value) and (a bare content element or a ...source content spread, both of which lower to an Add(...) call on the constructed receiver). Representing every element as one ordered — rather than a members list plus a separate elements list — is what lets the binder preserve lexical (source) order when members and content elements are interleaved.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Syntax.SyntaxChildSourceOrderAttribute
member.summary: Marks a syntax node class whose child properties are not in source order for every shape of the node. A !! suffix follows its operand, a type clause has prefix and suffix forms, and a declaration lists its annotations in a base class. GetChildren sorts the children of a marked class, and of its derived classes, by source position (issue #5185).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxCodeGenerator
member.summary: The top-level entry point consumers reach for (ADR-0142, issue #2200): given a .resx file's path plus its owning project's root namespace and root directory, computes the same namespace/class-name/manifest-name convention MSBuild's default resx code generation uses, parses the resx, and renders the generated G# designer source. Both the G# language server (regenerating on save) and cs2gs (producing the codebehind for a migrated .resx instead of translating Resources.Designer.cs) call through this single class so the two integrations can never drift.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxDesignerGenerator
member.summary: Generates the G# equivalent of a resx codebehind file — the class a C# project gets from ResXFileCodeGenerator / PublicResXFileCodeGenerator (ADR-0142, issue #2200). The generated class exposes the same shape as the CodeDom-produced C# class: a lazily-created ResourceManager, a settable Culture, a private parameterless constructor, and one static property per resx entry — a plain string property reading through GetString for the dominant string-resource case, or a typed property reading through GetObject (downcast with as) for anything else. This is the single generator shared by the G# language server (regenerates on .resx save) and by cs2gs (produces the codebehind for a migrated project's .resx files instead of translating the C# Designer.cs).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxDesignerOptions
member.summary: The inputs needs beyond the parsed itself (ADR-0142) — everything the real ResXFileCodeGenerator / PublicResXFileCodeGenerator derives from the owning MSBuild project (root namespace, resx-relative folder, and the "Access Modifier" custom-tool choice).

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxDocument
member.summary: A parsed .resx document (ADR-0142): the ordered set of real resource entries, with Visual Studio's design-time-only metadata rows (<data name=">>...">, produced by the WinForms/WPF designer) and <resheader> rows filtered out.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxEntry
member.summary: One <data> resource entry parsed from a .resx file (ADR-0142). Mirrors the subset of the resx schema the strongly-typed designer generator cares about: the resource's , its literal or base64-encoded , the optional developer (used to seed the generated property's doc comment), and — for a non-string resource — the assembly-qualified and/or that select how the property reads the value back out of the ResourceManager.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxIdentifier
member.summary: Turns a resx resource key into a valid G# member identifier (ADR-0142), mirroring the naming rules the real ResXFileCodeGenerator / StronglyTypedResourceBuilder applies to C# identifiers: any character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore is replaced with _, a leading digit is prefixed with _, and a name that collides with a G# reserved keyword — or with a name already emitted by this generator (including the fixed ResourceManager/Culture accessors) — gets a numeric suffix. G# has no verbatim-identifier escape (no C#-style @keyword), so the suffix is the only collision remedy available.

member.name: T:GSharp.Core.Resx.ResxTypeNameMapper
member.summary: Maps a resx type attribute — an assembly-qualified CLR type name such as System.Byte[], mscorlib, Version=4.0.0.0, ... — to a G# type clause (ADR-0142). G# resolves an arbitrary dotted CLR type name directly (no import required), so only two transforms are needed: strip the trailing assembly qualification, and rewrite CLR primitive element names / the C# T[] array suffix to their G# spellings (uint8, []T, ...). Non-primitive leaf types (e.g. System.Drawing.Bitmap) are passed through unchanged as a fully-qualified dotted type reference.
